2 Workload and Failure Mode



2.1 Semi-synthetic aggregate workload




The workload models a multi-tenant conversational-assistant service (e.g., customer-support chatbots), where each business carries a stable, reusable context. Our evaluation uses a semi-synthetic workload: a synthetic request stream designed to mimic aggregate workload characteristics—per-key rates, inter-arrival gaps, and popularity distribution—derived from de-identified operational serving telemetry. No raw requests, conversation content, user data, or business identifiers are used. The primary summary contains 128,824 opaque business keys and has a Gini coefficient of 0.756. Roughly 4% of keys account for 47% of requests, yet no key contributes more than 0.3%. The median per-key inter-arrival coefficient of variation is 1.93, and 80.8% of requests belong to multi-turn threads.




Prompts average about 1.2K input tokens, 90% of which precede the current turn. Most of those tokens are not a routing opportunity. The global template is common to all businesses and warms on every destination; a retrieved few-shot block changes often enough to break the exact prefix in 67% of consecutive request pairs. The reusable, key-specific segment is the per-business context, about 180 tokens or 15% of the prompt. We route on the business key and benefit only when that segment returns before eviction.




We evaluate two independently derived semi-synthetic aggregates and several explicitly labeled synthetic workloads. The aggregates retain only replay statistics, including opaque-key rates and inter-arrival gaps. Neither the paper nor its artifacts contain request text, user content, business names, or business identifiers. We reserve synthetic traffic for mechanism and boundary tests, where controlling skew, burstiness, or prefix reuse matters more than matching a full workload.




2.2 Why balancing and stickiness both fail




For a business with rate λb\lambda_{b} sprayed uniformly across RR destinations, the mean time between visits to one destination scales as R/λbR/\lambda_{b}. Increasing the fleet can thus make a prefix colder even though total cache capacity grows. If this revisit time exceeds the effective eviction time, every request repeats prefill work.




Pure affinity moves to the other extreme. A consistent hash keeps a prefix local, but the busiest hash bucket inherits the workload skew. Tail latency then follows the hottest destination rather than the fleet average. Bounded hashing and reactive reuse-versus-load policies reduce this problem, but may spill a request to a cold destination after a cap binds. The practical need is a stable many-key assignment computed with the rate distribution in view.




Deployment turns on a measurable tradeoff: whether the recoverable hit-rate increase outweighs the residual load skew. Model size, precision, prefix length, offered load, active-set breadth, and cache size all shift that balance. As Section 5.3 shows, a higher cache-hit rate can still accompany lower capacity.

3.2 Operational semantics




The table stays fixed within a control interval. Stability avoids per-request cap thrashing, but drift can make the assignment stale. Installing a replacement table also starts some assignments cold. Section 5.4 measures both effects.




Admitted and cold-tail prefixes share the engine’s native cache and eviction policy. CacheRoute neither reserves nor migrates KV blocks and offers no analytic residency guarantee. Before enabling a table, we shadow-replay it and measure served token-weighted KV hit and latency.

4 Experimental Method


Implementation.




Our client-side routing harness bypasses the serving deployment’s aggregate load balancer and sends each request according to one policy. An experiment identifier in request metadata attributes served, token-weighted KV-cache hits to the correct run. Policies use the same serving stack, request stream, warm-up exclusion, offered-load ladder, and health criteria. The routing layer neither changes model execution nor reserves cache capacity.



Testbeds.




The flagship system is Llama-3.3-70B in fp8, served by 30 tensor-parallel-2 destinations on 60 H100 GPUs. Each destination exposes 40,071 measured KV blocks (about 641K tokens). The mechanism testbed is Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in bf16 on 30 single-H100 destinations. We use a 70B fp16 run only as supporting cache-pressure evidence, not for the capacity headline.



Workloads.




The main replay draws opaque keys from a semi-synthetic peak-hour aggregate distribution. A second, independently collected semi-synthetic aggregate distribution tests distribution shift. Poisson, CV-matched Gamma, and moving-block-bootstrap arrival processes test burst sensitivity. The 8B study uses a semi-synthetic aggregate distribution except where we explicitly inject synthetic whales.



Policies.




We compare against Flat-LB (power-of-two-choices), sticky consistent hashing [Karger et al.(1997)], consistent hashing with bounded loads (CHWBL) [Mirrokni et al.(2018)], a DualMap-style two-candidate cache/load policy [Yuan et al.(2026)], and a Preble-style prefix-history and live-load policy [Srivatsa et al.(2024)]. The latter three are reimplemented in our harness under a common interface; our absolute results should not be read as reproductions of their original systems. CHWBL uses ϵ=0.25\epsilon=0.25, selected by an offline sweep, and the Preble-style policy uses a 1.5 load-cap factor.



Metrics and statistics.




SLO capacity is the highest offered-QPS ladder point with p99 latency at or below the stated threshold and failure rate at most 5%. We compute the threshold independently per run and report its mean; a value at the ladder maximum is right-censored. The flagship top-KK128 result uses five paired seeds {2,3,4,5,6}\{2,3,4,5,6\} and reports mean ±\pm 95% Student-tt confidence intervals. The top-KK256 confirmation uses eight seeds. The secondary-distribution and 8B studies use three paired seeds unless stated otherwise; their wider intervals warrant interpreting small differences as noise. KV-hit is served and token-weighted, not a simulator prediction.

We use a short shadow replay as the deployment gate. It preserves the candidate assignment without returning its responses to users. The replay compares served KV hit, per-destination load, and p99 against Flat-LB at one load below and one load near the current knee. A cache-hit increase is not enough; the plan is enabled only when p99 or capacity improves. We repeat the gate after changes to model, precision, context length, batching, cache allocation, or the active-set distribution.




5.4 Burstiness and replanning


Arrival burstiness.




On 70B fp8/top-KK128, a Gamma arrival process matched to the workload’s marginal CV=1.9 reduces CacheRoute’s 3.5-s capacity by one ladder step, from 180 to 160 QPS, while KV-hit moves from 94% to 90%. Flat-LB remains at 30 QPS. In a separate, single-sweep comparison, a moving-block bootstrap of 22,639 measured inter-arrival gaps from semi-synthetic aggregate workload A (block length 50, empirical CV=2.73) leaves CacheRoute at 180 QPS and 93% hit, while Flat-LB becomes left-censored below 30 QPS. These are two-policy, one-active-set sensitivities, not claims about all baselines. They show that the main improvement does not require smoothed arrivals.



Rate drift and remapping.




We perturb the primary rate vector over six intervals with a lognormal random walk (σ=0.3\sigma=0.3) and compare fresh and one-interval-stale plans at 160 QPS. Recomputing LPT from scratch changes 94.5% of key-to-destination sets, although only 1.1% of keys change assignment count. The stale plan loses 1.0 percentage point of KV hit and 192 ms of p99 on average; the worst transition loses 3.0 points and 858 ms. Installing the fresh plan, meanwhile, produces a transient 13.6-point KV-hit drop during rewarming. A deployment should therefore preserve placements until the measured staleness penalty exceeds the warm-up penalty. We have not implemented a churn-aware replanner.



Why we do not predict residency analytically.




We also tested a single-characteristic-time occupancy model against the 70B fp8 engine. Component-level instrumentation passed seven isolation checks, and each TP2 destination exposed 40,071 measured KV blocks. Prediction still missed served hit rate by 14.3 percentage points at the median and 44.7 points at p90. The observed curve drops sharply and then plateaus, a shape outside the tested model family. We neither size deployments with this model nor assign the shape to an engine mechanism without direct evidence. This failure is why shadow replay remains part of the deployment procedure.






6 Discussion and Limitations


What generalizes.




The planner requires a stable routing key, a reusable key-specific prefix, and rate estimates that remain useful for at least one cache-warming interval. Another routing key—a tenant, a document collection, an agent, or an application—could replace the business key used here. Because the router changes placement rather than model execution, it does not depend on a particular model architecture or cache implementation.



What does not yet generalize.




Equal-slot admission assumes roughly uniform stable-prefix sizes. We did not measure a byte-aware value function for heterogeneous long contexts and make no byte-knapsack or optimal-admission claim. Cold-tail traffic shares the native cache and can evict admitted prefixes. The aggregate replays preserve key popularity and, for the burst experiment, short-range gap correlation; they do not preserve exact per-key timestamps. Finally, two distributions cannot represent every market or application.




Preble, DualMap, and CHWBL are common-harness reimplementations, not the original codebases. They compare routing behavior under matched hardware but do not reproduce the published systems end to end. Several 8B knees are right-censored at 500 QPS, so we report ratios only when the sweep resolves them. The three-seed studies also have wide tt intervals; the five-seed flagship and eight-seed confirmation provide the stronger evidence.



Deployment checklist.




An operator adopting CacheRoute would begin with aggregate key rates and a single-destination measurement of qcapq_{\mathrm{cap}}. After choosing a conservative warm-slot allocation, they would shadow-replay the plan and Flat-LB at matched loads, comparing served KV hit, imbalance, p99, and failures. Canary traffic would follow only if the plan wins, and the router would fall back to Flat-LB when the active set or measured p99 leaves that envelope. None of these steps requires request content.





7 Related Work




PagedAttention/vLLM and SGLang make prefix KV reuse efficient within one serving engine [Kwon et al.(2023), Zheng et al.(2024)]. CacheRoute instead decides which destination receives the request.




Preble scores prefix reuse against live load, while DualMap combines static and dynamic mappings [Srivatsa et al.(2024), Yuan et al.(2026)]. Consistent hashing and CHWBL provide stable affinity with explicit load control [Karger et al.(1997), Mirrokni et al.(2018)]. CacheRoute constructs one global, rate-based table for a control interval. Admission and LPT are established heuristics; the new evidence concerns their use in a prefix-affinity plan and the workloads on which that plan helps.




GeoCover studies a different form of resource-constrained placement [Cheng et al.(2015)]: it selects roadside units for spatial network coverage, whereas CacheRoute assigns recurring prefixes to model destinations under serving load. The algorithms and guarantees do not transfer between the two problems. Their common ground is the allocation of limited infrastructure under skewed demand.




Mooncake and MemServe move or pool KV state across servers rather than preserve it through ingress affinity [Hu et al.(2024), Qin et al.(2025)]. Llumnix migrates requests to repair imbalance [Sun et al.(2024)]; DistServe and Splitwise separate prefill and decode placement [Zhong et al.(2024), Patel et al.(2024)]. These systems can still use an ingress plan to avoid prefill that routing would otherwise repeat.




8 Conclusion




CacheRoute plans prefix affinity and expected load once per control interval. On a 70B fp8 model across 60 H100 GPUs, it reaches 93.2% served KV hit and 2.3×2.3\times the capacity of the strongest baseline at a 3.5-s p99 SLO. The negative workloads set an equally important boundary: affinity can reduce capacity when the recoverable prefix work is small. Any real deployment would therefore measure its own boundary with shadow replay.

B.2 Threshold construction




For each run and policy, capacity is the largest offered-load point whose p99 meets the SLO and whose failure rate is at most 5%. Reported capacity is the mean of these per-run knees, rather than a confidence interval around one latency measurement. A run that fails at the lowest load is left-censored; one that passes at the maximum is right-censored. The primary 70B ladder is {30,60,80,100,120,140,160,180,220,300}\{30,60,80,100,120,140,160,180,220,300\} QPS, and the 8B ladder is {30,60,100,160,240,360,500}\{30,60,100,160,240,360,500\} QPS.




Continuous measurements use the sample mean and a two-sided 95% Student-tt interval. With n=3n=3, t0.975,2=4.303t_{0.975,2}=4.303, so those intervals are necessarily wide; with n=5n=5, t0.975,4=2.776t_{0.975,4}=2.776. Experiments, not individual requests, are the replication units.

Affinity adds only 8–11 percentage points of cache hit in these workloads, too little to offset modest skew. This reversal motivates the shadow-replay gate used in the main paper.




Appendix H Analytic Residency Model: Negative Result




Each TP2 destination in the 70B fp8 engine exposes 40,071 physical KV blocks, or approximately 641K tokens. An earlier configuration note used 30,000 blocks; the ratio between the values is 1.34×1.34\times. Our results use the measured block count, not that ratio, as the relevant configuration.




Component instrumentation passes seven isolation tests, and the business-hit crossover remains stable across the eviction sweep (coefficient of variation 0.038 over 24 cells). A single-characteristic-time occupancy model nevertheless misses served hit rate by 14.3 percentage points at the median and 44.7 points at p90; its rank agreement also falls below the deployment target. The measured residency curve drops sharply and then plateaus, outside the tested model family. We lack direct evidence to attribute that shape to batching, block quantization, or another engine mechanism.




Physical block capacity and aggregate rates are therefore insufficient for pre-deployment sizing on this engine. The deployment interface includes a shadow replay that measures served KV hit and p99 for the candidate assignment.


Claim-to-evidence map.




The main claims map to the following evidence:


• 



The 2.3×2.3\times headline is supported by the 70B fp8, 60-H100, top-KK128, five-seed hardware study; it is not a universal multiplier.


• 



The wider-active-set result is a separate eight-seed confirmation and is smaller (1.33×1.33\times at 3.5 s).


• 



The second distribution ties at top-KK128 and reaches 1.6×1.6\times only at top-KK256.


• 



The 8B ablation supports the affinity/placement decomposition; only synthetic whales exercise replication, while the primary workload has kb=1k_{b}=1.


• 



Burst robustness is a two-policy, one-active-set sensitivity and is not extrapolated to the other four baselines.


• 



The 32B loss/tie workloads establish a deployment gate, and the failed analytic predictor supports measuring residency rather than asserting a microarchitectural cause.

FILE vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py:1-80; SHA256 97bcfaa655c6d4a5ecdfb17ab87b80547e8216b9d15a91c341798ebbb558f146
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""DSpark speculator: semi-autoregressive parallel drafting.

DSpark drafts a block of ``num_speculative_tokens`` tokens in one parallel pass
(reusing the DFlash machinery: context-KV precompute + a query-block forward),
then injects intra-block dependency with a lightweight sequential Markov head.

Differences from DFlash:
  * Anchor-as-first-prediction: each request emits exactly ``N =
    num_speculative_tokens`` query tokens (anchor + N-1 noise), NOT ``1 + N``.
    Every query position is a prediction (the anchor predicts the first draft
    token), so we sample at all N positions and ``sample_pos = query_pos + 1``
    (standard next-token), whereas DFlash's masks sit AT the predicted position.
    This is the ``sample_from_anchor`` path in the shared prepare-inputs kernel.
    Speculators-format checkpoints instead use the DFlash ``1 + N`` fill-in
    layout (anchor is the bonus token).
  * Sequential Markov sampling: instead of DFlash's single parallel sample, we
    sample left-to-right, adding a prefix-dependent Markov bias derived from the
    previously sampled token at each step.

CUDA graphs (FULL, mirroring DFlash) cover the whole draft step: the parallel
backbone forward AND the sequential Markov sampling.
"""

from typing import Any

import torch

from vllm.config import VllmConfig
from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
from vllm.logger import init_logger
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.gumbel import gumbel_sample
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dflash.speculator import DFlashSpeculator
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark.utils import load_dspark_model

logger = init_logger(__name__)


class DSparkSpeculator(DFlashSpeculator):
    _speculator_name = "DSpark"

    def __init__(self, vllm_config: VllmConfig, device: torch.device):
        super().__init__(vllm_config, device)

        # Whether to sample from the anchor position. When True, uses anchor-as-first
        # (N slots, each position predicts the next token). When False, uses 1+N
        # fill-in block (anchor is a bonus token).
        self.sample_from_anchor = getattr(
            self.draft_model_config.hf_config, "sample_from_anchor", True
        )
        if self.sample_from_anchor:
            self.num_query_per_req = self.num_speculative_steps
        else:
            self.num_query_per_req = 1 + self.num_speculative_steps

        # DSpark consumes mean-pooled target aux hidden states at the target
        # layers, combined to hidden_size via main_proj. Store that combined
        # main_x (hidden_size wide). DSpark does not use the same pre-allocated buffer
        # that DeepSeek-V4's MTP uses.
        draft_hidden = self.draft_model_config.get_hidden_size()
        self.hidden_states = torch.zeros(
            self.max_num_tokens, draft_hidden, dtype=self.dtype, device=device
        )

        self._step_cols = torch.arange(
            self.num_speculative_steps, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
        )

        self._anchor_idx = (
            torch.arange(self.max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
            * self.num_query_per_req
        )

        # Reduced-vocab probabilistic drafting only; set in load_draft_model.
        self._d2t_scatter_index: torch.Tensor | None = None
        self._draft_scatter_buf: torch.Tensor | None = None
        self._draft_topk: int | None = getattr(
            self.draft_model_config.hf_config, "dspark_draft_topk", None
        )

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.config import ParallelConfig
from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_dp_group
from vllm.v1.worker.dp_utils import should_skip_dp_coordination
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils import (
    BatchExecutionDescriptor,
    CudaGraphManager,
)
from vllm.v1.worker.ubatch_utils import check_ubatch_thresholds, get_num_ubatches


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DPSyncState:
    """What a `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` call agreed across DP ranks.

    Every field is identical on every rank, so callers can branch on them
    without disagreeing about whether to run a collective. Never add a per-rank
    value here.
    """

    # Per-rank token counts, for the forward context. All entries hold the
    # agreed padded count, unless `eager`, where nothing was padded.
    num_tokens_across_dp: torch.Tensor
    # Agreed uniform decode length. None means the ranks disagreed, which is an
    # answer, not "unknown".
    uniform_token_count: int | None
    # Whether the ranks agreed to run eager. A dispatch reusing this must run
    # eager too; no shape was agreed, so picking a graph per rank would diverge.
    eager: bool
    # Agreed upper bound on any rank's request count. Holds the padded count when
    # a FULL descriptor imposed one, else the most any rank scheduled.
    num_reqs: int


def sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding(
    cudagraph_manager: CudaGraphManager | None,
    desired_batch_desc: BatchExecutionDescriptor,
    num_tokens: int,
    num_reqs: int,
    uniform_token_count: int | None,
    dp_size: int,
    dp_rank: int,
    max_query_len: int | None = None,
    num_active_loras: int = 0,
    parallel_config: ParallelConfig | None = None,
    allow_ubatching: bool = False,
    uniform_decode: bool = False,
) -> tuple[BatchExecutionDescriptor, DPSyncState | None]:
    """Coordinates the batch descriptor and DP padding across all ranks.

    `parallel_config` is only needed to decide whether to microbatch, so callers
    that never do (`allow_ubatching=False`) can leave it out.

    Returns (synced_batch_desc, sync). `sync` is None when no rank has work.
    """
    assert dp_size > 1, "DP size must be greater than 1"
    group = get_dp_group().cpu_group
    tensor = torch.zeros(6, dp_size, dtype=torch.int32, device="cpu")
    tensor[0][dp_rank] = num_tokens
    tensor[1][dp_rank] = desired_batch_desc.cg_mode.value
    tensor[2][dp_rank] = uniform_token_count or 0  # (0 means None)
    tensor[3][dp_rank] = max_query_len or -1  # (-1 means None)
    tensor[4][dp_rank] = int(allow_ubatching)
    tensor[5][dp_rank] = num_reqs
    if should_skip_dp_coordination():
        tensor[:] = tensor[:, dp_rank, None].clone()
    else:
        dist.all_reduce(tensor, group=group)

    num_tokens_across_dp = tensor[0]
    cg_mode_across_dp = tensor[1]
    uniform_token_counts_across_dp = tensor[2]
    max_query_lens_across_dp = tensor[3]
    allow_ubatching_across_dp = tensor[4]
    num_reqs_across_dp = tensor[5]

    # If ranks disagree on the uniform token count, or its 0 (means None) set to None
    synced_uniform_token_count: int | None = int(uniform_token_counts_across_dp[0])
    if synced_uniform_token_count == 0 or not torch.all(
        uniform_token_counts_across_dp == synced_uniform_token_count
    ):
        synced_uniform_token_count = None

    if torch.all(num_tokens_across_dp == 0).item():
        synced_desc = BatchExecutionDescriptor(
            cg_mode=CUDAGraphMode.NONE, num_tokens=0, num_reqs=0
        )
        return synced_desc, None

    if torch.all(allow_ubatching_across_dp == 1):
        # This rank voted too, so its caller passed a config.

title: Installed uniform drafter DP synchronization
fix(results): count SGLang logical KV pools once
body:
SGLang exports one `max_total_num_tokens` gauge per TP scheduler, so summing gauges inflated the TP4 result audited in #2823 from 6,338,048 to 25,352,192 tokens. Count each worker/endpoint and DP pool once across TP/PP/EP replicas, retaining separate prefill/decode roles and independent DP pools. Prefer available capacity telemetry over potentially incomplete worker-log bundles. Ranked telemetry with missing identity, changing capacity, or disagreeing replicas produces no capacity estimate.

The correction affects aggregate telemetry only. Legacy unranked metrics, log-only fallback, and the existing Dynamo-SGLang unsupported-capacity policy remain unchanged. No benchmark configuration or throughput/latency calculation changes.

Validation: 100 aggregation/server-log tests passed, including the real c4 and c256 capacity-series fixtures from [source run 34738529222](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34738529222). The TP4 fixture now yields 6,338,048 tokens; DP8 remains 241,231,872. An end-to-end processor test verifies both nested and compatibility capacity fields. `git diff --check` passed. No GPU sweep is required for this telemetry-only change.

Companion app correction and historical recovery path: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX-app/pull/1148

title: feat(speedbench): add MiMo-V2.6-Flash vLLM DFlash AL collector / feat(speedbench)：新增 MiMo-V2.6-Flash vLLM DFlash AL 采集脚本
body:
## Summary

Adds a SPEED-Bench acceptance-length collector for [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL)'s DFlash drafter on vLLM. Its output becomes the golden curve `infx/golden_al_distribution/mimov2.6flash_dflash.yaml`, which AgentX needs before any MiMo DFlash recipe (#4330 adds the non-speculative SGLang and vLLM keys) can launch.

**What it measures:** `benchmarks/single_node/speedbench/mimov2.6flash_fp4_b300_vllm.sh`, dispatched through `speedbench-al.yml` with `framework=vllm`.
- The drafter is the checkpoint's own `dflash/` subfolder (5 layers, BF16), served as shipped through `--speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", ...}'` with greedy drafting. This is the speculative path in [vLLM's MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL.yaml).
- Draft lengths 1–7, because the drafter's `block_size` is 8. The script rejects any other value before starting a server.
- Thinking off and on, through `--chat-template-kwargs` (`enable_thinking: false` / `true`). The script refuses thinking-on kwargs that do not set `enable_thinking: true`, since the workflow default targets other models.
- Server: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`, TP4, `mimo` parsers, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs as in vLLM's DFlash recipe, prefix caching off.
- Sampling: temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95, from the model card. Concurrency 32.
- AL = 1 + Δaccepted / Δdrafts from vLLM's spec-decode counters around each pass.

**Why DFlash rather than the native MTP layers:** vLLM v0.31.0 loads only the first of the checkpoint's 3 MTP layers and reuses it at every draft step, so an MTP curve would understate the model. DFlash is the drafter vLLM documents for this checkpoint.

**No perf-changelog entry:** no benchmark point changes.

**First GPU run:** [39319922997](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39319922997), in progress. It is 14 server starts plus a first-run checkpoint download, with the workflow's default 8-hour allocation. Dispatch it from this branch (no merge needed):

```bash
gh workflow run speedbench-al.yml --repo SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX --ref feat/mimov2.6flash-speedbench-collector \
  -f runner=b300 -f framework=vllm \
  -f model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL -f model-prefix=mimov2.6flash \
  -f image='vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0@sha256:c1c9f6fd5c109ba7f0546a59f5b2f15fb87f64c77782e90a27b648b42a8e67c3' \
  -f 'mtp-list=1 2 3 4 5 6 7' -f 'thinking-modes=off on' \
  -f thinking-kwargs='{"enable_thinking": true}' \
  -f category=coding -f output-len=4096 -f open-pr=false
```

`b300-dsxe` downloads the checkpoint, including `dflash/`, into its writable model root on the first run.

title: [Klaud Cold] Add MiMo-V2.6-Flash B200 SGLang and vLLM AgentX recipes / [Klaud Cold] 新增 MiMo-V2.6-Flash B200 SGLang 与 vLLM AgentX 配方
body:
## Summary

Adds AgentX coverage for [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL), a 309B-total / 15B-active MiMoV2 model, on B200 with upstream SGLang and upstream vLLM. Neither key uses speculative decoding yet.

**What runs:** two new keys, 24 points in total. Every point keeps the KV cache on the GPU (no CPU offload).

| Key | Image | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-sglang-agentic` | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` | TP4 at conc 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; TP2 at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic` | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` | TP8 at conc 1, 4; TP4 at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; TP2 at 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 |

Both images are pinned by digest. Admission is 2× concurrency for subagent fan-out, and decode CUDA graphs cover the concurrency.

**Precision (`fp4`), checked against the checkpoint's safetensors headers:**
- Routed experts, about 98% of the parameters, are packed MXFP4 (E2M1 with an E8M0 scale per 32 values).
- Dense MLP, fused QKV and MTP layers are FP8 E4M3 with 128×128 block scales.
- `o_proj`, router, embeddings and `lm_head` are BF16.
- On B200 both engines run the routed experts natively as MXFP4 weights × MXFP8 activations (FlashInfer TRT-LLM), and the FP8 layers as block-scaled FP8. This is the same mixed layout as `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, which this repo labels `fp4`.

**SGLang settings** (from the [SGLang MiMo-V2.5 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Xiaomi/MiMo-V2.5); V2.6-Flash uses the same `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` architecture and size class):
- `moe-runner-backend: flashinfer_mxfp4`. v0.5.21's MiMo default picks the FP8 TRT-LLM runner on SM100 for any `quant_method: fp8` checkpoint, which cannot read packed MXFP4 experts. The upstream fix (sgl-project/sglang#41668) landed after v0.5.21.
- `attention-backend: fa4`, because the default `trtllm_mha` rejects MiMoV2's asymmetric K/V head dims on Blackwell.
- No `language-model-only`: v0.5.21 rejects it for `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` (the first canary failed at startup on it). The vision and audio encoders (~2 GB) therefore load, with `mm-attention-backend: fa4` for the ViT; text-only AgentX requests never run them.
- `chunked-prefill-size 16384`, `mem-fraction-static 0.85`, `mimo` reasoning and tool-call parsers.
- No TP8: the fused QKV weights are interleaved for 4-way TP (`num_key_value_heads = 4`), and SGLang requires the attention TP size to divide 4.

**vLLM settings** (from [vLLM's MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL.yaml), which names v0.31.0 as the first release that loads this checkpoint):
- `gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, `max-model-len auto` (the largest context the KV pool holds, for the uncapped AgentX corpus), `max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, `mimo` parsers.
- TP8 is valid here: vLLM regroups the fused QKV per rank and replicates KV heads.
- vLLM's `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` is text-only, so no `language-model-only` flag is needed.
- KV cache stays BF16: the MiMo FP8 KV fix (vllm-project/vllm#58128) landed after v0.31.0.

Thinking stays on for both engines, which is the chat template's default.

**Known gaps:**
- **No speculative decoding yet.** `infx/golden_al_distribution/` has no MiMo curve, so a speculative run would fail at launch. #4331 adds a vLLM collector for the checkpoint's DFlash drafter; DFlash arms follow once that curve is committed.
- **Weights are not pre-staged on `b200-nscale`.** `runners.yaml` has no entry for this model, so `hf:XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` is served from the shared HF hub cache, the same way as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on this cluster. The repo is not gated. The first job downloads the checkpoint.
- **Checkpoint choice.** Xiaomi has since released `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD` (same architecture and format), which fixes the RL release's tool-call repetition. This PR stays on the RL checkpoint; MOPD can be added separately.
- **Not in the engine-mapping table.** This PR adds only the MODELS.md support-matrix row; maintainers decide the model-to-engine mapping.
- **Not yet run end to end on GPUs.** The first canary failed at server startup on `language-model-only` (fixed above); the `full-sweep-fail-fast` sweep reruns on the latest commit.

为 [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL)（MiMoV2 架构，总参数 309B / 激活 15B）在 B200 上新增基于上游 SGLang 与上游 vLLM 的 AgentX 覆盖。两个配置键暂不使用投机解码。

**运行内容：** 新增两个配置键，共 24 个点。所有点的 KV 缓存都保留在 GPU 上（不做 CPU 卸载）。

| 配置键 | 镜像 | 测试点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-sglang-agentic` | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130` | TP4，并发 1、4、8、16、32、64；TP2，并发 1、4、8、16、32 |
| `mimov2.6flash-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic` | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` | TP8，并发 1、4；TP4，并发 1、4、8、16、32、64；TP2，并发 1、4、8、16、32 |

两个镜像均按 digest 固定。准入上限为并发的 2 倍，以容纳子 agent 扇出；decode CUDA graph 覆盖到并发数。

**精度（`fp4`），已对照检查点的 safetensors 头信息核实：**
- 路由专家约占参数量的 98%，以打包的 MXFP4 存储（E2M1，每 32 个值一个 E8M0 缩放因子）。
- 稠密 MLP、融合 QKV 与 MTP 层为 FP8 E4M3，采用 128×128 分块缩放。
- `o_proj`、路由器、词嵌入和 `lm_head` 为 BF16。
- 在 B200 上，两个引擎都以原生 MXFP4 权重 × MXFP8 激活（FlashInfer TRT-LLM）运行路由专家，FP8 层按分块缩放 FP8 运行。这与 `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` 的混合布局相同，本仓库将其标记为 `fp4`。

**SGLang 设置**（参照 [SGLang MiMo-V2.5 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Xiaomi/MiMo-V2.5)；V2.6-Flash 与 V2.5 采用相同的 `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` 架构，规模也相同）：
- `moe-runner-backend: flashinfer_mxfp4`。v0.5.21 的 MiMo 默认配置会在 SM100 上为任何 `quant_method: fp8` 的检查点选择 FP8 TRT-LLM runner，而它无法读取打包的 MXFP4 专家。上游修复（sgl-project/sglang#41668）在 v0.5.21 之后才合入。
- `attention-backend: fa4`：在 Blackwell 上，默认的 `trtllm_mha` 不支持 MiMoV2 的非对称 K/V head 维度。
- 不使用 `language-model-only`：v0.5.21 对 `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` 会拒绝该参数（首次 canary 因此在启动时失败）。因此会加载视觉与音频编码器（约 2 GB），ViT 使用 `mm-attention-backend: fa4`；纯文本的 AgentX 请求不会调用它们。
- `chunked-prefill-size 16384`、`mem-fraction-static 0.85`、`mimo` 推理与工具调用解析器。
- 无 TP8：融合 QKV 权重按 4 路 TP 交错存储（`num_key_value_heads = 4`），SGLang 要求注意力 TP 大小能整除 4。

**vLLM 设置**（参照 [vLLM 的 MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL 配方](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL.yaml)，其中指出 v0.31.0 是首个能加载该检查点的版本）：
- `gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`、`max-model-len auto`（KV 池能容纳的最大上下文，适配不截断的 AgentX 轨迹）、`max-num-batched-tokens 16384`、`mimo` 解析器。
- vLLM 可以跑 TP8：它会按 rank 重新组织融合 QKV，并复制 KV head。
- vLLM 的 `MiMoV2ForCausalLM` 只含文本部分，因此无需 `language-model-only`。
- KV 缓存保持 BF16：MiMo 的 FP8 KV 修复（vllm-project/vllm#58128）在 v0.31.0 之后才合入。

两个引擎都保持开启思考模式，这是 chat template 的默认行为。

**已知缺口：**
- **暂未启用投机解码。** `infx/golden_al_distribution/` 中还没有 MiMo 曲线，投机解码运行会在启动时失败。#4331 新增针对检查点 DFlash 草稿模型的 vLLM 采集脚本；曲线提交后再加入 DFlash 配置。
- **`b200-nscale` 上未预置权重。** `runners.yaml` 中没有该模型的条目，因此 `hf:XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` 从共享 HF hub 缓存加载，与 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 在该集群上的做法相同。该仓库不需要申请访问权限，首个任务会下载检查点。
- **检查点选择。** 小米随后发布了 `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD`（架构与格式相同），修复了 RL 版本的工具调用重复问题。本 PR 仍使用 RL 检查点，MOPD 可另行添加。
- **未加入引擎映射表。** 本 PR 只在 MODELS.md 支持矩阵中新增一行，模型与引擎的映射由维护者决定。
- **尚未在 GPU 上完整跑通。** 首次 canary 因 `language-model-only` 在服务启动时失败（已在上文修复）；`full-sweep-fail-fast` sweep 会在最新提交上重新运行。

**AI 模型使用说明：** Claude Opus 5.5（`claude-opus-5-5`），通过 Claude Code 使用，未委派其他 agent；负责调研、配方与配置编写、本地验证、sweep 排错以及 PR 准备。

**改动类型：** 新功能、配置变更、文档更新。

title: [AMD][MI355X] Kimi-K3 vLLM AgentX nightly 49cb2bbf with dcp1 c1-c4 and dcp8 c4-c60 sweep / [AMD][MI355X] Kimi-K3 vLLM AgentX 更新镜像至 nightly 49cb2bbf 并扫描 dcp1 c1-c4 与 dcp8 c4-c60
body:
## Summary
- Move `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp` (`configs/amd-master.yaml`) from `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`. Follows #3951.
- Set `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MIN_SIZE_BYTES_MB=16` in the recipe's base env, so it applies at every concurrency: QuickReduce (INT4) only handles all-reduces of 16 MB or more.
- Set `AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1` in the recipe's base env at every concurrency, matching `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-atom-agentic-mtp`.
- Drop `load-format: fastsafetensors`, so every point loads with vLLM's default safetensors loader. In [run 38975751686](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38975751686), 19 of 20 jobs failed before the server came up, on six different nodes. All four server logs inspected died during fastsafetensors weight loading: rank 3 or 4 ran out of GPU memory (`hipErrorLaunchOutOfResources`, 200-310 MB free) at shard 10 or 11 of 12.
- Every variant except `override_tp8_c1` sets `quantization-config: '{"targets":{"*in_proj_qkvgfab":"fp8_per_channel"}}'`, so only the KDA `in_proj_qkvgfab` projection is quantized online to FP8 per-channel. `override_tp8_c1` keeps its `fp8_per_channel` linear config but no longer ignores `*in_proj_qkvgfab`. Both strings pass vLLM's `QuantizationConfigArgs` validation at 49cb2bbf.
- New concurrency sweep: dcp1 c1 and c4 with no KV offload, plus dcp8 with the SimpleCPUOffload DRAM tier at c4, c10, c16, c24, c32, c48, c52 and c60. **dcp1 c4 and dcp8 c52/c60 are new**; dcp8 c1 and dcp8 c2 are dropped, along with their recipe variants.
- The new `override_tp8_c52_dcp8_simple` and `override_tp8_c60_dcp8_simple` use the c48 layout: a 4-token DSpark draft with synthetic acceptance, `max-num-seqs` set to 2 x CONC (104, 120), and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs at every even size up to 2 x CONC x 5 (520, 600).
- The new dcp1 `override_tp8_c4` uses a 7-token DSpark draft, matching `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-atom-agentic-mtp` at dcp1 c4.

| Variant | CONC | dcp | KV offload | DSpark k | max-num-seqs | max graph size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `override_tp8_c1` | 1 | 1 | none | 7 | 1 | 16 |
| `override_tp8_c4` (new) | 4 | 1 | none | 7 | 8 | 64 |
| `override_tp8_c4_dcp8_simple` | 4 | 8 | dram | 5 | 8 | 48 |
| `override_tp8_c10_dcp8_simple` | 10 | 8 | dram | 4 | 20 | 100 |
| `override_tp8_c16_dcp8_simple` | 16 | 8 | dram | 4 | 32 | 160 |
| `override_tp8_c24_dcp8_simple` | 24 | 8 | dram | 4 | 48 | 240 |
| `override_tp8_c32_dcp8_simple` | 32 | 8 | dram | 4 | 64 | 320 |
| `override_tp8_c48_dcp8_simple` | 48 | 8 | dram | 4 | 96 | 480 |
| `override_tp8_c52_dcp8_simple` (new) | 52 | 8 | dram | 4 | 104 | 520 |
| `override_tp8_c60_dcp8_simple` (new) | 60 | 8 | dram | 4 | 120 | 600 |
- The new image (343 commits after fe4df3df) brings these Kimi-K3 and ROCm changes: vllm-project/vllm#57392 (AITER Gluon KDA kernels for decode and spec decode), #61207 (fused KDA decode weights staged after loading), #61654 (the MLA wrapper no longer reads W_UK_T before weights load), #61895 (low-latency MoE router GEMM for any shape on MI355), #59406 (preshuffled FP4 GEMM config probed by logical K), #58381 (lighter MLA metadata build), #59070 (DCP prefill context kept in FP8 through AllGather), #59468 (DSpark draft slots no longer reserved in the scheduler token budget) and #61230 (AITER v0.1.25 base).
- **Draft data types: no change.** The Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark checkpoint is all BF16 with no `quantization_config`. At both images, `K3DSparkModel` (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py`, also used on ROCm) takes its quant config from `get_draft_quant_config()`, which reads the draft's own model config, so the target `quantization-config` does not reach the draft. The draft runs BF16 weights with an fp8 KV cache. Evidence is in the PR comment.

## Validation
- [Run 38975751686](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38975751686) (with fastsafetensors): only the dcp1 c1 benchmark job passed; the other 19 jobs failed before the server came up.
- [Run 39002920671](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39002920671) (default loader): all 20 Kimi-K3 jobs passed, benchmark and eval-only, at every point from dcp1 c1 to dcp8 c60.

<details><summary>中文</summary>

## 概要
- 将 `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`（`configs/amd-master.yaml`）的镜像由 `nightly-rocm100-fe4df3df…` 更新为 `nightly-rocm100-49cb2bbf…`。承接 #3951。

- 移除 `load-format: fastsafetensors`，所有并发点改用 vLLM 默认的 safetensors 加载器。在 [run 38975751686](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38975751686) 中，20 个作业里有 19 个在服务启动前失败，涉及 6 个不同节点。检查过的 4 份服务日志均在 fastsafetensors 加载权重时失败：加载到第 10 或 11/12 个分片时 rank 3 或 4 显存耗尽（`hipErrorLaunchOutOfResources`，剩余 200-310 MB）。

- 新镜像（fe4df3df 之后的 343 个提交）包含以下 Kimi-K3 与 ROCm 改动：vllm-project/vllm#57392（decode 与投机解码改用 AITER Gluon KDA kernel）、#61207（融合 KDA decode 权重在加载后再准备）、#61654（MLA wrapper 不再在权重加载前读取 W_UK_T）、#61895（MI355 上适用于任意 shape 的低延迟 MoE router GEMM）、#59406（按逻辑 K 探测 preshuffled FP4 GEMM 配置）、#58381（简化 MLA metadata 构建）、#59070（DCP prefill 上下文经 AllGather 时保持 FP8）、#59468（调度器 token 预算不再为 DSpark 草稿预留槽位）以及 #61230（基础镜像升级到 AITER v0.1.25）。

title: refactor(collectivex): use Python orchestration and consolidate modules / 统一 Python 编排并合并 CollectiveX 零散模块
body:
## Description

CollectiveX's workflow now calls Python directly. Python owns allocation, image/source staging, backend preparation, rank startup, retries, artifact collection, and cleanup; **all seven original CollectiveX Bash files are removed**. Job steps execute through the real `simple-slurm==0.3.6` API. Explicit `salloc --no-shell`, targeted queue queries, and cancellation preserve the existing allocation model.

The benchmark side separates the former monolithic harness (1,662 lines at the initial baseline; 1,774 in current main) into orchestration, measurement, correctness, and results. DeepEP/UCCL share compatible Buffer operations. Small helper modules were folded back into their owners: implementation files fell from **41 in the first refactor to 28**, versus **25 at the original baseline**. There is no shell-to-Python argument protocol or generated shell environment file.

This is intended to preserve behavior: matrix coverage, CLI arguments, workload/timing profiles, event ordering, source/image pins, cache identities, per-pool placement and retries, result schema, failures, and cleanup. All work stays in the worktree created from `origin/main` at `960ff1ffa51e160df422394e0477a4410fa65888`. The final integration merges current main at `4f94801a5` and preserves its concurrently landed CUDA-graph replay and NCCL rank-major/zero-copy changes; those are upstream behavior, not new refactor features.

**The 30% implementation LOC reduction target is not met.** Python plus Bash grows **194 physical lines (+2.1%)**. The final result has fewer files than the first refactor and no repository-owned Bash orchestration, but Python's explicit resource handling, argument lists, and process boundaries do not produce a net line reduction. Tests, error handling, and measurement explanations were not sacrificed to meet a percentage.

### Structure and call flow

`collectivex-sweep.yml → ci.py → runtime/execution.py → simple-slurm srun / Docker torchrun → runtime/node.py → bench/run_ep.py → EPBackend adapter → ep_harness.run_sweep → ep_results`

- `ci.py`: matrix/extraction, execution, independent finalization, and private-workspace cleanup.
- Runtime has **eight substantive modules**, plus its package initializer: `config.py` (pool policies/settings/arguments), `scheduler.py` (Slurm/processes/locks/logs), `probe.py` (hardware/network discovery and selectors), `storage.py` (images and staging), `build.py` (pins/source/build caches), `node.py` (compute-host preparation and rank bootstrap), `execution.py` (shard lifecycle), and `docker.py` (Slurm-less pools).
- `run_ep.py` owns CLI setup and lazy backend dispatch. `ep_backend.py` owns the abstract transport/input contract. `ep_measurement.py` owns `EPTiming`, event timing, reductions, and samples. `ep_harness.py` orders passes, `ep_oracle.py` checks them, and `ep_results.py` owns identity/accounting/publication.
- `BufferOperations` in `ep_buffer.py` shares the active DeepEP/UCCL Buffer operations; vendor constructors, quantizers, and different normal transports remain in their adapters. `EPBackend` inherits `EPTiming`; orchestration mostly uses functions and data classes, with `SlurmAllocation` owning one allocation.
- Swap-blocks uses the same cluster lifecycle with its existing independent benchmark and schema. OperatorX's probe and runtime-directory consumers remain covered.

[English implementation map](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/refactor/collectivex-modules/experimental/CollectiveX/docs/architecture.md) · [中文实现导览](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/refactor/collectivex-modules/experimental/CollectiveX/docs/architecture_zh.md)

### LOC and file accounting

Baseline: current main `4f94801a5`, so upstream changes are excluded from the PR totals. Physical lines, including comments and blanks, across `experimental/CollectiveX/` and its workflow. Moves are counted in both revisions. Environments, generated results, local validation tools/logs, and the dependency manifest/lockfile are excluded from this feature-local table.

| Category | Current main | Final | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Python implementation | 6,980 | 9,578 | +2,598 |
| Bash implementation | 2,404 | 0 | -2,404 |
| Tests | 3,057 | 4,025 | +968 |
| Documentation | 1,235 | 1,756 | +521 |
| Configuration/workflow | 602 | 552 | -50 |
| Other | 15 | 15 | 0 |
| **Total** | **14,293** | **15,926** | **+1,633** |

Implementation excluding blank lines, standalone comments, and Python docstrings: **6,608 → 6,777 (+169)**. Standalone implementation comments/docstrings: **1,919 → 1,839**; blank lines: **857 → 962**. Repeated shell scaffolding/commentary is consolidated; the non-obvious transport, timing, build, and cleanup rationale stays with the code or the architecture guide.

| Files under CollectiveX | Original | First refactor | Final |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Implementation | 25 | 41 | 28 |
| Tests | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| Docs | 4 | 6 | 8 |
| Config/other | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| **Total** | **39** | **58** | **48** |

The added docs include the previously missing Chinese README/methodology counterparts, required when updating their stale paths and local-check instructions. All 106 current-main test methods remain; 29 were added. Test methods were relocated when consolidating files.

Outside that table, `pyproject.toml` adds 3 lines, `uv.lock` adds 13 net lines, and the existing SRT launcher test fixture adds 3 net lines.

### Commits and validation

Each logical commit is independently tested over the full local CI scope: `utils/`, `runners/`, CollectiveX and OperatorX, excluding upstream `utils/srt-slurm`. Each has the existing GPU-only `swap_blocks` skip on this CPU host.

| Commit | Responsibility | Passing tests / subtests |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `850d65ea2` | Harness decomposition | 2,001 / 184 |
| `a815489f9` | Shared correctness lifecycle | 2,004 / 190 |
| `172623c2b` | Shared legacy operations and timing | 2,006 / 190 |
| `4e2b256e6` | Runtime/build helper boundaries | 2,009 / 190 |
| `97b3dde6d` | Reuse untimed combine paths; remove redundant state | 2,011 / 194 |
| `fc1f14c55` | Initial architecture guide | 2,011 / 194 |
| `a9e09e413` | Python/simple-slurm foundation | 2,017 / 194 |
| `ddac8b4ae` | Python node/build/cache lifecycle | 2,024 / 194 |
| `d9938c972` | Python execution/workflow; remove Bash; consolidate modules | 2,030 / 194 |
| `940da8f39` | Rendezvous diagnostic isolation; consolidate tests | 2,030 / 194 |
| `65dc61694` | Bilingual runtime documentation | 2,030 / 194 |
| `ecd380cff` | Integrate current main; relocate graph behavior; repair upstream Git test double | 2,046 / 196 |
| `c475d9e81` | Rename active shared Buffer operations and update imports/docs | 2,046 / 196 |

- Before integration, six deterministic harness executions matched the original baseline. After integration, **ten executions match current main**: complete artifacts (excluding `generated_at`), return codes, and operation traces for eager success/pre/post/chain/error/drift and graph success/no-rewrite/output-failure/post-failure. The full generated matrix also matches.
- Real CLI tests use the installed `simple-slurm` library against executable Slurm/Docker doubles, covering literal metacharacter arguments, bare/Pyxis flags, cache reuse/failures, remote zipapp execution, rank bootstrap, preparation failure, thermal retry, continuing after case failure, SIGTERM/143, artifact collection, Docker retries, and runner-UID block copies.
- [H200 NCCL EP8 low-latency live run](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36113678473) **passed** on `940da8f39`: all nine measured ladder points passed correctness, chained-output and post-chain checks; artifacts uploaded and allocation/staging cleanup completed.
- The first live run exposed scheduler diagnostics being read as the rendezvous address. `940da8f39` adds an explicit machine-readable address marker and a regression test exercising the actual zipapp/library path with stderr diagnostics. The successful run above validates that fix.
- Pre-rename head `ecd380cff`: [hosted Tests/Lint](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36115249936) and [workflow security](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36115249937) **passed**.
- The integration-head H200 and MI300X Docker canaries remained queued with no benchmark execution and were cancelled before handoff. Earlier extra queued canaries were also cancelled when main changed. The successful H200 run above predates that integration; **no final-head GPU, Docker hardware, or full-fleet validation is claimed**.
- Repository Ruff checks and additional unused-name checks pass. Workflow security audit passes, with two narrow documented custom-Python-shell exceptions for bootstrap steps. Local full-suite runs use Bash 5.2 built inside the worktree; macOS Bash 3.2's missing `mapfile` caused unrelated failures, and no runner code was changed to accommodate it.
- Rename head `c475d9e81` passes the same full local suite (2,046 tests, 196 subtests, one GPU-only skip) and lint.
- A narrow live canary is not a full fleet sweep or a statistical proof of transport-performance equivalence.

### Judgment calls

1. **Library choice:** use portable `simple-slurm`, without requiring Slurm-version-matched PySlurm headers/shared libraries on every runner. It really executes each `srun`. Its API internally invokes a shell; all dynamic values are quoted. “No Bash orchestration” does not mean the library never invokes `/bin/sh`.
2. **Allocation semantics:** keep explicit allocations and native lifecycle queries/cancellation because replacing them with `sbatch` changes resource ownership and cancellation behavior. Do not add a Python daemon or cluster service.
3. **Small-file consolidation:** configuration owns pool policies and block-copy arguments; probes own network selectors; scheduler owns process helpers; builds own dependency pins; measurement owns timing; CLI/identity/ladder helpers live with their consumers. Keep genuine process boundaries and numerical responsibilities separate. Name the active shared implementation `ep_buffer.py`/`BufferOperations`; it is not deprecated compatibility code.
4. **No numeric redesign:** retain explicit isolated timing and sibling chain loops, event placement, call depth, source pins, quantizers, and different wire contracts. Combine sharing applies to untimed oracle work.
5. **Worker environments:** install the host dependency with the locked `collectivex` extra, but invoke its interpreter directly so the host venv does not replace the pinned container's `PATH`/Python. Compute-host utilities travel as a stdlib zipapp; vendor imports remain lazy. Node setup publishes a private, allowlisted JSON environment instead of executable shell text.
6. **Recovery:** preserve per-pool allocation/health/image retry policies and cache keys. Persist allocation/container ownership for independent finalization; stop jobs before collection/deletion, retain recovery state when stop is unconfirmed, and preserve signal exit status. AMD Docker block copies retain runner UID/GID, and Python bytecode writes are disabled for container utilities.
7. **Concurrent main changes:** merge the newly landed graph-replay/NCCL changes into their new owners and compare against that main revision. Keep the same graph defaults, capture/replay events, rank-major reduction, and output fields. One existing SRT test double needed to recognize Git global `-c`/`-C` options used by main; this fixes 14 unrelated test failures without changing production launcher code.
8. **Scope/LOC:** favor behavioral equivalence and explicit handling over the 30% target; report the shortfall and test/docs growth honestly. No recipe, image, source pin, workload or timing-profile change is intended, so `perf-changelog.yaml` is untouched. No full serving sweep/eval reuse or merge authorization is claimed.

## AI model disclosure

GPT-6 performed implementation, self-review, tests, docs and PR preparation as the sole agent. The runtime exposes no more specific deployment/version identifier, so a more exact version could not be independently verified. No subagents were used for this refactor.

## Related issue / change type

User-requested structural refactor and documentation update; no associated issue. This PR does not merge or publish a performance dataset.

title: Document and test ordinary sync-free receive tensor lifetimes
body:
## Summary

Document and exercise the lifetime contract of **ordinary independently allocated receive outputs** from compact `dispatch(do_cpu_sync=False)`.

- Add a README paragraph explaining valid receive prefixes, output ownership versus stream readiness, the explicit ready-event/`record_stream` handoff, and why a prefix view retains the full capacity allocation.
- Add a 166-line standalone native regression for saved-view backward after later dispatches and delayed cross-stream consumers under allocator pressure.

No production Python/C++/CUDA implementation, default, or API changes. The internal dispatch copy epilogue still runs. This is not borrowed communication-buffer storage or a zero-copy dispatch implementation.

## Regression coverage

The new `tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py` uses the independent NCCL dispatch reference and requires bitwise equality of payloads, local expert indices, routing weights, source-token metadata, and the saved-activation weight gradient.

Each process run covers:

- Deterministic dispatch off/on; output allocation on the compute/communication stream.
- Uneven inputs, balanced routes, masked routes, and highly skewed routing with empty receivers.
- Two selected experts on the same destination rank, distinguishing unique receive rows from token/expert assignments.
- A prefix saved with `ctx.save_for_backward`, followed by three additional dispatches through the same buffer before backward.
- A delayed reader on another stream, dropping the original receive allocation references and allocating/filling four same-capacity tensors on the allocation stream. The copy destination and allocator warm-up are prepared before the delay. Pressure writes must finish while a **pre-read** event is still pending; a pending post-copy event alone is insufficient.

Scheduling can miss the pressure window. All ranks agree on numerical correctness and window validity, then retry in collective lockstep with a longer delay (at most three attempts). Actual corruption fails immediately; an inconclusive window is never silently reported as coverage.

The consumer handoff uses a CUDA event captured **after the first dispatch-event wait**, including its deterministic-sort hook. It does not depend on repeated waits on the original `EventOverlap`; that is separate from this lifetime coverage.

## Validation

### Current polished revision

Head: `97fa6d18ff717df99acbdbb862325bda3d4a0d46`, based on public main `b5a33eefda39485f438dc764695b71ba7b9249b6`.

The current 166-line test passed on H200 with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA 13.2 and NCCL 2.32.3. Each native lifetime policy was run once with eight ranks: 24 distributed saved-prefix/backward cases in total, with 24 valid delayed-consumer allocator-pressure windows. This is positive coverage of the current reorganized test; the historical negative and scheduling controls below were not rerun against this revision.

```bash
EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=0 python tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 64 --hidden 512
EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=1 python tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 64 --hidden 512
```

### Historical validation of the earlier test version

Tested commit: `01c31d0d75f155ca00ba933a6b9ab7a01459169e`, based on upstream `93eb6eb238127e96c6d7a4a625a6dad158348509`. The results in this subsection belong to that earlier test version, not to a rerun of the current 166-line test.

One node, eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs in a single NVLink domain; PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA runtime 13.2, loaded NCCL 2.32.3. The unchanged upstream native extension and the tested source archive/test-file hashes were verified. No borrowed-view implementation or event-wrapper patch was included.

Both native lifetime policies were run in fresh processes, three repeats each, using the same two command lines above.

Validation controls: `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, `EP_REUSE_NCCL_COMM=0`, `EP_BUFFER_DEBUG=0`, `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Seed 42; deterministic PyTorch algorithms enabled with uninitialized-memory filling disabled.

| Native record-stream policy | Fresh repeats per arm | Positive rank/cases | Exact saved-view gradients | Deleted-record rejections | Forced-retry passes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=0` | 3 | 288/288 | 288/288 | 96/96 | 96/96 |
| `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=1` | 3 | 288/288 | 288/288 | 96/96 | 96/96 |

Two additional controls were run outside the PR using that exact earlier public test source, without changing DeepEP's implementation:

- **Negative control:** AST-remove exactly the consumer-side `prefix.record_stream(reader)` expression from `cross_stream_pressure`. For balanced nonempty receives, run both deterministic modes and both allocation streams. All 24 distributed cases were rejected by the specific `CROSS_STREAM_RECEIVE_MISMATCH` assertion; actual local data corruption was observed in all 192 rank/cases. Other assertions or an ineffective window do not count as detection.
- **Scheduling control:** synchronize only rank 0 immediately before its first `pending_before` query. All ranks must retry attempt 0 together and pass on a later effective attempt. All 24 distributed cases / 192 rank/cases passed.

An earlier draft's post-copy-event stress missed the deleted-record mutation. That draft is not the sensitivity evidence above; the pre-read/completed-pressure ordering and destination preallocation were added before rerunning all historical arms.

All eighteen historical fresh launches exited successfully. Source/input hashes, exact per-rank coverage, control mutation identities and completion/exit sentinels were audited from downloaded logs. Archive SHA256: `834a31fa761e439678244ae49cdaf98491ead5fb23b4724500ba038366eac777`.

Local checks for that earlier revision: Python compilation, Ruff 0.6.5, YAPF 0.40.2 (no diff), and `git diff --check` passed.

## Scope

This establishes component lifetime/gradient correctness for ordinary compact BF16 receives in one physical NVLink domain. It does not establish full-model convergence, training throughput gains, borrowed-storage safety, FP8/expanded layouts, or multi-node hybrid routing. Capacity-retention assertions deliberately distinguish logical tensor bytes from retained storage bytes.

title: perf: skip unused source-order sorts for expanded deterministic dispatch
body:
Fresh expanded deterministic dispatch runs its own stable expert/source sort, and cached expanded dispatch writes into the saved sorted slots, so the compact source-order sort computed before them is never consumed. `deterministic_sort` now returns early for cached expanded dispatch and only builds the compact sort inside the compact branch.

| Deterministic layout | Sorts before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh expanded | 2 | 1 |
| Cached expanded | 1 | 0 |
| Compact | 1 | 1 |

Two repeated-dispatch checks in `tests/ep/test_ep.py` now compare only the valid receive prefix: unused sync-free capacity is undefined even without expert-alignment padding.

8×H200 (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132): the EP8 functional suite passes (72 direct + 36 deferred configurations, 12,288 rank-dispatch checks across both record-stream policies, BF16/FP8, CPU/GPU counts, fresh/cached); fresh expanded dispatch at 1024 tokens/rank, hidden 3072, top-8 is 4.7–5.8% faster (12/12 process repeats on each of two nodes, A/A spread 0.81%). Per-process data: [gist](https://gist.github.com/yuweih205/1696535356c2654b255f28617f9fa96f).

DeepEP V2.5 是一次 V2 → V2.5 的大重构（163 文件，+11.7k/−17.4k）：删除 V1/NVSHMEM/fmt，引入 DeepJIT 子模块做运行时编译，把 ElasticBuffer 拆成 EPBuffer/EngramBuffer/PPBuffer/BucketBuffer（共享 BufferBase + comm::Context），新增 LB 权重预取/梯度归约、bucket 集合通信（all-gather/reduce-scatter/all-reduce）和 deferred epilogue。整体架构清晰，comm::Context 抽象出符号内存 + NCCL window + GIN 生命周期后各 buffer 实现明显变薄。已确认 V1/NVSHMEM/fmt/legacy 相关引用（csrc/utils/format.hpp、hash.hpp、lazy_init.hpp、shared_memory.hpp、docs/legacy.md、docs/nvshmem.md 等）在源码中无残留。
但存在几类需要在合并前处理的问题：(1) .gitmodules 使用 SSH 地址，匿名用户无法初始化子模块；(2) 新开启 ruff Q000 规则且几乎全部 .py 文件都在 diff 内，多处 Q000/F541/B904/B010/E722/W293 会让 format.yml CI 失败；(3) 测试中使用了 dist.all_gather_single / dist.reduce_scatter_single，需确认 PyTorch 是否提供；(4) EP_NIC_NAME 环境变量被静默删除且 BucketBuffer 硬性要求同时检测到 NVLink 和 RDMA 带宽，非 mlx5_0 NIC 或无 IB 机器上不可用；(5) do_handle_copy/sl_idx 默认值静默变更；(6) 托管 NCCL comm 与 Context::finalize 的析构顺序风险；(7) comm.get_comm_stream 模块级签名与方法绑定冲突。此外 deep_ep/include/deep_ep/impls/bucket/** 的设备内核（约 1.8k 行）只审阅了接口层，同步语义需由能在多机 GPU 上运行 tests/bucket/* 与 tests/ep/test_ep.py 的同学确认。本次为静态审阅，无法编译或运行 GPU 测试。
v4
DeepEP V2.5 是一个体量很大的重构 PR：删除 V1/legacy 与 NVSHMEM 依赖，把通信能力拆分为 EPBuffer / BucketBuffer / EngramBuffer / PPBuffer 四类 buffer，统一 BufferBase、comm::Context 与 DeepJIT 运行时，并新增 bucket 集合通信、冗余专家权重预取/梯度归约、延迟 epilogue、多 layer Engram 等能力。整体结构清晰、测试覆盖（尤其 tests/bucket/test_mixed.py）较充分；但本 PR 引入了一个明确的功能回归（EP_NIC_NAME 被删除），并存在若干接口安全性与文档一致性问题。

With the evolution of hardware, networking, and model architectures, the previous DeepEP V1 had accumulated too much legacy baggage and performance issues. Today, we are excited to introduce
DeepEP V2
, which includes a complete refactoring of Expert Parallelism — achieving extreme performance with several times fewer SM resources compared to V1, while supporting significantly larger scale-up and scale-out domains — as well as experimental 0 SM Engram, 0 SM Pipeline Parallelism, and 0 SM Context Parallelism all-gather.
We are also happy to announce that we have switched from the NVSHMEM backend to the more lightweight
NCCL Gin backend
.
New Features
Fully JIT (Just-In-Time compilation)
NCCL Gin backend
Header-only & lightweight
Able to reuse existing NCCL communicators
EPv2
CUDA graph compatible, or faster CPU sync in saving memory mode
High-throughput and low-latency APIs unified into a single interface, with a new GEMM layout
Larger scale-up & scale-out domain support (up to EP2048)
Analytical SM & QP count calculation — no more auto-tuning needed
Both hybrid & direct modes remain supported
For V3-like legacy training, SM usage reduced from 24 to 4 - 6 while maintaining equivalent or better performance
0 SM Engram (with RDMA)
0 SM PP (with RDMA)
0 SM CP (with Copy Engine)
Notes
Buffer size consumption is larger than V1
0 SM RDMA low-latency EP is no longer supported
Engram, PP, and CP are experimental features
Still On-going Features
Elastic GPU & CPU buffers
: A contiguous virtual address space that maps to a hybrid of GPU and CPU physical memory under the hood, enabling fully automatic and transparent Engram or imbalanced EP
Reducing intermediate buffer sizes by leveraging EP replay to handle load imbalance
All-gather updates and reduce-scatter implementations for DP & TP

Bumps the deep_ep git pin in pyproject.toml from bfded348
(2025-10-29, pre-V2) to b306af0 (2026-04-29), which is the
merge commit of DeepEP PR
NVIDIA-NeMo#605
"Introducing EPv2".

Why
---
The current pin predates the DeepEP V2 API (ElasticBuffer,
PP/CP/Engram support). Consumers of NeMo-RL's Megatron backend
that follow
NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#4632
("Shape Y" Megatron V2
adoption) cannot resolve deep_ep.ElasticBuffer with the
current pin; the virtualenv still installs the pre-V2 tree.

This change bumps only the pin. It does not by itself change
any NeMo-RL code path. Paired with Megatron-LM#4632, it
enables the end-to-end V2 path that is already running on
AWS p5en.48xlarge 2x H200 in the reproduction repo below.

(V2 merge 2026-04-29)

(Megatron-side V2 adoption)

Add `RTP_LLM_DEEPEP_BACKEND={legacy,elastic}` runtime switch so rtp-llm can
keep the v1-compatible `deep_ep::legacy::Buffer` path (default) and
opt into the v2 unified `ElasticBuffer` (PR
deepseek-ai/DeepEP#605
) without
forking the engine. Unknown values silently fall back to legacy so a typo
never flips a production deploy to v2.

- deepep_wrapper.py: add DeepEPBackend / deepep_backend() / is_elastic_buffer
  helpers, branch _init_deepep_buffer at the entry, and add a new
  _init_elastic_buffer that uses ElasticBuffer.get_buffer_size_hint to size
  the unified buffer. The three legacy init paths
  (_init_normal_buffer / _init_low_latency_buffer / _init_low_latency_m2n_buffer)
  are kept verbatim so v1 behavior is preserved.
- deepep_normal_router.py: branch prepare()/finalize() at the entry on
  is_elastic_buffer(); the elastic path skips get_dispatch_layout (unified
  API computes layout internally), uses the v2 dispatch 5-tuple and reads
  num_recv_tokens_per_expert_list from EPHandle. The legacy 6-tuple call
  site is untouched.
- deepep_low_latency_router.py: collapse the v1 two-API setup
  (low_latency_dispatch / low_latency_combine) onto ElasticBuffer's unified
  dispatch / combine when the elastic backend is active. _is_elastic is
  cached at construction time so prepare()/finalize() only branch once.

moe: add DeepEP V2 ElasticBuffer probe and opt-in buffer path
…
1d6b522
DeepEP V2 (
deepseek-ai/DeepEP#605
, merged 2026-04-29) introduces
`ElasticBuffer` alongside the legacy `Buffer`. Both classes are
exported from `deep_ep.__init__`, so SGLang's existing V1 code path
continues to work unchanged on a V2 install.

This patch adds a second import probe (`have_deepep_v2`) next to the
existing `use_deepep` flag, then lets users opt in to the V2
`ElasticBuffer` ctor behind `SGLANG_DEEPEP_USE_V2=1`. The V1 path is
byte-identical when the env var is unset, so this is a backwards-
compatible addition.

V2 collapses the V1 NVL/RDMA byte-pool ctor into a single MoE-shape
ctor and derives the internal buffer size from `num_max_tokens_per_rank`,
`hidden`, and `num_topk`. `num_allocated_qps=0` asks V2 to auto-size
and auto-cap the Queue-Pair budget on AWS EFA (the 128-slot GIN ring
ceiling; see `_is_efa_fabric` in `deep_ep/buffers/elastic.py`).

Why:
- Removes the need for users to monkeypatch `deep_ep.Buffer` to reach
  V2 semantics, and mirrors the probe shape already used in
  NVIDIA/Megatron-LM's `fused_a2a.py` (`HAVE_DEEP_EP_V2`). Opt-in
  env-var gate keeps the change infra-bump-shaped, not a default
  switch flip.
- vLLM is landing a parallel native-V2 path in
vllm-project/vllm#41183
(16 commits, active review). SGLang users
  running mixed-framework MoE stacks benefit from having V2 reachable
  in SGLang without a runtime monkeypatch.

V2 parity rules baked in:
- `num_max_tokens_per_rank` sourced from
  `envs.SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` when the
  caller did not pin it (matches the V1 low-latency path).
- `num_topk=0` at ctor time: DeepEP V2 accepts this and derives a
  conservative group-size-based hint, so we don't need to know the
  router topk at buffer construction.
- `clean_buffer()` skips the legacy `clean_low_latency_buffer` call
  when the underlying buffer is an ElasticBuffer (no equivalent on
  V2, per `deep_ep/buffers/elastic.py`).

title: github:deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM:411 fetched implementation patch
Fix cross-expert output overwrites in SM90 masked GEMM
body:
SM90 masked GEMM flattens the output into a 2D TMA descriptor. When a store tile extends past an expert's capacity, it can overwrite valid rows of the next expert. This affects both BF16 and FP8: capacity 32 reproduces it, and capacity 96 also fails when experts are nearly full.

Keep the expert dimension in the output descriptor and reuse the existing 3D TMA store path. This preserves tile selection and the compute pipeline without adding buffers or synchronization. Boundary regressions are integrated into the existing BF16 and FP8 test suites.

This revisits the limitation discussed in #15 and the small-capacity failure reported in #268. #15 previously fixed small capacities by shrinking the store tile and rejected larger capacities not divisible by the tile size; it also suggested 3D TMA but deferred support for those cases. This change handles both small and non-tile-aligned capacities through the same output path.

On H200, the median paired latency changes across six rounds were between −0.17% and +0.16% for the larger tested shapes. The smallest shape was about 1.9% slower for BF16 and 1.5% slower for FP8, roughly 0.06–0.08 µs. The uniform 3D path avoids maintaining separate aligned and unaligned implementations, at that small measured cost.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation</summary>

Requires an SM90 GPU and a source build of DeepGEMM. Save the following as `repro.py` outside the source checkout and run `python repro.py` against the installed baseline or patched package:

```python
import torch
import deep_gemm
from deep_gemm.testing import calc_diff

torch.manual_seed(29)
a = torch.randn((8, 32, 256), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
b = torch.randn((8, 256, 256), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
d = torch.empty((8, 32, 256), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
counts = torch.tensor([0, 1, 16, 31, 32, 1, 32, 32],
                      device='cuda', dtype=torch.int)
valid = torch.arange(32, device='cuda')[None, :] < counts[:, None]
reference = torch.bmm(a.double(), b.double().mT).bfloat16()

for _ in range(16):
    deep_gemm.m_grouped_bf16_gemm_nt_masked(a, b, d, counts, 32)
    diff = calc_diff(d[valid], reference[valid])
    assert diff < 1e-5, f'{diff=}'
```

Running this exact script against the baseline failed with `AssertionError: diff=tensor(0.1456, device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.float64)`; the patched wheel completed all 16 checks. Only valid rows are checked; padding values are unspecified.

Run the included regressions from the checkout after building and installing the patched package:

```bash
cd tests
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import test_bf16
import test_fp8_fp4

torch.manual_seed(17)
test_bf16.test_m_grouped_gemm_masked_boundaries()
test_fp8_fp4.test_m_grouped_gemm_masked_boundaries()
PY
```

Both passed with the final built wheel, including a fresh-JIT-cache run. Both fail at capacity 16 when run against the baseline package. A separate timed run with the JIT cache populated took 0.23 s for the BF16 test body and 0.09 s for FP8; this excludes process startup and imports, and does not estimate cold compilation time.

Supplemental validation, using separate local harnesses not included in this PR:

- Base: `057ca5964aae0879ff2e0eb71ee05a3cb0ba3df7`; candidate: `20865936a058d55c4c583cc2b0c2bcf3bc319a2f`. H200, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0.
- 34 configurations per arm, covering BF16 and FP8, capacities from 1 to 257, single-expert and all-empty cases; 16 eager and 16 Graph calls each. Baseline and revert each had 24 failing configurations; the fix had none. Two configurations were all-empty and only checked completion. The revert reused the original package in a fresh process/cache.
- Independent FP64 matmul references, rounded to BF16; FP8 references used the actual quantized inputs and scales. No run-to-run changes were observed in the fixed panel.
- 37 adjacent-path checks passed, covering ordinary GEMM layouts, output dtypes and accumulation, batched GEMM, and K-grouped GEMM.
- Native `python setup.py bdist_wheel` passed with setuptools `75.8.0`.

Performance used six paired rounds with alternating arm order. Each measurement took the median of seven CUDA-event samples, each containing 1,000 Graph calls. Input generation and quantization were outside timing; FP8 API scale conversion was included. Positive values below mean slower; values are medians of paired latency changes.

| Groups | Capacity | N | K | Expected M | BF16 | FP8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 128 | 256 | 256 | 64 | +1.931% | +1.526% |
| 32 | 4096 | 1536 | 2048 | 20 | +0.070% | −0.143% |
| 6 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 1024 | +0.155% | +0.023% |
| 32 | 4096 | 6144 | 7168 | 192 | −0.167% | −0.056% |

Clocks were not locked; sampled SM clocks ranged from 1305 to 1980 MHz. Small differences on the larger shapes should not be interpreted as established speedups. CPU launch latency, model-level impact, other GPU architectures, and the full build matrix were not evaluated.

</details>

title: Update CUTLASS to 4.8.0 for SM107 (Rubin) support
body:
## Summary

We encountered TMA/TMEM device assertions while running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash through vLLM on Rubin (SM107). Could DeepGEMM update its vendored CUTLASS dependency from **4.2.1 to 4.8.0**, which adds initial SM107 support?

The failure was observed with `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` at `e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f`. We also confirmed that upstream [`deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM` at `78b6900`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/tree/78b69000794d0937b47ae3387eff7663410264d1/third-party) carries the same CUTLASS pin, `f3fde58372d33e9a5650ba7b80fc48b3b49d40c8`. The dependency limitation is therefore shared, although we have not reproduced the runtime failure on an unmodified upstream checkout.

The DSV4.1-Flash error output is included below. A colleague reported similar behavior with GLM5.3 on Rubin, which suggests the issue is not model-specific.

## Observed failure

In our September 22, 2026 run, model weights loaded, but startup profiling failed before requests could be served. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the stack pointed to `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`:

```text
Trying to use TMA Descriptor Prefetch without CUTE_ARCH_TMA_SM90_ENABLED.
Attempting to use TMEM allocation PTX without CUTE_ARCH_TCGEN05_TMEM_ENABLED
CUDA error 710 (CUDA_ERROR_ASSERT): device-side assert triggered
```

DeepGEMM's [pinned architecture selector](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepJIT/blob/e5bdee2bc4ca519eba00cfc5f0c6e950e6a96a16/include/deep_jit/backend/cuda/device.hpp#L68-L79) selects `sm_107f` for capability 10.7. However, the [pinned CUTLASS headers](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/f3fde58372d33e9a5650ba7b80fc48b3b49d40c8/include/cutlass/arch/config.h) lack SM107 enablement; their SM100 feature guards require `__CUDA_ARCH__ == 1000`. The errors indicate that the affected CuTe TMA/TMEM helpers were compiled without their feature macros enabled, selecting assertion fallbacks. This is consistent with an architecture-guard mismatch.

## Environment

| Component | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| GPU | Rubin, SM107 / compute capability 10.7 |
| Host architecture | Linux ARM64 |
| Driver | 620.43 |
| CUDA runtime | 13.4; exact NVCC patch version was not captured |
| Python | 3.12.3 |
| PyTorch | `2.15.0.dev20260908+cu134` |
| vLLM | `0.29.1rc1.dev513+g0961bbae2.d20260922.cu134` |
| vLLM source | `0961bbae2894d574be790d219651824eb199318e` |
| DeepGEMM | vLLM fork, `e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f` |
| Current CUTLASS | **4.2.1**, `f3fde58372d33e9a5650ba7b80fc48b3b49d40c8` |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` |
| Model revision | `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277` |

Base container:

```text
vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-0961bbae2894d574be790d219651824eb199318e@sha256:551a8c08c5119b5dbc7e902aabcd6ce2d903f084f76d4fa13fd887008bfd83d3
```

Configuration: TP4, V2 model runner, eager execution, CPU-offloaded Engram, no speculative decoding, maximum model length 32768, maximum sequences 8, and maximum batched tokens 8192. The optional `mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13==0.3.13.post1` package was installed, but the Mooncake connector was disabled for this diagnostic run.

## Proposed update and current workaround

Update the CUTLASS submodule pin from **4.2.1 to [4.8.0](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/releases/tag/v4.8.0)**, released **September 21, 2026 PDT / September 22 UTC**. This release adds initial Rubin support, including enabling existing SM100-compatible kernels for `sm_107a` and `sm_107f` and updating TMEM handling.

The release notes specify the R615 driver associated with CUDA 13.4 GA for SM107 execution and state that R610 from the Developer Preview is insufficient. Our recorded run used driver **620.43**.

Our temporary workaround sets DeepGEMM's JIT compiler target to `sm_100f` when the device reports capability 10.7. This allowed the exercised DSV4.1-Flash paths to run in a separate custom build; it was not a controlled A/B against the failing container above.

## Validation and questions

We have not tested the 4.8.0 upgrade. We do have SM107 access and can run DSV4.1-Flash against a candidate branch to confirm whether the failure clears.

Is updating CUTLASS to 4.8.0 the recommended approach for SM107 support? Are there known compatibility or regression concerns, or required DeepGEMM changes beyond the submodule bump?

Issue body actions
Description
On SM90 GPUs, tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm can produce incorrect and non-deterministic GEMM outputs when processing multiple K blocks.
Repeated calls with identical inputs can return different results.
Root cause
The kernel uses asynchronous WGMMA instructions with register-source A operands. Previously, the next iteration loaded its A fragment
before waiting for the preceding iteration's WGMMA to complete. This could overwrite A registers while they were still being read by
the in-flight WGMMA.
Fix
Proposed fix:
#448
The fix moves
warpgroup_wait<0>()
immediately after
warpgroup_commit_batch()
, ensuring that each iteration's WGMMA completes
before its A registers are reused.
The PR also adds a regression test covering split-K, PDL enabled/disabled, and default/side streams. It checks outputs against FP32
references and verifies repeatability across identical launches.
Validation
With the fix applied, both the existing hyperconnection tests and all 24 configurations of the new regression test passed on an SM90
GPU.

fix will introduce some performance regression which suppose to be mitigated in upcoming PRs。

Currently, every DFlash/DSpark config caps max_length at 4096 and sets no RoPE scaling, so it is not possible to finetune a drafter for long context, which is where acceptance length degrades the most. This PR adds optional rope_scaling / max_position_embeddings config fields and a long-context config.
