title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3
body:
## Summary

PR adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3 on ROCm. Part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion (#51303): each model needs varlen-capable sparse kernels before adaptive verification can redistribute draft tokens across requests
It was validated end to end with amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 and nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark on MI325.

Scope: only the ROCm Triton indexer and sparse-decode paths gain ragged decode support. The CUDA and AITER MiniMax M3 backends still report device/CPU query-length mismatch as unsupported, so adaptive verification stays disabled there. With adaptive verification off, the uniform decode path is unchanged.

## Changes

- MiniMax M3 indexer and sparse attention (ROCm Triton): device-side ragged decode metadata; both AMD index-score launch policies, the fused top-k selector, and sparse decode map packed query tokens to requests from device `query_start_loc`.
- `kernel_paged_attention_2d`: return for `query_len != 1` (previously `> 1`). FULL cudagraph replay can pad the request dimension with zero-length rows, which fell into the decode path and read one row past the logical query buffer.
- Rejection sampler: adaptive verification allows the regular chunked path for batches with no draft tokens, whose logits layout isnever compacted.
- Warmup: synthetic draft rows are bounded by the same rejection-sampler budget used at runtime, so large `max_num_seqs` configs nolonger fail at startup.
- Adaptive verification overhead: confidence D2H copies use a non-blocking ring, and only TP rank 0 computes the draft budget, thenbroadcasts it.
- DSpark config: prefer speculators-format top-level confidence-head fields and fall back to NVIDIA's legacy `dflash_config` fields.


Token-to-request mapping uses upstream's `compute_token_to_req_indices`, a device-side binary search over `query_start_loc`. It doesn't depend on `max_query_len` and handles zero-length rows and the padding tail.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs (adaptive verification, MiniMax M3 DSpark, token-to-request mapping, paged-decode zero-length). The closest is #52893, which skips AITER sparse PA under spec decode; this PR adds ragged decode to the Triton path instead.

## Testing

On MI325:
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`: 138 passed, 1 skipped.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: all passed.
- `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention` (`chunked_prefill_paged_decode`, source build of this branch): 128 passed, 256 skipped.

- Stress test of the ragged index top-k and sparse decode kernels at serving-sized batches: 60 random batches of 380–512 requests (1–8 query tokens each, up to 4K context, zero-length padding rows), reference-checked every 10th batch: all passed.

## End-to-end results 

MI325, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark` drafter with its default confidence head, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, FULL cudagraphs, default memory settings, `--max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 512`. Fixed vs adaptive verification on the same build.

GSM8K, full test set (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 64):

| Checkpoint | TP | Fixed | Adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` | 2 | 0.8196 | 0.8226 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` | 4 | 0.8779 | 0.8711 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` (BF16) | 8 | 0.8704 | 0.8688 |

Repeated MXFP8 runs vary by about ±0.01 for both modes (fixed 0.860–0.878 over 6 runs, adaptive 0.867–0.879 over 9 runs). One earlyadaptive MXFP8 run scored 0.801; it did not reproduce in 9 later runs and is still being investigated.

Sonnet 550 in / 150 out / 200 shared prefix, ignore EOS, output tok/s (adaptive gain vs fixed):

| Concurrency | MXFP4, TP=2 | MXFP8, TP=4 | BF16, TP=8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 649.96 → 674.59 (+3.8%) | 2241.79 → 2166.80 (−3.3%) | 3451.90 → 3327.16 (−3.6%) |
| 256 | 882.77 → 930.58 (+5.4%) | 2560.18 → 2605.40 (+1.8%) | 4005.66 → 4063.85 (+1.5%) |
| 320 | 965.59 → 1020.85 (+5.7%) | 2643.30 → 2733.47 (+3.4%) | 4099.15 → 4268.66 (+4.1%) |
| 380 | 1013.94 → 1071.63 (+5.7%) | 2686.83 → 2778.46 (+3.4%) | 4190.48 → crash (see below) |
| 420 | 1040.76 → 1102.05 (+5.9%) | 2713.55 → 2692.00 (−0.8%) | 4263.58 → crash |
| 500 | 1089.06 → 1146.61 (+5.3%) | fixed OOM → 1929.71 | 4228.05 → crash |

The gain shrinks as verification gets cheaper: TP=4 and TP=8 leave little verify cost for adaptive budgeting to save. MXFP8 fixed verification at concurrency 500 runs out of memory allocating the full verification logits (1.6 GB) at the default `--gpu-memory-utilization`; adaptive verification bounds that allocation and completes all requests.

### Known issue: BF16, TP=8, adaptive, concurrency ≥ 380

The adaptive BF16 server aborts with `HW Exception by GPU node-N ... reason: GPU Hang` under sustained load at concurrency 380–420 (reproduced twice; fixed verification is stable at the same load, MXFP4 TP=2 and MXFP8 TP=4 adaptive are stable through concurrency 500). The ragged MiniMax kernels pass the stress test above. Most likely root cause fix in #56831 - this is well-known issue at this point. Need to run TP=8 test with this PR applied).

## Earlier results (before rebase)

MXFP4 target with the `olka-fi/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-DSpark` drafter, TP=2, same Sonnet workload, 3–5 minute steady-state runs; 9,040 requests, none failed.

| Concurrency | Fixed tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | Fixed median TPOT | Adaptive median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 299.82 | 330.13 | +10.1% | 381.78 ms | 342.55 ms |
| 256 | 413.86 | 479.84 | +15.9% | 500.45 ms | 406.09 ms |
| 320 | 471.08 | 573.31 | +21.7% | 570.16 ms | 446.81 ms |
| 380 | 488.89 | 603.86 | +23.5% | 615.22 ms | 478.64 ms |
| 420 | 528.18 | 658.30 | +24.6% | 645.89 ms | 489.64 ms |
| 500 | 568.84 | 731.51 | +28.6% | 667.91 ms | 521.15 ms |

title: [Bug]: DSpark draft token count inflated by reusing target DP sync state with adaptive verification
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text commit id: ac71b175172f2c092d7141f41f0777b914788cfb ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With adaptive verification and DP enabled, DSpark reuses the target model’s DP sync state, whose `num_reqs` may reflect the target CUDA graph’s padded request capacity rather than the logical request count. This causes unnecessary padding in the draft batch. For example, a single request requiring 7 draft query tokens is expanded to 112 tokens when the target graph has a request capacity of 16. The drafter then selects and replays a 133-token CUDA graph. This issue appears to share the same root cause as #58984. * serve script ```text vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code \ --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[16,32,64,128,256,512],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":512}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` * profiling result ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid target request padding in DP drafter
body:
## Purpose

When a target FULL CUDA graph pads its request count, `DPSyncState.num_reqs` describes graph capacity rather than the number of scheduled requests. Reusing that capacity for uniform drafter steps makes active DP ranks select larger draft graphs than needed.

This PR keeps the DP-wide maximum real request count alongside graph capacity and uses it for uniform drafter dispatch. It also shrinks online dummy-rank DFlash batches coherently across input preparation, graph dispatch, attention metadata, EPLB preparation, and draft generation. Startup graph capture retains its required capacity.

## Test Plan & Result

The performance validation below uses the official nightly build at the PR base. This PR uses the same nightly plus only the four Python files changed by this PR; the runtime SHA-256 values were verified after the overlay was applied.

### GPU environment

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- Hardware: two non-production nodes, one arm per node, with 8x NVIDIA H20 96GB per arm.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`
- Baseline: the official nightly without a source change.

### vLLM Startup Command

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8010 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[16,32,64,128,256,512]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Performance Test

```bash
# Concurrency 64 example.
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8010 \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 3500 \
  --random-output-len 1500 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 640 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --seed 42 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --extra-body '{"seed":42}' \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 64 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed
```

All 890 requests completed in each arm without failures or Pod restarts.

Each point uses `num-prompts = 10 * concurrency`, random input 3500, output 1500, and seed 42. Both arms receive byte-identical input and output token arrays at each point.

| Concurrency | Output TPS Baseline -> This PR | Mean TPOT Baseline -> This PR | Acceptance Baseline -> This PR | Mean TTFT Baseline -> This PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 84.42 -> 86.09 (+1.98%) | 11.32 -> 11.15 ms (-1.57%) | 94.22% -> 85.63% (-8.58pp) | 795.0 -> 716.5 ms (-9.88%) |
| 8 | 471.97 -> 539.51 (+14.31%) | 15.23 -> 13.72 ms (-9.94%) | 84.54% -> 88.38% (+3.84pp) | 1339.1 -> 1271.8 ms (-5.02%) |
| 16 | 775.13 -> 842.71 (+8.72%) | 18.71 -> 17.01 ms (-9.06%) | 80.29% -> 82.97% (+2.68pp) | 1179.1 -> 1089.1 ms (-7.63%) |
| 64 | 1341.96 -> 1356.23 (+1.06%) | 44.55 -> 43.89 ms (-1.47%) | 81.09% -> 76.13% (-4.97pp) | 2306.4 -> 2371.9 ms (+2.84%) |

Acceptance varies between the two arms, but This PR improves output throughput and mean TPOT at every measured concurrency. This consistent end-to-end benefit across C1/C8/C16/C64 supports the optimization in this PR.

### GSM8K Test

Both arms were evaluated simultaneously with EvalScope 1.9.1 using the full 1319-sample zero-shot GSM8K test split and identical generation parameters.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":0}}' \
  --eval-batch-size 8 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95,"max_tokens":8192,"timeout":3600,"seed":0,"reasoning_effort":"high"}' \
  --work-dir ./gsm8k-results \
  --no-timestamp
```

- Baseline: 1270/1319 (96.29%).
- This PR: 1264/1319 (95.83%).
- Paired outcomes: 1257 both correct, 13 baseline-only correct, 7 This PR-only correct, and 42 both wrong.
- Exact two-sided McNemar test: `p=0.26318`; no statistically significant difference.
- API errors: zero in both arms. Baseline had three and This PR had five outputs reach the 8192-token limit.
- EvalScope performance: mean latency 7.58 -> 7.13 s (-5.90%); average output throughput 52.17 -> 56.16 tok/s (+7.65%).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to instrument the DP drafter path, identify the online dummy-rank graph mismatch, implement the follow-up optimization, run GPU validation, and summarize the results.

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4.1: Restore CUDA VL expert remapping and recording
body:
## Motivation

Vision-enabled DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints route text-only requests through CUDA `vision_topk()` too. Outside MegaMoE, that path skips ordinary TopK finalization: expert-distribution counts stay empty and nonidentity EPLB placement does not reach the physical-expert dispatch boundary.

Fixes #42188.

## Modifications

- Keep device-side, per-token text/image correction-bias selection and finalize CUDA VL routes through ordinary TopK's capture, expert mapping, shared-slot and recorder path.
- Pass existing expert-location dispatch information through both normal and dual-stream DeepSeek MoE call sites.
- Retain fused packed output when finalization preserves its IDs and weights; use the standard unpacked result after remapping.
- Mask padding after shared-slot rewrites. Preserve the existing non-CUDA and MegaMoE behavior.

No modality-admission synchronization, public option or dependency is added.

## Accuracy Tests

Head: `1c598de9d1757973d74d02b1360cda328b3f152e`, based on `e5dc10e73b0c4ccae7a9c4f454411b399e83a4f0`.

The validation below was completed before the test-only deletion commit `1c598de9d1`. That commit removes the new VL routing regression file; both runtime implementation files remain byte-identical to the validated `b1ce87b364` revision. This PR now contains only the two implementation files.

The removed H200 regression had 7 passing methods at `b1ce87b364`. On unmodified `6fe630ae14`, it produces 12 failing subtests and one error. It covers real per-layer counting, text/image bias selection, nonidentity static/dynamic expert mapping, packed output, shared scaling and per-rank slots, padding, empty rows, CUDA graph input refresh, and both actual MoE entry points with a small numerical expert boundary. Existing MegaMoE regressions (2) and CPU multimodal graph regressions (2) also pass.

Matched checkpoint A/B: `6fe630ae14` versus `3860e0f414`, 8xH200, TP8/EP4/DP1, local DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 snapshot, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1. The implementation and validation test were byte-identical after rebasing to `b1ce87b364`; the test file is removed in the current head. A full 5,749-file Python-tree audit finds only the two intended implementation files differ between the A/B arms.

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text/image-color/OCR functional requests | 19/19 | 19/19 |
| Logical expert-count total, each of 3 rounds | 0 | 5,222,400 |
| Official sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K | 1282/1319 (97.19%) | 1281/1319 (97.12%) |
| GSM8K errors / truncations | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Recorder rounds use 32 requests x 64 output tokens. Every one of 40 layers records 130,560 selections, matching `32 * (22 + 64 - 1) * top6 * 8 replicated ranks` under the existing stat-reduction convention. Both dump replicas agree and are not summed together. GSM8K uses temperature 0, seed 0, C32, max 2048 tokens, thinking off; 1315/1319 parsed answers agree, with two baseline-only and one candidate-only correct results. This is a finite task evaluation, not exact output equivalence.

Real attention-DP2 validation requires the existing padding fixes from [#40424](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40424), adapted in a separate validation copy. Unpatched main reaches that PR's `Repeat.cu` padded-row assertion during startup; the unchanged helper reproduces it on H200 with crash-safe input dumps. Those dependency fixes are outside this PR.

With that explicit dependency, TP8/EP4/attention-DP2 eager and BCG each pass 49/49 requests: text -> mixed text/image -> text, plus an idle peer. During the mixed phase, requests are directed to text-only DP0 and image-bearing DP1; scheduler logs confirm the routing. The only prefill graph bucket is 256 tokens. Actual graph-pass deltas are 15/14/15, including six image-bearing DP1 passes. All 48 paired answers agree ignoring three color-word capitalization differences. Both DP2 arms disable decoder bounded replay, which currently rejects attention TP4/DP2.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same fixed-source TP8/EP4/DP1 A/B: speculation and HiCache off, context 65536, memory fraction 0.70, chunked prefill 2048. Each run uses 128 requests, C32, exactly 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, seed 42, 16 warmup requests and a cache flush. Every measured request succeeds with the stated token lengths.

| Output tok/s | Baseline run 1 | Baseline run 2 | Candidate run 1 | Candidate run 2 | Mean change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Default recorder disabled | 1003.57 | 1004.94 | 999.68 | 999.28 | -0.48% |
| `stat` recorder configured | 997.18 | 1003.45 | 978.80 | 978.39 | -2.17% |

The stat configuration captures the ordinary recorder work restored by this fix, including after recording is stopped between diagnostic rounds. Its measured cost is reported separately from default serving.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Provide checkpoint accuracy, recorder and speed evidence.
- [x] Validate actual DP2 eager/BCG behavior with the explicit existing padding-fix dependency.
- [x] Validation revision `b1ce87b364` [Lint passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39100619572).
- [ ] Upstream GPU CI and required maintainer approvals.

The previous GPU workflow attempts stopped at the draft gate and did not execute tests. Maintainer `run-ci` approval is still needed.

Motivation
Enable candidate-only indexer scoring on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4.1, following
#40574
.
The current protocol already publishes compact candidate block IDs, but Hopper consumers still traverse the full logical score space before selecting among the candidates. This PR uses those block IDs during scoring, so consumers produce compact scores directly instead of a context-width score matrix.
The Triton implementation reads candidate K positions directly, avoiding a per-query

K tensor.

/

interfaces.

add
fp4_index_logits_candidates

title: [Tracking] GLM-5.3-Flash performance optimization on Hopper (SM90)
body:
<!-- Title: [Tracking] GLM-5.3-Flash performance optimization on Hopper (SM90) -->

This issue tracks performance work for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA Hopper (SM90) GPUs.

This list is part of the Q4 roadmap #42473 (Kernel optimization, PoC: @BBuf). Related: SM120 tracking #37813, GLM-5.3-Flash bug tracking #37524.

## DSA attention and indexer

- [x] Q8KV8 FP8 sparse prefill on GLM-5.3-Flash with BF16 KV cache — #41790
- [x] Support TileLang FP8 KV cache on CUDA — #42957
- [x] k-pool: 256-token logical page so index page id = logical page id — #42178
- [ ] Support the flashmla_sparse_q8 prefill backend on CUDA — #44217
- [ ] Unify the q8kv8 sparse-prefill topk_length source with the BF16 path — #36305
- [ ] Pick any divisor of the tile count for the TileLang sparse decode split — #45274
- [ ] Split top-k across CTAs for small CUDA BF16 TileLang sparse decode — #43917
- [ ] Support group-scaled FP8 NoPE KV reads for CUDA TileLang — #39349
- [ ] Add GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 KV cache on SM90 with FA3 — #45072

## KDA (linear attention)

- [x] Fuse GLM-5.3-Flash KDA projections and prefill metadata — #39688
- [x] Support ReplaySSM ring-write in the fused chain-verify kernel — #36821
- [x] Support Helion MTP verification and harden prefill, decode — #42857
- [ ] Extend the CuTe DSL MTP verify kernel to SM90 — #44612
- [ ] Defer accepted-state materialization for SM90 Triton verify — #39025
- [ ] Make KDA backend dispatch hardware- and shape-aware — #37901
- [ ] Run the KDA projection GEMMs in FP8 on SM90, extending [#38764](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38764) and [#44629](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44629) @JackChuang

## MoE and communication

- [x] Extend FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE autotune coverage to prefill chunks — #43363
- [x] Add H20 block-FP8 MoE configs for GLM-5.3-Flash EP4/EP8 — #38913
- [x] Support GLM-5.3-Flash with DeepEP v2 — #40466
- [ ] Add H20 fused_moe configs for GLM-5.3-Flash TP8/TP4 — #45089

## Speculative decoding (MTP / DFlash)

- [ ] Skip the per-rank eager-draft fallback for a missing DSA seed under DP attention — #41269
- [ ] Register the NextN draft's DSA index cache for hybrid linear-attention pools — #41334
- [ ] Allow PP + EAGLE/NEXTN prefill for Glm5Next — #41335
- [ ] Gather DFlash aux hidden states for every scattered MoE all-to-all backend @JackChuang
- [ ] Fill the MTP draft KV without attention for all but the last prompt token after prefill @JackChuang

## CUDA graph

- [ ] Init persistent cache for breaking modules in prefill breakable graph — #43776
- [ ] Enable breakable prefill CUDA graphs for GLM-5.3-Flash with prefill context parallel — #44293

## Fixes

- [ ] Pad the TileLang sparse MLA prefill output back to the padded extend batch — #44262
- [ ] Fix the TileLang FP8 sparse decode crash with NoPE (d_tail=0) — #40301
- [ ] Reject unsupported k-pool backends early — #41898
- [ ] transform_index: support non-2048 top-k widths and guard out-of-range indices — #39431
- [ ] Fix MoE padding handling in hybrid MTP verification — #43271
- [ ] Pad hybrid target verify to complete request groups — #37587
- [ ] Match KPool draft-extend writes to precomputed plans — #37588
- [ ] Size decode Mamba spec-state scratch by running batch, not decode extra slots — #44015

title: [Feat] [NPU] kimi-k3: Support DCP with shared compact communication
body: ## Motivation Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Kimi-K3 on Ascend NPU, including DSPARK speculative decoding. Shard target-model MLA KV cache across DCP ranks to reduce per-rank KV storage for a given logical context capacity. ## Modifications - Add sharded MLA KV allocation, reads, and writes while preserving the scheduler's logical token address space. Reuse the shared DCP-aware Triton KV writer, prefix-index builder, and page-table kernel. - Share the MLA DCP page-table fill entry between TRTLLM/CuteDSL and Ascend, preserving backend-specific launch parameters, optional virtual-to-physical translation, and caller-owned graph buffers. - Adapt Ascend FIA to rank-local KV pages, sequence lengths, and causal masks for decode and DSPARK target verification. Gather sharded prefix KV when needed for prefill/extend. - Reuse Q AllGather and compact DCP AllToAll with BF16/FP16 partial outputs and FP32 LSE, followed by the shared Triton LSE merge. Handle empty KV shards safely. - Integrate local metadata and sequence-length updates with NPUGraph capture/replay. Supported scope: Kimi-K3 MLA with FP16/BF16 KV cache and non-NZ FIA V1. Speculative decoding supports DSPARK with static verification; mixed-chunk execution and replicated Q projection are not supported. ## Run #!/usr/bin/env bash set -eo pipefail CODE_PATH=XXX title: [Refactor] moe: Derive routing inputs from the layer and active forward
body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* __->__ #44994
* #44993
* #44991
* #44480

## Motivation

Model forwards can omit expert placement or the live token count, routing logical IDs against physical expert weights or processing padding as real tokens. Move those decisions into TopK and the active forward. Automatic padding also makes inactive routes reachable at EP1, so every affected consumer must skip their data, weights and expert addresses safely.

## Modifications

- Resolve placement per call and capture draft identity during construction. Align draft weight loading with identity routing, including in-range draft layer IDs; retain target placement-aware loading.
- Bind the prepared ForwardBatch across eager execution, graph capture/replay, CPU graphs and TBO children. Bind copied row/tail batches too. Decline DeepSeek row-tail capture when its MoE count is a separate GLOBAL buffer, using the existing eager path.
- Preserve lazy routing metadata until materialization. Keep the producing layer ID in TopKConfig, including piecewise reconstruction, so lazy LP conversion defaults to the correct solver while explicit overrides (including 0) still win. Keep the existing five-field tuple ABI. Reject logits-only consumers that cannot apply required remapping. Route DeepSeek graph admission through the same layer contract. Keep shared expert columns outside LP solving and routed-only remapping.
- Make Triton, Marlin, GGUF, W4AFP8 and Humming consumers honor inactive routes independently of EP, including NaN inputs/weights and poisoned intermediate buffers. Generic Marlin reuses its projection allocation, clearing the down view after activation consumes the up view; LoRA retains separate zeroed buffers.
- Support the published `sglang-kernel==0.4.10` GGUF provider with Python block-size selection, safe vector indices, masked inactive intermediates/contributions, and initialized MMQ slack metadata. Retain the AOT source fixes for future wheel builds.
- Initialize CUTLASS FP8 gather maps and use a masked Triton reduction that skips inactive data and weights. Pass token count and supported weight strides at runtime without value specialization so new lengths reuse compiled kernels. This fixes both block-FP8 and MXFP8 without requiring a newly released AOT wheel.
- Reject LongCat zero-expert placement configurations at startup, since routed-only placement tables cannot represent its identity experts safely. Plain identity placement remains available.
- Assert the Marlin allocation property rather than an incidental `.zero_()` call; set its CI runtime estimate to 720 seconds to cover cold compilation.

## CI repairs and validation

Current head: `2447ebc8cd21ba19ceb5f94c67826d30ff4aeaa0`; base #44993 is `4275a5026050615139c3658a72b6a7d05d65b17f`. Updated by normal fast-forward pushes.

Two latest repairs:

- Shared-expert routing fixture: publishing TP=1 and then overriding EP=8 failed topology validation before routing. Supply a consistent virtual TP=EP=8 topology at rank 3, without process groups or collectives. Registration and numerical assertions are unchanged. On one NVIDIA H200, the original complete file produced seven topology subtest errors; the repaired file passed all four tests at both stack production revisions, including five CUDA router variants, shared contribution and fullgraph compile behavior.
- AMD AITER prefill: eager draft extend selected a new query-offset table in `ForwardMetadata`, while CK still received the backend's stale prompt table. Measured Q had 80 rows but the passed offsets reached 4,648, immediately followed by the GPU memory fault. Publish ordinary prefill offsets into the same metadata owner and consume that owner's view in CK, ASM and 5D prefill. Kernel selection, KV padding and speculative helpers are unchanged. [#40872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40872) describes the same defect with a producer-side repair; this patch keeps the existing per-forward owner authoritative at consumers.

AMD before/after: the unchanged EAGLE canary failed with a memory fault on both this stack and its original main base. After repair, all 20 requests and original assertions passed (50.6s process). A second serialized observation run passed too: CK received `[0,4,...,80]`, all 588 eager CK calls returned, and no malformed query CSR or HSA fault was observed. Decode graphs and all test assertions remained enabled as configured. Hardware: one AMD MI350X; original CI used MI300. Torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, AITER 2bb549102, CK 96afae1d5. NHD/BF16 is exercised; the corresponding 5D/FP8/ASM corrections have source review coverage. Final source differs from the tested repair only by removing a stale comment. Independent source review and configured pre-commit checks passed.

H200 fixture runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18. This is single-GPU routing validation, not eight-GPU collective or full-model validation.

Other failures in the latest CI run:

- JIT B200 failed before tests: its local wheel was truncated to 94 MiB and lacked a ZIP central directory. A sibling verified the same artifact and installed its full 356 MiB wheel successfully (4,821 tests passed). A clean artifact download/retry is needed; no retry was triggered here.
- Qwen3-Next FP8 HiCache multi-turn KL exceeded its unchanged threshold. The same production code passed this method in the preceding run. The local numerical A/B ran zero comparisons: its Rust cache extension could not build against Torch 2.14.1. No version-check bypass was applied. This failure remains unattributed; no numerical fix or passing baseline is claimed.
- AMD disaggregation failed at startup with HIP OOM, also seen in an earlier main run. The AITER query-offset fix addresses the separately reproduced EAGLE memory fault, and does not claim to fix this startup failure.
- NPU QwenImage has identical failing metrics in three unrelated PR runs with the same expected image. A scoped source audit found no changed numerical path from this MoE stack, but no bare-base NPU A/B was run and its root cause remains unresolved.

Earlier CI-only repairs at `0a3e1cfa68` remain included: inherited DeepSeek dual-stream fixture correction from #44993, current activation import, Bailing NextN/V3 parity ownership, and Python 3.11 wheel selection in the simulator job. Their recorded validation was 54 quantization tests, 85 kernel namespace tests, the complete DeepSeek opcheck/compile/graph-replay test at both production revisions, two parity tests, 49 fusion-gate tests plus 11 subtests, and artifact-name matching. Those checks were not rerun for these bounded changes. Full CI and full-model acceptance remain pending; earlier validation below stays tied to its named revisions.

## Earlier validation after rebase

Head: `5a0a941ff3013d5c98cff1a5854d03bebff7324c`. Rebased onto main `553836c1647b3bfbeb266b49d76ec2c9df012425`; base `cheng/refactor/moe-layer-backend-semantics` is `fc2dd3d90bf86fe1b61741c1bb8d28a4e121dc8a`.

- At this exact head, 6 focused CPU module(s) passed: 66 tests plus 115 reported subtests. Across all four PR heads, 15 focused modules completed 482 test executions plus 347 reported subtests, all passing.
- Each PR's full incremental tree matches the pre-rebase change applied to its rewritten base, retaining prior merge-only integration fixes. The stack remains #44480 -> #44991 -> #44993 -> #44994.
- Configured pre-commit checks passed over all 152 changed files in the full stack. Strict registration/entrypoint checks passed: 2,478 files / 3,012 registrations. CPU tests used Python 3.12.15 and Torch 2.14.1+cu130 with GPUs hidden.

GPU, full-model accuracy/throughput and full CI were not rerun for this rebase. Prior hardware measurements below remain evidence for their named earlier revisions; checked CUTLASS/Marlin/GGUF consumer sources are unchanged, which is source evidence rather than a new GPU run.

## Previous validation (before rebase)

Previous head: `068e12b7c155babfdc6eea074812b12c7830a3df`, including #44993 at `b37b73a1ae1bdf3d73b6108deb76a14679a079b4`, all lower PRs, and main `693d33330647c57f82e09ac39a34122fa46b5763`.

- At this exact integrated head, 12 focused CPU modules passed: 119 tests plus 200 reported subtests. Coverage includes lazy LP ownership, routing metadata/graph bounds, dispatcher contracts, shared/routed scale, native model policy admission, ModelOpt/FP8 ownership, runner extensions and placement. The lower PR was also checked independently. New regressions fail against their pre-fix production sources for the intended conditions.
- All 3 CUTLASS FP8 CUDA test methods passed on one NVIDIA B300, including real native block-FP8/MXFP8 GEMMs and mixed/all-inactive graph replay. The reduction test spans 12 token counts, contiguous/transposed weights, FP16/BF16 and poisoned NaN routes. The old real Triton cache grew to 23 entries per dtype; the fixed kernel retains 1. Tested kernel/test bytes are unchanged by the final merge.
- Native environment: Python 3.12.15, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and published `sglang-kernel 0.4.10`. Incompatible FlashInfer 0.7.1 cubin/cache packages were ignored; kernels compiled as needed.
- Configured hooks passed on all 11 files touched in this round. Strict registration/entrypoint checks pass: 2,472 files / 3,006 registrations.

Earlier validation at the preceding heads remains historical: 856 CPU tests across 43 modules with 7 skips, 18 native Marlin cases, 2 prior CUTLASS FP8 methods and 4 GGUF cases against the published 0.4.10 wheel. The new focused CPU and 3-method CUTLASS runs above replace the corresponding coverage for this revision; the Marlin/GGUF kernels are unchanged this round.

The earlier reduced Qwen3 TP4/EP4 reverse-placement graph smoke matched 72 generated IDs and logprobs at its recorded revision; it was not rerun as full-model validation here. No new all-valid reduction latency, dropped-block scan cost or serving throughput measurement is claimed. Native TRT-LLM selector parity, full-model accuracy, ROCm/NPU/AMX and external FlashInfer/HPC/KT consumer coverage remain unverified. Full CI has not been established for this head.

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] moe: Add a fused CUTLASS MXFP4A8 backend for SM90.
body:
## Motivation This PR adds an SGLang-native CUTLASS **MXFP4A8 fused MoE backend for SM90/Hopper**, targeting MXFP4-expert models such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The implementation keeps expert weights in MXFP4 (E2M1 with block-32 E8M0 scales), dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 E4M3, and executes both expert GEMMs on Hopper FP8 tensor cores. The current scope is deliberately limited to **TP deployments with EP=1**. `EP>1` is not supported by this PR and is rejected explicitly during weight initialization. ## Summary - Add an MXFP4-to-FP8 mixed-input CUTLASS path for SM90. - Add load-time Humming-compatible MXFP4 weight preprocessing. - Add an EP1 fused runtime covering routing metadata preparation, input permutation and quantization, GEMM1, SwiGLU, requantization, GEMM2, output permutation, router weighting, and top-k reduction. - Add shape-specialized SM90 schedulers for serving-time token buckets. - Preserve the existing INT4A8 path unchanged. - Add numerical tests for MXFP4 conversion, scale layouts, grouped GEMM, and cross-backend consistency against FlashInfer. The backend is selected with: ```bash --moe-runner-backend cutlass ``` ### Execution flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant X as BF16 input participant R as Top-k routing participant S as SGLang fused path participant F as FlashInfer participant W as MXFP4 weights participant Y as MoE output X->>R: tokens and topk=6 W-->>S: Humming-compatible view W-->>F: Humming view par SGLang EP1 path R->>S: GPU-built routing metadata S->>S: reorder + per-token FP8 quant S->>S: grouped GEMM1 S->>S: SwiGLU + FP8 requant S->>S: grouped GEMM2 S-->>Y: reorder + router-weight reduction and FlashInfer R->>F: topk IDs + router weights F->>F: bucketed tactic lookup F->>F: fused MoE body F-->>Y: fused finalize end Note over S,F: Same logical MXFP4 weights and routing inputs
Different runtime orchestration and scheduling ``` ## Implementation ### MXFP4A8 tensor-core path Weights remain in checkpoint-native MXFP4. Activations are quantized per token to FP8 E4M3. The E2M1 values `{0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6}` are exactly representable in E4M3, so the E2M1-to-E4M3 conversion uses a lossless signed-nibble lookup. The mixed-input mainloop derives the scale group from `TileK / PackedScalesNum`, allowing the existing INT4A8 group-128 path and the new MXFP4A8 group-32 path to share the same mainloop without changing INT4 behavior. ### Load-time weight preprocessing The EP1 path prepares one runtime representation after checkpoint loading: - interleaved MXFP4 weights; - folded E8M0 offsets; - one residual scale per expert. The representation follows the SM90 Humming preprocessing semantics. Runtime execution is implemented by SGLang AOT kernels. Only the fused representation is retained for EP1 to avoid storing two complete weight layouts on H20. ### Fused EP1 execution `cutlass_mxfp4a8_fused_moe_core` performs: 1. expert-offset, problem-size, and permutation preparation; 2. routed-input reorder and per-token FP8 quantization; 3. grouped GEMM1; 4. fused SwiGLU, optional clamp, and FP8 requantization; 5. grouped GEMM2; 6. output reorder, FP32 router-weight multiplication, `routed_scaling_factor`, and top-k reduction. For `M <= 64`, metadata preparation and shuffled input quantization use a bounded fused CUDA path. Larger batches use the AOT metadata and quantization kernels without host synchronization. Intermediate tensors are retained in reusable workspaces. ### SM90 scheduling The implementation includes: - a persistent single-warpgroup ping-pong kernel for tiny and arbitrary serving-time shapes; - a precomputed grouped scheduler with prebuilt TMA descriptors for validated large-M buckets; - a packed warp-shuffle GEMM2 epilogue. | Tokens | GEMM1 config | GEMM2 config | |---:|---:|---:| | `M <= 64` | 100 | 100 | | `M = 2048` | 313 | 313 | | `M = 4096` | 320 | 334 | | `M >= 8192` | 322 | 334 | | Other shapes | 101 | 101 | ## Validation ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash end-to-end A/B Hardware and runtime: - 8x NVIDIA H20; - native DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint; - TP8 / EP1; - FP8 KV cache and DSV4 attention; - separate fresh containers for the two backends; - identical package versions except for the locally built `sglang-kernel` wheel; - FlashInfer 0.6.18 W4A8 as the upstream baseline. Serving workload: - exact paired token-ID prompts; - 128 requests; - concurrency 32; - output length 1536; - repeat 1. | Input -> output | CUTLASS output tok/s | FlashInfer output tok/s | Throughput | Mean TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8192 -> 1536 | 1399.19 | 1247.18 | **+12.19%** | **-17.26%** | | 16384 -> 1536 | 933.52 | 814.49 | **+14.61%** | **-16.95%** | | 32768 -> 1536 | 541.48 | 466.34 | **+16.11%** | **-16.18%** | All 384 requests completed successfully. Neither server log contained a CUDA error, OOM, or traceback. ### GSM8K The complete 1319-question GSM8K set was evaluated with five fixed shots, temperature 0, 32 threads, and repeat 1. | Backend | Correct | Accuracy | |---|---:|---:| | CUTLASS MXFP4A8 | 1252 / 1319 | 94.9204% | | FlashInfer | 1246 / 1319 | 94.4655% | The paired discordance was 16 CUTLASS-only correct versus 10 Humming-only correct (exact McNemar `p=0.3269`). This run does not establish a statistically significant accuracy difference. ### Kernel and operator tests | Test suite | Result | |---|---:| | CUTLASS MXFP4 grouped GEMM | 11 passed | | CUTLASS vs FlashInfer fused MoE | 3 passed | | Existing INT4 grouped GEMM | 605 passed | | Focused DSV4 norm/RoPE | 16 passed | The cross-backend test generates one logical MXFP4 weight set and uses the same BF16 input, top-k IDs, and router weights for both implementations. It covers `M=1`, `M=16`, and `M=65` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash `topk=6`, and requires: - normalized L2 error `< 2.5%`; - cosine similarity `> 0.9995`. ## Limitations - Supported hardware: SM90/Hopper. - Supported expert-parallel configuration: **EP=1 only**. - `EP>1` is explicitly rejected; this PR does not claim a legacy or DeepEP fallback. - Hidden size must be divisible by 128; intermediate size must be divisible by 32 and may be padded for validated GEMM shapes. - The load-time representation reuses FlashInfer's SM90 preprocessing semantics; runtime execution uses SGLang AOT kernels. - The reported performance results are specific to DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 8x H20 with the configuration above. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with the repository pre-commit configuration. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Validate MXFP4, INT4, and DSV4 regressions. - [x] Provide complete GSM8K accuracy results. - [x] Provide paired end-to-end performance results against current upstream FlashInfer. - [ ] Add user-facing documentation if maintainers request it. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39389973536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973536) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39389973468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973468) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39389973442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39389973442)

Description
hit-zhengbao

Issue body actions
We are evaluating an MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 GEMM on NVIDIA H100.
The fused-E8M0 Humming kernel is numerically correct, but with group-32
MXFP8 activation scales it is significantly slower than both:
Humming's generic group-scale path
A QDQ baseline that dequantizes both operands and then runs a BF16 GEMM
We would like to ask whether group-32 MXFP8 input scaling is an intended
performance target and whether there are plans to optimize this case on Hopper.
Quantization format
The operands use the following format:
Activation payload: FP8 E4M3
Activation scale: per-token, per-K-group power-of-two scale
Activation group size: 32
Weight payload: MXFP4 E2M1
Weight scale: E8M0
Weight group size: 32
Output dtype: BF16
This is an MXFP8-style activation representation: each 32-element K group
contains an E4M3 payload and one power-of-two scale.
Humming receives the decoded real FP32 activation scales through
input_scale
. The original activation scales are exactly representable
as E8M0 powers of two.
This differs from the DeepEP grouped-FP8 case added by
#37
:
PR
fix: support grouped FP8 MXFP4
#37
activation group size: 128
This case activation group size: 32
Both cases use MXFP4 weights with E8M0 group size 32
Environment
GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
Humming commit tested:
79c1cef
/
#35
Output dtype: BF16
Warmup: 20 iterations
Measurement: 200 iterations
Timing: CUDA events and CUDA Graph replay
GEMM operation count:
2 * M * N * K
PR
#37
was merged after the tested commit. Based on its diff, it adds the
group-128 integration and fixes non-fused scale tail decoding, but does
not appear to change fused WGMMA accumulator scheduling or the H100
heuristics. We can confirm the measurements on the latest main if needed.
Humming configuration
The fused kernel is configured approximately as follows:

used by

.

.
Correctness
The following implementations were compared against an FP32 reference:
Fused-E8M0 Humming
Generic Humming group-scale path
QDQ followed by BF16 GEMM
All tested correctness cases passed.
QDQ baseline
The QDQ latency includes activation dequantization, weight dequantization,
and the BF16 GEMM. It is not a GEMM-only baseline.

For large-M shapes, the fused kernel reaches only approximately
20-22 effective TFLOPS.
Suspected bottleneck
Our current understanding is:
For FP8,
kPartMmaShapeK
is 32.
With
input_scale_group_size=32
, every WGMMA step reaches an activation
scale boundary.
scale_d
is therefore false at every K=32 step.
The current path performs
wgmma_commit()
followed by
wgmma_wait<0>()
, register fencing, and accumulator scaling for every
K=32 group.
The fused H100 heuristic selects a relatively large
128x128x128
base tile, which may increase the cost of processing the accumulator
at each group boundary.
With the group-128 input scales used by PR
#37
, four K=32 WGMMA operations
can accumulate before applying the activation scale. The synchronization
and accumulator-processing overhead can therefore be better amortized.
This is only our interpretation of the current implementation; please
correct us if we are missing another bottleneck.
Comparison with an experimental Gluon implementation
For reference, an experimental Gluon implementation reaches approximately
580-665 effective TFLOPS for the same large-M shapes.
That implementation performs one-time offline preprocessing of the static
MXFP4 weight into a cached FP8 weight tensor and therefore consumes an
additional
N * K
bytes of device memory. It is not a direct memory-footprint
comparison with Humming's packed-MXFP4 kernel, but it suggests that the
group-32 activation scaling itself does not necessarily prevent high
throughput if preprocessing extra static weight storage is acceptable.
We do not expect the packed-MXFP4 Humming kernel to match this result
without considering that memory tradeoff.
Questions
Is MXFP8 activation group size 32 an intended performance target for
Humming's fused-E8M0 W4A8 kernel?
Is the current implementation primarily optimized for group-128 input
scales such as the DeepEP format in PR
fix: support grouped FP8 MXFP4
#37
?
Are there plans to optimize the group-32 case on Hopper?
Would you recommend a different block/warp shape or disabling stream-K
for this workload?
Could an accumulator ring, delayed retirement, or another scheduling
strategy reduce the per-group
wgmma_wait<0>
overhead?
Would it be useful for us to provide the complete benchmark script,
Nsight Compute reports, or results from additional shapes?
Thank you.

Hi，the attachment contains the source code.
Core Kernels
1. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_accs_kernel
Processes one 32-element K group at a time:
WGMMA(A_fp8, W_fp8) -> FP32 partial
partial *= input_e8m0_scale
master += partial
This is the key to preserving numerical accuracy: the activation scale is applied to the FP32 partial accumulator, avoiding an additional rounding step from dequantizing and casting the activation back to FP8.
2. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_accs_batched_kernel
Loads multiple 32-element K groups in each TMA stage, typically using LOAD_K=128 or LOAD_K=256. This reduces TMA transactions, barrier overhead, and main-loop scheduling costs. It is the default high-performance path for large M.
3. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_splitk_kernel
Used for small M. It increases parallelism by distributing the K dimension across multiple CTAs. Each CTA accumulates into an FP32 temporary output using atomic additions, after which the result is converted to the requested output dtype.
4. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_prmt_kernel
A fallback path used when the WPREQ exactness guard fails. It uses prmt.b32 to fuse the decoding of packed MXFP4 weights with their weight scales into FP8 values. This path requires an offline T2 weight repacking step.
5. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_kernel
The most general but slower fallback path. It explicitly performs MXFP4 decoding, E8M0 scale application, and FP8 conversion inside the main loop.

Thank you. I manually performed some temporary local tuning and achieved only 500+ TFLOPs, which is lower than gluon. This is mainly because Humming's current implementation is not friendly to groupwise input scaling; a major optimization would require reimplementing a separate WGMMA path.
Additionally, I noticed a few issues with your code:
For the kernels under small batch sizes, you dequantize the input, multiply by the scale, and then quantize back to FP8. This is likely to cause serious precision problems, especially when the actual FP16 input values are very small (e.g., on the order of 0.001).
For the benchmarking script, you use CUDA Graphs. This may inflate the performance numbers for small batch sizes because the L2 cache is not flushed. I suggest using DeepGEMM's testing script instead.

title: Minimizing Information Leakage under Padding Constraints
body:
An attacker can gain information of a user by analyzing its network traffic.
The size of transferred data leaks information about the file being transferred
or the service being used, and this is particularly revealing when the attacker
has background knowledge about the files or services available for transfer. To
prevent this, servers may pad their files using a padding scheme, changing the
file sizes and preventing anyone from guessing their identity uniquely. This
work focuses on finding optimal padding schemes that keep a balance between
privacy and the costs of bandwidth increase. We consider R\'enyi-min leakage as
our main measure for privacy, since it is directly related with the success of
a simple attacker, and compare our algorithms with an existing solution that
minimizes Shannon leakage. We provide improvements to our algorithms in order
to optimize average total padding and Shannon leakage while minimizing
R\'enyi-min leakage. Moreover, our algorithms are designed to handle a more
general and important scenario in which multiple servers wish to compute
padding schemes in a way that protects the servers' identity in addition to the
identity of the files.

title: Beyond Parallel Blindness: Information Floors and Model Gaps in Block Drafting
body: Block drafters propose several tokens in one forward pass, before earlier target tokens are realised. Their rejection mixes two losses: missing within-block path information and imperfect modelling of observable information. Accepted length cannot distinguish them. We separate the two with an information floor, the minimum expected rejection at a specified conditioning order; rejection above this floor is the model gap. Estimating both from target rollouts across four domains, four open-weight targets, and a frontier API target yields three findings. First, the all-parallel floor reaches 0.286 at the final slot on Qwen3-4B, limiting even the best proposal to 71% per-slot acceptance. Second, one realised token removes 86--100% of this floor, a locality also recovered by an independent mutual-information analysis. Third, current drafters remain far above their floors: the final-slot model gap accounts for 43--64% of DFlash rejection and 85--92% of DSpark's oracle-conditioned rejection. These findings separate the value of short-range conditioning from proposal quality. Guided by this distinction, we replace a context-independent predecessor correction with a prefix-attention head that reads committed context conditional on the predecessor. With supporting backbone components, the resulting Qwen3-4B drafter improves mean serving accepted length by 3.83% over the released DSpark checkpoint across nine tasks, without increasing the conditioning order.

title: VIA-SD: Verification via Intra-Model Routing for Speculative Decoding
body: Speculative decoding (SD) addresses the high inference costs of LLMs by having lightweight drafters generate candidates for large verifiers to validate in parallel. Existing draft-verify methods use binary decisions: accept or fully recompute. Yet we find that many rejected tokens can be verified correctly by a slim submodel derived from the full verifier via intra-model routing, instead of the full verifier. This motivates our slim-verifier to handle tokens requiring moderate verification resources, reducing expensive large-model calls. We propose Verification via Intra-Model Routing for Speculative Decoding (VIA-SD), a multi-tier framework using a routed slim-verifier. Draft tokens are processed hierarchically: direct acceptance for high-confidence cases, slim-verifier regeneration for medium-confidence cases, and full-model verification for uncertain cases. Across four representative tasks and multiple model families, VIA-SD reduces rejection rates by 0.10-0.22 and delivers 10-20% speedups over strong SD baselines, while achieving 2.5-3x acceleration over non-drafting decoding. Moreover, VIA-SD is compatible with existing SD frameworks without modifying their training procedures. Our results suggest multi-tier SD as a general paradigm for scalable and efficient LLM inference. Project page: https://zju-xyc.github.io/VIA-SD-Project-Page/

title: Add Kimi K3 B300 EFA AgentX sweep / 新增 Kimi K3 B300 EFA AgentX 扫描
body:
**Host freezes: trigger isolated to degraded EFA devices on long-running nodes.** A standalone Mooncake-over-EFA reproducer (no vLLM or NIXL; production store config: 8 ranks/node, 160 GB THP segments, GPU buffer registered with EFA) froze every node that had run since Oct 6-14 (3/3, within 30 s to 5 min of traffic) and none of the rebooted nodes (0/7), with either the CUDA VMM or the `cudaMalloc` allocator; a sweep job also froze node 09. Every long-running node checked reports `reg_mr_err=46` on each EFA device from earlier registration failures; rebooted nodes report none, and the current workload creates none. Those nodes are excluded until operators reboot them, and the setup script refuses any node whose EFA devices report failed registrations. Disaggregated jobs no longer requeue (one hung job previously moved across four node sets). The disaggregated workers also drop `enable-cumem-allocator` and set `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`, since Mooncake moved ~2 GB/s per rank into VMM buffers versus 14-27 GB/s into `cudaMalloc` buffers on healthy nodes. The setup script installs the pinned `aiconfigurator-core` wheel, verified against its published SHA256, before Dynamo's source install pulls its intermittently failing placeholder package.

Bring the Kimi K3 DSpark AgentX search space from #4047 to B300: ten DCP disaggregated points and three low-latency aggregate points, with one eight-GPU node per DCP8 worker.

Use EFA for NIXL and Mooncake, preserving the model, concurrency matrix, golden acceptance selection and eval coverage. The setup builds a pinned THP-enabled Mooncake client with host-chunk collapse and backports upstream libfabric CUDA VMM synchronization fixes. It also adds a default-on opt-out for vLLM's NVLink-only latent-MoE tail. These serving-stack changes require a patch waiver.

The two-node TP16 point uses stock decode and portable collectives, with custom allreduce, GEMM-AR and the fused latent-MoE tail disabled. These fused paths require GPU multicast across the TP group, which is unavailable across EFA-connected nodes. Single-node TP8 points retain their fused paths.

The [current sweep](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39258024329) has passed all three aggregate benchmarks and their tool-schema evals; **the full sweep is not yet green**. The 2P3D c192 job failed before serving because two workers downloaded an `aiconfigurator-core` wheel that failed its published SHA256 check; this is being treated as a transient installation failure pending retry, with no installer change or checksum bypass. The registration fix passes local full-model Dynamo prefill startup and fresh-image wheel validation at unchanged capacity; the public disaggregated path remains unverified. A scheduler exclusion avoids a node with a separately reproduced pre-container task-launch failure.

<details><summary>Validation details</summary>

Current-head results, with one-hour profiling submission windows and unchanged native result and power gates:

| Configuration | GPUs | Total TPS/GPU | P90 ITL | P90 TTFT | Valid profiled requests | Tool eval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8/DCP8 c2 | 8 | 2,681.25 | 3.43 ms | 1.32678 s | 417 | 403/408 |
| TP8/DCP8 c4 | 8 | 4,028.18 | 4.87 ms | 1.60057 s | 621 | 404/408 |
| TP16/DCP16 c1 | 16 | 568.12 | 12.83 ms | 1.88693 s | 177 | 401/408 |

All three power bundles report valid coverage and package integrity, with no validation failures. Native content validation excluded one, three and one profiling records, respectively. The c2 job also cancelled one outstanding request after its end-of-window grace deadline; it still passed the native gate. The TP16 runtime config confirms the portable fallback was used.

Tool eval residual failures concern generated tool calls or arguments, not API/backend rejection. These evals use no Mooncake connector and do not establish external-cache correctness. In an earlier [sweep](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39216083365), the same 1P2D GSM8K configuration completed with 97.35% strict-match accuracy over 1,319 questions.

A local DCP8 1P1D stability run completed one hour of AgentX profiling with 4,517 valid requests, zero profiling errors and successful result validation. It used real acceptance and is not a controlled performance comparison against the synthetic-acceptance sweep. The local TP16 checks establish serving functionality, not completed benchmark or accuracy validation.

The host-collapse fix passes an eight-client mixed-backing registration reproducer and full-model Dynamo prefill startup with all eight 160 GiB mappings fully huge-page-backed. A fresh-image build installed `0.3.13.post1+gc3fa13ec.collapse1`; its separate 8 GiB Store sanity check passed a 5,632-byte put/get. Cross-node 8 MiB GPU-to-host WRITE, host-to-GPU READ and GPU-to-GPU READ also passed with CUDA VMM enabled and aligned 8 GiB host regions. These local checks do not establish full disaggregated sweep completion.

</details>

<details><summary>中文</summary>

**主机冻结：触发条件定位为长时间运行节点上已退化的 EFA 设备。** 独立的 Mooncake-over-EFA 复现程序（不含 vLLM 和 NIXL，采用生产配置：每节点 8 个 rank、160 GB THP 段、GPU 缓冲区注册到 EFA）使所有自 10 月 6–14 日以来未重启的节点冻结（3/3，流量开始后 30 秒至 5 分钟），而重启过的节点均未冻结（0/7），与使用 CUDA VMM 还是 `cudaMalloc` 无关；一个扫描作业也导致节点 09 冻结。所检查的长时间运行节点的每个 EFA 设备都记录了 `reg_mr_err=46`（来自早期的内存注册失败）；重启过的节点为 0，当前负载也不会产生新的注册失败。在运维重启前排除这些节点，启动脚本也会拒绝任何 EFA 设备存在注册失败记录的节点。分离式作业不再自动重新排队（此前一个挂起的作业曾辗转四组节点）。分离式 worker 去掉 `enable-cumem-allocator` 并设置 `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`，因为在健康节点上 Mooncake 写入 VMM 缓冲区每 rank 仅约 2 GB/s，写入 `cudaMalloc` 缓冲区则为 14–27 GB/s。启动脚本在 Dynamo 源码安装前，先安装经官方 SHA256 校验的固定版本 `aiconfigurator-core` wheel，避免其占位包间歇性下载失败。

将 #4047 的 Kimi K3 DSpark AgentX 配置空间移植到 B300：包含十个 DCP 分离式推理性能点和三个低延迟聚合式推理性能点，每个 DCP8 worker 使用一个八卡节点。

NIXL 和 Mooncake 使用 EFA，保持模型、并发矩阵、标准合成接受率选择和评估覆盖范围不变。启动脚本构建支持 THP 和主机内存块折叠的固定版本 Mooncake，并回移 libfabric 上游的 CUDA VMM 同步修复；另外为 vLLM 依赖 NVLink 的 latent-MoE tail 增加默认开启的开关。这些推理栈修改需要补丁豁免。

双节点 TP16 配置使用常规解码和可跨节点使用的集合通信，关闭 custom allreduce、GEMM-AR 和融合 latent-MoE tail。这些融合路径依赖 TP 组内 GPU 多播，而 EFA 连接的节点间不支持该能力。单节点 TP8 配置保留融合路径。

新一轮扫描的三个聚合式性能测试均已通过原有结果和功耗验证：TP8 c2 为 2,681.25 TPS/GPU，TP8 c4 为 4,028.18 TPS/GPU，TP16 c1 为 568.12 TPS/GPU；工具调用评估分别为 403/408、404/408 和 401/408。原有内容校验分别排除了一、三、一条 profiling 记录；c2 在测量窗口结束后的宽限期截止时取消了一条未完成请求，仍通过原有门槛。2P3D c192 在服务启动前失败，原因是两个 worker 下载的 `aiconfigurator-core` 软件包未通过官方 SHA256 校验；暂按偶发安装失败处理，等待重试，不修改安装流程或绕过校验。完整扫描尚未全部通过，公开分离式推理路径仍待验证。调度排除规则已避开可独立复现容器启动前任务创建失败的故障节点；内存注册修复已通过本地完整模型 Dynamo prefill 启动和全新镜像的软件包验证，缓存容量与评估要求未降低。

</details>

<details><summary>AI model disclosure</summary>

Prepared with OpenAI Codex. The runtime does not expose an exact model/version identifier, so it could not be verified. No delegated agents were used.

</details>

title: Add GB200 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash P/D without KV offload / 新增无 KV 卸载的 GB200 P/D
body:
Add DeepSeek V4.1 Flash AgentX on GB200 as 1P/1D DEP4/DEP16 at concurrency 64, 128, and 256. Uses Engram UVA, DSpark5 synthetic AL 3.51, NIXL P/D transfer, and GPU-resident KV without MooncakeStore.

新增 GB200 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash AgentX 1P/1D DEP4/DEP16 配方，并发为 64、128、256。使用 Engram UVA、DSpark5 合成 AL 3.51、NIXL P/D 传输；KV 驻留 GPU，不启用 MooncakeStore。

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a five-node multinode Slurm/disagg benchmark path with launcher and cache-mount changes on a shared GB200 cluster; misconfiguration could waste GPU time but does not touch auth or data handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **GB200 disaggregated AgentX** lane for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: one DEP4 prefill worker and one DEP16 decode worker on five nodes, swept at concurrency **64, 128, and 256**. KV stays **GPU-resident**; prefill/decode exchange KV via **NIXL** only (no MooncakeStore tier), with Engram CPU offload and **DSpark5** plus synthetic acceptance length **3.51** for throughput.
> 
> A new srt-slurm recipe (`disagg-gb200-1p1d-dep4-dep16-c64-c256-dspark5-agentic.yaml`) drives `agentic_srt.sh` with Dynamo router 1.4.0 and the pinned vLLM flash image.
> 
> **Registry and ops wiring:** `nvidia-master.yaml` key `dsv41flash-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-disagg`, perf changelog, and EN/ZH procedure docs. **`launch_gb200-nv.sh`** resolves weights from the shared HF hub snapshot, clones **srt-slurm v1.0.36** for this AgentX P/D path, overlays v4.1-flash recipes, and mounts HF **blobs** for agentic containers.
> 
> A small **`test_dsv41flash_gb200_pd.py`** guards the recipe shape (NIXL roles, no Mooncake/external KV store).
>

title: [H3 CI]: add video serving metrics and GPU energy [DO NOT MERGE] / 新增视频服务指标与 GPU 能耗（暂勿合并）
body:
## Description

Run H3 video benchmarks through InferenceX GitHub Actions → Slurm → H200, retaining original playable media, provenance, video/audio checks and measured GPU power/energy. Add opt-in closed-loop client concurrency and a bounded C1/C2/C4 smoke matrix using one two-GPU allocation.

通过 InferenceX GitHub Actions → Slurm → H200 执行 H3 视频测试，保留原始可播放媒体、来源信息、视频/音频检查及实测 GPU 功率/能耗。新增可选客户端闭环并发，以及复用同一次双卡分配的 C1/C2/C4 小规模测试。

- Preserve serial baseline/candidate regression by default. Serving workers submit the next request after media download; validation runs separately. Retain every scheduled outcome, raw lifecycle timing and job ID, including failures and unfinished attempts. / 默认保留串行 baseline/candidate 回归。服务模式在媒体下载后提交下一请求，校验独立执行；保留每个计划请求的结果、原始时间和任务 ID，包括失败及未完成请求。
- Run exactly four measured requests per concurrency with separate warmup. Reuse the existing supervisor, UUID ownership checks, media verifier and cleanup; stop later cells on failure. Resolve Slurm-assigned physical device minors to GPU UUIDs before launch. / 每档并发正式测量四次，预热单独记录。复用监督器、GPU UUID 归属检查、媒体校验和清理，失败后停止后续档位；启动前将 Slurm 分配的物理设备编号映射为 GPU UUID。
- Export delivery latency, completion counts, throughput, observed client concurrency and optional deadline goodput. Integrate GPU-board energy once across overlapping requests. Retain prompt/seed/settings, model/runtime pins, memory samples and raw artifacts; unavailable measurements remain null. / 导出交付延迟、完成计数、吞吐、实际客户端并发及可选截止时间有效吞吐。重叠请求的 GPU 板级能耗只积分一次；保留输入、版本、显存采样和原始产物，缺失指标保持空值。
- Keep the existing paired-result contract and portable reports. The serving matrix has its own raw summary/report; paired frontend export is skipped for this single-runtime smoke. / 保留现有配对结果契约与离线报告。并发矩阵提供原始汇总及报告；单运行时测试跳过配对前端导出。

**Validation / 验证 — `30a8a65d839e67bb67e979f7e34987f82baa2696`**

- [Current-head Linux CPU CI](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34318363797): **555 passed**, entry-shell syntax and workflow lint passed. Local relevant checks and incremental changelog validation passed; historical changelog entries remain unchanged. / 当前提交 Linux CPU CI **555 项通过**，入口 shell 语法、工作流 lint、本地相关检查及增量 changelog 校验通过，历史条目保持不变。
- [Real two-H200 serving CI](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34318467752): **12/12 measured requests technically valid, zero failures, plus three separate benchmark warmups**. Slurm `82338.0`, `worker-10`, two allocated and two participating H200 GPUs; reused the prepared runtime. Allocation released after 54m33s. / 真实双 H200 CI：**12/12 正式请求通过技术完整性检查，零失败，另有三次独立预热**。Slurm `82338.0`，节点 `worker-10`，分配及参与均为两张 H200，复用已有运行环境；54 分 33 秒后释放分配。
- [Original artifact](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34318467752/artifacts/10092515697): `serving-smoke.json`, `report/index.html`, per-request records, 15 original MP4s, telemetry and power reports. Offline verification checked all 106 file hashes, all 12 report video references, raw concurrency/latency arithmetic and independently integrated raw power samples. Fixed-input media hashes match; prior full-decode evidence was reused for identical bytes, with technical checks passing. / 原始产物含矩阵汇总、离线报告、逐请求记录、15 个原始 MP4、遥测及功率报告。本地核对 106 个文件摘要、12 个报告视频链接、原始并发/延迟计算，并独立积分功率采样。固定输入的媒体摘要一致，复用相同字节的完整解码证据，技术检查通过。

Same frozen workload at all three loads: MiniMax-H3 `42ed227…`, SGLang `71de97b…`, TP1/Ulysses2, no DiT CPU offload, 50 steps, seed 11, one drum-taps prompt, 1344×768, 107 frames at 24 FPS (4.458 s decoded video), native 32 kHz stereo audio.

三档使用完全相同的固定负载：MiniMax-H3 `42ed227…`、SGLang `71de97b…`、TP1/Ulysses2、关闭 DiT CPU offload、50 步、种子 11、同一鼓点提示词、1344×768、24 FPS 共 107 帧（解码视频 4.458 秒），原生 32 kHz 双声道音频。

| Client concurrency / 客户端并发 | Valid / 有效 | Delivery median / 交付中位数 (s) | Valid clips/hour, both GPUs / 双卡有效视频每小时 | Mean two-board power / 双卡平均板级功率 (W) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 4/4 | 119.50 | 30.12 | 1373.87 |
| 2 | 4/4 | 237.68 | 30.26 | 1378.11 |
| 4 | 4/4 | 297.69 | 30.27 | 1377.92 |

Latency is submission to downloaded media. Hourly throughput is normalized from the roughly eight-minute measured delivery window per cell, excluding preparation and warmup; it is not an hour-long sustained test. Board power covers first submit through last observed provider completion, includes intervening gaps, and excludes host/unselected GPUs. Energy is 163.88–164.18 kJ per valid clip. Increasing client concurrency did not materially increase observed throughput in this small sample; GPU-parallel batching is not established.

**Limits / 限制**

Four samples per load do not establish P90/P95, sustained capacity or cross-hardware superiority. Queue/execution timestamps, actual batching, fixed offered arrival rates, multi-replica launch, calibrated perceptual quality and full deployment cost remain unavailable. Technical validity does not establish paired fidelity or release qualification. The matrix therefore retains `ci_accepted=false` and `release_qualified=false` even though the requested smoke passed. title: perf: reuse compact dispatch sort permutations for cached handles
body:
Compact deterministic dispatch sorts the received rows by source index on every call. For a cached dispatch the handle already fixes that order: the same slots are refilled, the receive counts are the same, and `topk_idx` is asserted immutable. This stores the permutation on the handle next to `cached_recv_src_metadata_before_sort` at the first dispatch and reuses it, so cached compact dispatch no longer builds the sort keys, masks the unused capacity, or sorts.

The stored permutation follows the same stream and lifetime rules as the handle's existing cached metadata, so no per-call checks are needed and the reuse also holds under CUDA Graph capture and for deferred epilogues waited on another stream. Each handle keeps one extra int64 tensor of capacity rows (128 KiB at 16k rows). No API, default, native or test-file changes; `tests/ep/test_ep.py` already compares repeated cached dispatch against the reference, and the EP8 suite passes on this branch with CPU counts (direct and deferred epilogues) and in the sync-free mode.

Measured on 8×H200 (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132), one cached dispatch per rank, 2048 tokens/rank, hidden 4096, top-2, BF16, deterministic, `do_cpu_sync=False`, under both `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM` policies; outputs (payload, `topk_idx`, weights, source index) are bitwise identical to main across 608 fresh/cached/deferred/graph cases per policy:

| Per cached dispatch | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Device kernels and memsets | 24 | 6 |
| Host enqueue time | 328 µs | 129 µs |
| Synchronized wall time, 8-rank max | 439 µs | 280 µs |
| Kernels in a captured cached dispatch | 15 (incl. sort) | 6 |

The removed kernels (radix sort, `arange`, compare, `clone`, `masked_fill`, memsets) account for about 46 µs of device time per call; the wall-time reduction is mostly host overhead and is a component measurement, not a training-throughput claim. Independent of #786, which removes the unused sorts of the expanded layout; both touch `deterministic_sort` and the later one needs a trivial rebase.

title: Add opt-in borrowed receive storage for compact BF16 dispatch
body:
`dispatch(..., borrow_recv=True)` skips the activation copy of the dispatch epilogue: the epilogue writes only metadata plus a row map and returns a `DispatchRecvView` (`slab`, `row_indices`) over the communication buffer, which an indexed consumer such as a gathered GEMM reads directly. The view holds an exclusive lease: `release(*streams)` orders the next communication after the consumers, and dispatch/combine/LB calls/`destroy()` reject an active view. Supported: fresh compact BF16 dispatch within one NVLink domain with CPU counts and `defer_epilogue=False`; everything else is rejected up front. Default behavior is unchanged.

8×H200, deterministic, hidden 3072, top-8, 16 local experts, dispatch plus the same indexed consumer: −13.1% at 8192 tokens/rank and −13.5% at 16384, but +15.9% at 1024, hence opt-in. Fixed-route serial forward only; no overlap or training-throughput claim. Combined with DeepGEMM #463 in a live EP8 + gate/up GEMM + SwiGLU step: −17%. Raw cycles and the reproducer: [gist](https://gist.github.com/yuweih205/d3fd1e4c3fcb97364f36ec8fda996cfe).

Test: `python tests/ep/test_recv_view.py --num-processes 8` (bitwise payload/metadata against the gathered inputs, replay/combine after release, delayed cross-stream readers, invalid-mode rejection).

Re-validated 2026-10-16 at 71157be (100350f differs only in documentation; native code byte-identical to the measured build) on 8×H200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132: `test_recv_view.py` 16/16 cases under both `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM` policies; the EP8 functional suite passes with CPU counts for direct and deferred epilogues. With `--do-cpu-sync 0` the unmodified suite stops at its full-capacity `recv_x_twice` comparison on this branch exactly as on upstream main; with the valid-prefix comparison from #786 it passes on both.

title: github:deepseek-ai/DeepEP:693 fetched implementation patch
[Bug] SM90 `fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd", a, b, d, c)` silently drops `c` and returns `a @ b.T`
body:
## Description

On SM90, `deep_gemm.fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd", a, b, d, c=c)` returns $d = a \cdot b^\top$ instead of $d = c + a \cdot b^\top$. No error is raised, and the output looks like a normal result. The same happens when `d` and `c` are the same tensor (in-place accumulation). On SM100 the result is correct.

[The README's convention](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/README.md?plain=1#L63) is `D = C + A @ B` ("`fp8_gemm_nt` will do a `D = C + A @ B.T`"), and `fp8_einsum` accepts `c` on every architecture. `"bhr,hdr->bhd"` is the only `fp8_einsum` expression that runs on SM90, so any caller that accumulates through it on Hopper gets a wrong result.

## Environment

- H100 80GB HBM3 (sm_90), driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), torch 2.9.1+cu130.
- DeepGEMM `main` 1fc9c66, CUTLASS f3fde58, built with `./develop.sh`.

## Root Cause

The host prepares `d` for an accumulating kernel, but on SM90 it launches a kernel that only stores:

1. `fp8_einsum` passes `c` to `fp8_bmm` ([einsum.hpp L276](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/einsum.hpp#L276)), which calls `gemm::early_return` ([L230](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/einsum.hpp#L230)). It copies `c` into `d`, expecting the kernel to add into `d` ([gemm.hpp L49–L51](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/gemm.hpp#L49-L51)):

   ```cpp
   // With accumulation, do copy before GEMM (assuming the GEMM kernel does not support different C/D)
   if (c.has_value() and not is_cd_same)
       d.copy_(c.value());
   ```

2. On SM90, `fp8_bmm` calls `sm90_fp8_bmm` ([einsum.hpp L247](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/einsum.hpp#L247)), which launches `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d_impl`. It sets `with_accumulation = c.has_value()` in the `GemmDesc` ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp L300](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L300)), but the flag is not a template argument of the kernel ([L36–L61](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L36-L61)), and the kernel writes `D` with a plain TMA store ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.cuh L434](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.cuh#L434)):

   ```cpp
   if constexpr (kGemmType == GemmType::Batched) {
       cute::SM90_TMA_STORE_3D::copy(&tensor_map_d, smem_ptr,
                                     n_idx, m_idx, scheduler.current_group_idx);
   ```

   This overwrites the `c` that step 1 copied into `d`. For comparison, `sm90_bf16_gemm` passes `with_accumulation` to its kernel as `kWithAccumulation` and switches the store to a reduce-add.

3. The other launcher of the same kernel, `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d` (used by `fp8_gemm_nt`), rejects `c` ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp L81](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L81)):

   ```cpp
   DG_HOST_ASSERT(not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
   ```

   `sm90_fp8_bmm` has no such check.

`tests/test_einsum.py` passes `c` to `fp8_einsum` only on SM100 ([L183](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/tests/test_einsum.py#L183)), so the SM90 path with `c` is untested.

## Reproduction

`repro.py`:

```python
import torch
import deep_gemm
from deep_gemm.utils.math import per_block_cast_to_fp8, per_token_cast_to_fp8

torch.manual_seed(0)
b, h, r, d = 128, 8, 4096, 1024
x = torch.randn(b, h, r, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
y = torch.randn(h, d, r, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
x_fp8, x_sf = per_token_cast_to_fp8(x.view(-1, r), use_ue8m0=False)
y_fp8, y_sf = zip(*(per_block_cast_to_fp8(y[i], use_ue8m0=False) for i in range(h)))
a_ = (x_fp8.view(b, h, r), x_sf.view(b, h, r // 128))
b_ = (torch.stack(y_fp8), torch.stack(y_sf))

ab = torch.einsum('bhr,hdr->bhd', x.float(), y.float())
# as large as a @ b.T, in the layout fp8_einsum requires for C: [h, b, d] viewed as [b, h, d]
c = (ab.std() * torch.randn(h, b, d, device='cuda')).bfloat16().permute(1, 0, 2)
d_out = torch.empty_like(c)
deep_gemm.fp8_einsum('bhr,hdr->bhd', a_, b_, d_out, c=c)

rel_err = lambda ref: ((d_out.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item()
print(f'relative error vs c + a @ b.T: {rel_err(c.float() + ab):.3f}')   # expected: small
print(f'relative error vs a @ b.T:     {rel_err(ab):.3f}')               # actual: small
```

## Expected vs Actual

Expected: `d_out` ≈ `c + a @ b.T`, with a relative error at the FP8 level. If SM90 does not support `c` here, a host assertion is expected, as in `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`.

Actual (`python repro.py` on the H100 above): `d_out` is `a @ b.T` up to the FP8 error, and `c` is missing.

```
relative error vs c + a @ b.T: 0.707
relative error vs a @ b.T:     0.037
```

## Suggested Fix

Either of the following removes the silent wrong result. Which one fits the intended SM90 support?

1. **Reject `c` in `sm90_fp8_bmm`**, as `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d` does:

   ```diff
   @@ -287,7 +287,7 @@ static void sm90_fp8_bmm(const torch::Tensor& a, const torch::Tensor& sfa,
                             const std::string& compiled_dims) {
   -    DG_HOST_ASSERT(d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
   +    DG_HOST_ASSERT(not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
        DG_HOST_ASSERT(major_a == cute::UMMA::Major::K and major_b == cute::UMMA::Major::K);
   ```

   With this change, `repro.py` raises `RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp:290): not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16` on the same H100. As in `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`, the check runs after `early_return` has copied `c` into `d`.

2. **Support `c` on SM90**: add an accumulation flag to `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d_impl` that writes `D` with a TMA reduce-add, as `sm90_bf16_gemm` does with `kWithAccumulation`, and pass `with_accumulation` to it from `sm90_fp8_bmm`.

I can open a PR for either option.

title: Add shape-aware recommended alignment for SM90 small-M grouped GEMM by qescccczmr · Pull Request #350 · deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM · GitHub
body:
Conversation
qescccczmr
commented
Jun 2, 2026
Copy link
Copy Markdown
Summary
This PR adds a shape-aware recommended M/K alignment helper for contiguous grouped layouts.
The existing
get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout()
keeps SM90 on the legacy 128 alignment. For SM90 m-grouped contiguous GEMM, this can introduce extra
padded rows for some small-M non-psum shapes.
This PR adds an opt-in recommendation helper that returns 64 only for the empirically validated shape family:
SM90
non-psum m-grouped contiguous layout
num_groups == 4
expected_m == 128
expected_k <= 256
All other shapes fall back to the existing theoretical alignment.
This does not change the default alignment.
Motivation
Grouped contiguous layout requires each expert segment to be aligned by
get_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout()
. In the target small-M case, using 128 alignment pads
the generated test shape from
M=640
to
M=768
.
Reducing the recommended alignment to 64 for the validated shape reduces padded rows while preserving correctness.
Broader scans showed regressions for other shapes such as
expected_m=64
,
expected_m=192
,
num_groups=8/16
, and
k>=512
, so this helper intentionally keeps the 64
recommendation restricted.
Changes
Add
get_recommended_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout(use_psum_layout, expected_m, expected_k, expected_num_groups)
.
Expose the helper through the Python layout API.
Document the helper in README.
Rename the benchmark/test wording from small-K to small-M.
