title: [Feature]: Expand MNNVL CuTe DSL AllReduce profiles beyond GB300 H=8192 TP8/TP16
body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

## Problem

The MNNVL CuTe DSL all-reduce fusion backend currently ships built-in static profiles only for GB300, BF16, `H=8192`, `Top-K=10`, and TP8/TP16. `MNNVLCuteDSLConfig.resolve()` keys profiles by TP size, hidden size, Top-K, and dtype, and raises `No MNNVL CuTe DSL profile supports this static shape` for other combinations.

This makes an otherwise promising backend difficult to use outside the initial Qwen3.8 2.4T-style geometry. In particular, inference engines cannot select it broadly for other tensor-parallel models or hardware without carrying custom profiles and doing their own correctness/performance tuning.

The backend's LL/BT/HT protocols cover decode through prefill and the initial implementation reports strong gains over the existing composed MNNVL and NCCL paths. Broadening the validated profile matrix would make those protocols usable by more models and would unblock a general vLLM integration instead of a model-specific one.

## Requested outcome

Expand the validated and tuned MNNVL CuTe DSL profile matrix beyond the initial GB300 `H=8192`, `Top-K=10`, TP8/TP16 configuration.

Concretely, it would be useful to have:

- Profiles for representative hidden sizes and model families beyond the initial geometry.
- TP2/TP4 coverage where the protocols and topology support it, in addition to TP8/TP16.
- Validation and tuning on SM100 and SM103, plus a clear path for architecture-specific profiles on future MNNVL systems.
- A documented/public benchmark workflow for sweeping `M`, selecting LL/BT/HT crossover points, and producing checked-in presets.
- A safe dispatch/fallback story so inference engines can probe support without hard-coding one model configuration.

## Target hardware

- SM100 (B200, GB200)
- SM103 (B300, GB300)
- Future architecture

## Inference engine

- vLLM
- PyTorch native

## Affected model or model family

Tensor-parallel models using MNNVL all-reduce fusion. The initial checked-in profiles correspond to Qwen3.8 2.4T-style `H=8192`, TP8/TP16 geometry; the request is to support additional public model shapes rather than another single-model specialization.

## Workload and configuration

- Data type and quantization: BF16 all-reduce input; fused residual add + RMSNorm, optionally preceded by MoE finalize/shared-expert add. Future quantized output fusion can be evaluated separately.
- Batch size or request concurrency: decode through prefill; sweep the full supported `M` range so LL, BT, and HT crossover points are tuned per profile.
- Sequence lengths or token counts: all; the relevant dispatch dimension is `M`.
- Parallelism: TP2/TP4/TP8/TP16 over NVLink/MNNVL, subject to topology support.
- Relevant shapes: multiple hidden sizes and Top-K values beyond `H=8192`, `Top-K=10`.
- Environment: Blackwell SM100/SM103 first; future-architecture profiles when public hardware validation is available.

## Current workaround

Use the existing TRT-LLM MNNVL, NCCL, or framework-specific all-reduce backend, or maintain a private `MNNVLCuteDSLConfig` and retune all LL/BT/HT presets and route boundaries. The first options leave performance on the table, while the latter is not a maintainable integration strategy for frameworks.

## Impact

- Missing model or hardware support
- Throughput
- Latency
- API usability or integration complexity
- Testing, maintainability, or documentation

## Acceptance criteria

- Add correctness-tested built-in profiles for at least one non-`H=8192` model geometry, and add TP2/TP4 coverage where supported.
- Exercise both fusion patterns across the newly supported profiles:
  - AllReduce + residual add + RMSNorm
  - MoE finalize + shared-expert add + AllReduce + residual add + RMSNorm
- Publish benchmark results across representative `M` values and derive LL/BT/HT route boundaries from those results.
- Preserve the existing GB300 TP8/TP16 profile performance and numerical contracts.
- Provide a support-query or documented fallback path suitable for inference-engine dispatch.
- Keep hardware-specific tuning isolated in profiles so future architectures can be added without model checks in framework integrations.

## Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- Initial backend: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4358
- Related but distinct PDL-overlap request: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5151
- Related TP12/Kimi K3 shape request: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4542
- Current profile definitions: `flashinfer/comm/mnnvl_cutedsl/presets.py`
- Profile resolution: `flashinfer/comm/mnnvl_cutedsl/config.py`
- Existing routing tests: `tests/comm/test_mnnvl_cutedsl_config.py`

I can help with tuning, public benchmark sweeps, and follow-up PR work for additional shapes.

title: perf(comm): gather MoE-finalize routes together and accumulate in FP32
body:
## 📌 Description Stacked on #6630 (poll the local Lamport buffer); please review that one first. This makes `trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion` faster and more accurate: - **Gather the top-k rows together.** The finalize loop handled one route at a time: load the permuted index, then load that row, then move to the next route. Each row load had to wait for its own index load. Now the kernel loads the indices and scales of 8 routes first, then all 8 rows, so the row loads are in flight together. - **Accumulate in FP32.** The routed sum, the `routed_scaling_factor`, the shared-expert add and the sum over ranks were all done in the activation dtype, rounding after every step. They now stay in FP32 and round once. This matches `allreduce_fusion` with `fp32_acc=True`. Test fixes in `test_trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion_finalize.py`: - Its reference is now computed in FP32. The old BF16 reference does each multiply and add in BF16, and the BF16/TP4 case failed on B300 even before this change. - `scale_out` is now sized for the `SWIZZLED_128x4` layout the kernel writes: `round_up(T, 128) * round_up(H / 16, 4)` bytes. The test allocated `T * H / 16` elements, and the kernel wrote past the end. That only showed up as an illegal address once the FP32 reference allocated tensors next to it. ## 🔍 Related Issues #2269, #3671 (fused finalize slower than finalize + `kARResidualRMSNorm`) ## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist ### ✅ Pre-commit Checks - [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method). - [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`. - [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. ## 🧪 Tests - [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed. - [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.). B300 (SM103), TP4, CUDA 13.4. The `test_trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion_finalize.py` row is with this PR's test file: | | before (#6630) | this PR | |---|---|---| | `test_trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion_finalize.py` (FP16/BF16 x TP2/TP4, back-to-back) | BF16/TP4 fails | all pass (2/2 runs) | | `test_trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion.py` | passes | passes | Latency and accuracy: one launch inside a CUDA graph, TP4, BF16, top-k 8, `launch_with_pdl=True`. Each rank has its own GEMM2 rows, softmax routing weights and shared-expert output. The reference is FP64. "stock" is FlashInfer main; "#6630" adds only the local-poll fix. | hidden | tokens | stock (us) | #6630 (us) | this PR (us) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 6144 | 1 | 8.60 | 7.50 | 6.20 | | 6144 | 4 | 8.75 | 7.63 | 6.49 | | 6144 | 16 | 9.22 | 8.25 | 7.10 | | 6144 | 32 | 15.06 | 11.14 | 9.14 | | 6144 | 64 | 26.24 | 20.13 | 15.19 | | 6144 | 128 | hangs | 38.85 | 29.02 | | 7168 | 1 | 8.80 | 8.10 | 6.56 | | 7168 | 16 | 9.66 | 8.76 | 7.40 | | 7168 | 64 | 19.08 | 13.04 | 12.11 | | 7168 | 128 | hangs | 23.47 | 21.85 | | mean abs error vs FP64 | stock / #6630 | this PR | BF16 rounding of the exact result | |---|---|---|---| | `residual_out` | 7.6e-3 to 8.0e-3 | 6.0e-3 | 4.8e-3 | | `norm_out` | 2.1e-3 to 2.2e-3 | 1.75e-3 | | End to end in vLLM (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP 3, B300), with a vLLM change that finalizes each decode MoE layer in this kernel (PR to follow, it will link here). Target verify forward latency (`vllm bench forward`, CUDA graph, spread < 0.1%), deferring vs not deferring the finalize: | kernel | 1 request (4 tokens) | 3 requests (12 tokens) | 7 requests (28 tokens) | |---|---|---|---| | #6630 only | +0.4% to +0.6% | +0.4% | +2.1% to +2.2% | | this PR | -1.2% to -1.3% | -1.5% | -0.8% | That is, with only #6630 fusing the finalize does not pay off; with this PR it does. On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang (vllm-project/vllm#62174 with this PR, #6630 and #6632): decode time on the same turns drops 1.2-3.1% at concurrency 1-8 and 0.4% at 16 on 4x GB200, 1.6-3.1% on 4x B300.
Benchmark script: python fi_finalize_bench.py 4 out.json ```python """FlashInfer trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion: error vs an FP64 reference and latency. usage: python fi_finalize_bench.py WORLD_SIZE OUT_JSON [--tokens 1 4 16 64 128] [--hidden 6144 7168] Each rank gets its own random GEMM2 rows, routing (top-k 8, softmax weights) and shared expert output, as in a TP MoE layer. The reference finalizes, adds the shared output, all-reduces, adds the residual and applies RMSNorm in FP64. Latency: one CUDA graph of 20 back-to-back launches, replayed 50 times, max over ranks of the median per-launch time. """ import argparse import json import socket import statistics import torch import torch.distributed as dist import torch.multiprocessing as mp import flashinfer.comm as comm TOP_K, MAX_TOKENS, EPS, RSF = 8, 2048, 1e-5, 2.5 def worker(rank, world_size, port, tokens_list, hidden_list, out_path): torch.cuda.set_device(rank) dev = torch.device("cuda", rank) dist.init_process_group("nccl", init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}", rank=rank, world_size=world_size, device_id=dev) results = [] for hidden in hidden_list: _, workspace = comm.trtllm_create_ipc_workspace_for_all_reduce_fusion( rank, world_size, MAX_TOKENS, hidden, group=dist.group.WORLD) for tokens in tokens_list: g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(1000 * rank + tokens) rows = 2 * tokens * TOP_K + 8 gemm2 = (torch.randn(rows, hidden, device=dev, generator=g) * 0.5).bfloat16() idx = torch.randperm(rows, device=dev, generator=g)[: tokens * TOP_K] idx = idx.view(tokens, TOP_K).int() weights = torch.softmax(torch.randn(tokens, TOP_K, device=dev, generator=g), -1).bfloat16() shared = (torch.randn(tokens, hidden, device=dev, generator=g) * 0.5).bfloat16() gs = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(7 + tokens) # same on every rank residual = (torch.randn(tokens, hidden, device=dev, generator=gs) * 4).bfloat16() norm_w = (1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(hidden, device=dev, generator=gs)).bfloat16() norm_out = torch.empty_like(residual) res_out = torch.empty_like(residual) def run(): comm.trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion( allreduce_in=gemm2, residual_in=residual, norm_weight=norm_w, expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx=idx, norm_out=norm_out, residual_out=res_out, quant_out=None, scale_out=None, workspace_ptrs=workspace, launch_with_pdl=True, world_rank=rank, world_size=world_size, eps=EPS, shared_expert_output=shared, expert_scale_factor=weights, routed_scaling_factor=RSF) # Every rank's workspace and inputs are ready before any rank writes to a peer. torch.cuda.synchronize() dist.barrier() run() torch.cuda.synchronize() # FP64 reference over all ranks' partial outputs. partial = (gemm2.double()[idx.long()] * weights.double()[..., None]).sum(1) * RSF partial += shared.double() dist.all_reduce(partial) ref_res = partial + residual.double() ref_norm = ref_res * torch.rsqrt(ref_res.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + EPS) ref_norm *= norm_w.double() err_res = (res_out.double() - ref_res).abs() err_norm = (norm_out.double() - ref_norm).abs() # Error of just rounding the reference to BF16, the floor for a BF16 output. floor_res = (ref_res.bfloat16().double() - ref_res).abs() s = torch.cuda.Stream() s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream()) with torch.cuda.stream(s): for _ in range(3): run() torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s) graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() with torch.cuda.graph(graph): for _ in range(20): run() times = [] for _ in range(50): dist.barrier() torch.cuda.synchronize() st, en = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) st.record() graph.replay() en.record() torch.cuda.synchronize() times.append(st.elapsed_time(en) * 1000 / 20) t = torch.tensor([statistics.median(times)], device=dev) dist.all_reduce(t, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX) stats = torch.tensor([err_res.max(), err_res.mean(), err_norm.max(), err_norm.mean(), floor_res.mean()], device=dev, dtype=torch.float64) dist.all_reduce(stats, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX) row = {"hidden": hidden, "tokens": tokens, "us": round(t.item(), 2), "res_max_err": stats[0].item(), "res_mean_err": stats[1].item(), "norm_max_err": stats[2].item(), "norm_mean_err": stats[3].item(), "res_mean_err_bf16_floor": stats[4].item()} results.append(row) if rank == 0: print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) del graph if rank == 0: json.dump(results, open(out_path, "w"), indent=1) dist.barrier() dist.destroy_process_group() if __name__ == "__main__": p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("world_size", type=int) p.add_argument("out") p.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 4, 16, 64, 128]) p.add_argument("--hidden", type=int, nargs="+", default=[6144, 7168]) a = p.parse_args() with socket.socket() as sock: sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)) port = sock.getsockname()[1] mp.spawn(worker, args=(a.world_size, port, a.tokens, a.hidden, a.out), nprocs=a.world_size) ```

title: [cake deslop] cake_comm (2): drop byte-identical MNNVL a2a SM103 file, template union/Ulysses clones, share one prelude (-13.6K lines)
body:
**Background.** This issue covers the Cake-generated comm kernels for SM100/SM103:
- the MoE all-reduce union (`trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion(..., backend="cake")`);
- the finalize-allreduce fusion (`trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion(..., backend="cake")`);
- `flashinfer.comm.cake_fused_norm_combine`;
- the Ulysses all-to-all (`UlyssesCommunicator`, nvlink backend);
- the DCP all-to-all (`decode_cp_a2a_alltoall`);
- the MNNVL MoE all-to-all (`get_moe_alltoall_module(backend="cake")`).

Together they are 59 kernel sources (36,269 lines), 7 bindings/launchers (1,101 lines) and 5 JIT loaders (1,530 lines). The first round handled each family separately: #5769 union (#5848; #5945 then regenerated it into the current 27 kernels / 60 routes), #5770 fusion bundle (retired by #5849/#5856), #5771 finalize (#5852, #5870), #5773 norm-combine (#5874), #5804 DCP (#5948) and #5807 Ulysses. #5953 made the Ulysses kernels arch-neutral but left the 24 dtype clones untemplated. Since then, #5894 added scratch-tensor retention to the union loader, and #6057/#6128/#6166 grew `cake_moe_finalize_kernels.cu` to 1,446 lines. #6545 regenerated the MNNVL all-to-all bundle (first committed in #4784); no earlier sub-issue covered it. Counts are at 3184bbea.

**Findings**
- **Byte-identical MNNVL pair.** `csrc/generated/mnnvl_moe_alltoall_sm100.cu` and `_sm103.cu` are byte-identical at 6,533 lines each. They were already identical in #4784 (3,018 lines each), and #6545 regenerated both the same way. The only per-arch text is the `#if __CUDA_ARCH__ == 1000` smem guard (lines 121-126), so one source compiled per `-gencode` gives the same TU. Only `flashinfer/jit/comm.py:310-311` (`gen_moe_alltoall_module`) and six test lines reference the file names. `aot.py:1039-1041` builds both modules. All 33 `kernel_flashinfer_mnnvl_moe_alltoall_*` kernels are used by the top_k lists in `moeAlltoAllFusedKernels.cu`, so nothing inside the file is dead.
- **Union constant clones.** 9 of the 27 kernels in `csrc/cake_trtllm_moe_allreduce_union/kernels/` form 4 groups (4,582 lines) that differ in only 2-7 normalised lines. 2,515 of those lines are redundant. The differences:
  - `__launch_bounds__(224)` vs `(224, 5)`;
  - `#pragma unroll 8` vs `4`;
  - pipeline depth 1 vs 2;
  - `ws4_bf16_sm103_t1_t1_e8_serial_clear` vs `ws4_bf16_wide_mlp`: unroll, `#pragma unroll 1`, and a lane-0 load + shfl broadcast of `expert_scale`.

  The launcher already takes `-DCAKE_UNION_{KERNEL,DTYPE,WORLD_SIZE,BLOCK,CLUSTER}` (`cake_trtllm_moe_allreduce_union_launcher.cu:21-27`, `kernel_defines()`). The bf16/f16 twins differ by 161-406 lines and are not clones.
- **Union exact-shape routes.** 18 of the 27 kernels (9,507 lines) and 36 of the 60 routes are selected only through `_SPECIALIZATION_RULES` (`flashinfer/jit/cake_trtllm_moe_allreduce_union.py:306-355`, 32 keys / 37 entries). A rule matches on `num_experts` ∈ {8, 12, 16}, one of the token bands 1-32 / 32-96 / 96-192 / 192-384 / 1536-2048, and `launch_with_pdl`. Every other shape falls to the 9 class programs (4,638 lines) in `select_specialization()`/`route_for()`. 6 of the 36 rule-only routes reuse class kernels. The module comment says each band is ≥2 % faster than the class program, but `benchmarks/comm` has no union benchmark. `hidden_dim` is fixed at 7168. 16 of the 54 (kernel, arch) pairs are never requested. That is harmless under per-request JIT, although the docstring (lines 22-24) says every kernel is compiled per arch.
- **Ulysses dtype clones.** `csrc/generated/ulysses/` has 24 kernels (4,982 lines): {bf16, f16, f32} × ws {2, 4, 6, 8} × mode {0, 1}. All 24 are reachable through `csrc/cake_ulysses_dispatch.cu:136-185`. With hash and dtype tokens normalised, ws8 mode1 bf16 vs f16 differ in 0 lines and f16 vs f32 in 4 (vector width 8 vs 4), so 3,242 lines are redundant. Six bf16 files have benchmark-point branches (`B==1`, `S==16380/8190/5460`, `grid==36`) with hard-coded reciprocal magics (167 lines). These match the four large BF16 rows of `tests/comm/cake_ulysses_a2a_fixture.py`. `FLASHINFER_ULYSSES_GENERATED` compiles out the portable path (`ulysses_all_to_all.cu:167-178`), so the module has no fallback.
- **Inlined prelude.** 30 TUs each paste the same prelude (int typedefs, `CakeTensorMap64`, the `CUtensorMap` assert, `make_warp_uniform`): 1,048 lines in total (Ulysses 24 × 36, DCP 2 × 27, norm-combine 3 × 34, finalize 28). The union already moves this block into `cake_trtllm_moe_allreduce_union_common.cuh` (52 lines). That header differs from the Ulysses copy only by `CakePeerPointerTable` and `<math_constants.h>`. The MNNVL file uses a different prelude and is out of scope.
- **Norm-combine bindings.** The three `csrc/cake_fused_norm_combine/*_binding.cu` (114 + 114 + 117 lines) differ only in:
  - the symbol;
  - block size (320 vs 160);
  - dynamic smem (10496 vs 128);
  - one cooperative launch attribute.

  `VARIANTS` (`flashinfer/jit/cake_fused_norm_combine.py:42-77`) already records these values. Only tests read `capacity_receipt` (line 75). `COMPILE_FLAGS = []` exists only to produce `use_fast_math=False`, and `gen_jit_spec` defaults to `True` (`flashinfer/jit/core.py:708,746-747`).
- **Exact-shape DCP and norm-combine.** The generated DCP path runs only when all of these hold; otherwise the helix kernel runs:
  - cp_size is 2 or 4;
  - partial rows are 128 × 2-byte with 2 × fp32 stats;
  - `DCP_A2A_CHANNEL_COUNT` is unset (`csrc/trtllm_dcp_alltoall.cu:40,159`).

  The two DCP kernels (394/345 lines) differ only in constants derived from cp_size, plus a cp2-only self-copy branch. Norm-combine requires world size 8, hidden 2560, bf16 and capability (10,0)/(10,3).
- **Dead host code.**
  - `flashinfer/jit/cake_moe_finalize_comm.py`: `WORLD_SIZES`/`DTYPES`/`OUTPUT_PROFILES`/`kernel_names` are unused, because the binding hard-codes the 12 symbols in `kKernels[2][3][2]`.
  - The union's `exported_arches()` and `cake_ulysses.supported_capabilities()` are called only by tests.
  - The `Route.kernel` tuple typing and `route_kernel` tuple branch (union loader `:81-87, 510-514`) are dead: all 60 routes name one kernel.
  - Line 7 of `cake_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion_binding.cu` still refers to `sm_100a/*_device.cu`, which no longer exists.
- **Host path.** Repeated per-call checks on the union path:
  - `_check_cake_moe_allreduce_arch` (`trtllm_ar.py:929-935`) calls `torch.cuda.get_device_capability` on every call, uncached.
  - The union loader (`:660-686`) re-checks world size, hidden dim, dtype, workspace and arch.
  - The launcher (`:95-121`) re-checks 9 tensors and calls `cudaGetDevice`.

  The finalize binding keeps its own sm_count and mutex+map occupancy caches. It passes a constant `v_scale_factor = 1.0f` (`:253`), and the kernels still multiply by it. `csrc/tvm_ffi_utils.h` has no shared SM-count helper; 57 csrc files re-implement it.
- **Tests and benchmarks.** About 530 test lines assert table or text structure:
  - `test_cake_moe_allreduce_union.py:48-165, 406-424`;
  - `test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall_fused_adapter.py:411-743`, which counts the 33 kernel definitions and exact `#define` strings in both MNNVL files;
  - `test_cake_fused_norm_combine.py:58-118`.

  `benchmarks/comm/bench_cake_ulysses_a2a.py:28` imports the 537-line shape fixture from `tests.comm`.

**Proposed steps**
- [ ] Delete `csrc/generated/mnnvl_moe_alltoall_sm103.cu` (1 file, −6,533 lines). In `flashinfer/jit/comm.py:309-312`, point both sm100a and sm103a at the remaining file, optionally renamed to `mnnvl_moe_alltoall.cu`. Update `tests/comm/test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall_fused_adapter.py:224,230` and the two-name loops at `:497-500` and `:703-705`. Confirm with a `cuobjdump --dump-sass` diff of `mnnvl_moe_alltoall_sm103a` on B300 and with the MPI tests in that file. The AOT module list does not change.
- [ ] Union: build each pipe clone group from one source, with `CAKE_UNION_MIN_BLOCKS` / `CAKE_UNION_UNROLL` / `CAKE_UNION_PIPE_DEPTH` passed through `kernel_defines()` (−2,006 lines):
  - `ws2_bf16_pipe.cu`: 3 × 454 → 454;
  - `ws2_f16_pipe.cu`: 2 × 448 → 448;
  - `ws8_bf16_pipe.cu`: 2 × 650 → 650.

  Keep every KERNELS/ROUTES name; `kernel_source()` (`:573-574`) reads a new `source` field. Update `test_cake_moe_allreduce_union.py:79-98, 406-424`. Confirm with per-(kernel, arch) SASS diffs of the 7 modules on B200/B300 and the distributed test at ws 2 and 8. If `__launch_bounds__(224, 5)` produces the same SASS as `(224)`, drop `ws2_bf16_pipe2_u4_b5` and `ws8_bf16_pipe1_u4_b5` outright (2 fewer routes).
- [ ] Norm-combine: replace the three `*_binding.cu` (345 lines) with one launcher parametrised by `-DCAKE_FNC_KERNEL/BLOCK/DYN_SMEM/COOPERATIVE` and built from `VARIANTS` (−230 lines). Drop `capacity_receipt` and `COMPILE_FLAGS` (`cake_fused_norm_combine.py:23,75,78,296,316-318,376`), but pass `use_fast_math=False` to `gen_jit_spec` explicitly, or the three kernel TUs change SASS. Update `test_cake_fused_norm_combine.py:93,97-99,350-353`. Confirm with a SASS diff of the three kernel modules and the 8-GPU `test_eight_peer_fused_norm_combine_matches_the_reference` on B200/B300.
- [ ] Move the inlined prelude of the Ulysses, DCP, norm-combine and finalize kernels into one shared header (about −1,000 lines). For example, `csrc/cake_prelude.cuh` = the union common header + `CakePeerPointerTable` + `<utility>`. Switch the 27 union kernels to it and delete the union-only header. Confirm with `nvcc -E` diffs of all 57 TUs (ignoring line markers) and per-module SASS diffs. Check that the DCP kernels' own `make_warp_uniform(uint32_t)` overload does not clash with the merged header.
- [ ] Remove the dead host code listed above, including the stale finalize binding comment (−34 lines). Switch `test_cake_moe_allreduce_union.py:172` to `union.ARCHES` and `test_cake_ulysses_a2a.py:70` to `target_capabilities()`. Drop the tuple-route helpers at `test_cake_moe_allreduce_union.py:44-45, 57-58, 324-328`.
- [ ] Union: fold `ws4_bf16_sm103_t1_t1_e8_serial_clear` into `ws4_bf16_wide_mlp` behind one more define, or have the exporter emit the pair as one program (−509 lines). Confirm with a SASS diff of the two ws4 bf16 modules on B300 and the distributed test at ws=4 bf16. Run a 1-32-token benchmark on GB300 to check that the recorded ≥2 % win holds.
- [ ] Ulysses: regenerate as 8 templated sources, one per (world_size, mode) (−3,242 lines). Each source gets `extern "C"` bf16/f16/f32 instantiations and a `VEC_WIDTH` constant (8 for 16-bit, 4 for f32). Keep the 24 symbols so `cake_ulysses_dispatch.cu` does not change, and cut `GENERATED_KERNEL_SOURCES` to 8 entries. Separately decide the fate of the 167 lines of bf16 performance-shape branches. Keeping them behind a per-dtype `#if` leaves SASS unchanged; dropping them means re-running `bench_cake_ulysses_a2a.py` on the four large bf16 rows. Run `test_cake_ulysses_a2a.py` at ws 2/4/6/8.
- [ ] Make the union, Ulysses and ws4 dedups in the Cake exporter, not by hand-editing generated text, or the next regeneration overwrites them (as #6545 did with the MNNVL files). It is still open whether the exporter can emit `-D`-parametrised and dtype-templated programs. The union launcher and #5870's single templated finalize source are precedents.
- [ ] Union host path: keep one Python validator, either in `trtllm_ar.py` or in `run_cake_moe_allreduce_union` (about −60 lines, medium confidence). Cache the capability query in `_check_cake_moe_allreduce_arch`. In the finalize binding, fold the constant `scale_factor` at the next regeneration and keep or share its caches; a shared helper does not exist yet and would need to be created. The negative-path tests in `test_cake_moe_allreduce_api.py` / `test_cake_moe_allreduce_union.py` check exact `ValueError` messages raised before module load. If `scale_factor` is folded, confirm with a finalize SASS diff.
- [ ] Add a union benchmark built from the `test_cake_moe_allreduce_distributed.py` rows: experts 8/12/16 × five token bands × ws 2/4/8 × bf16/f16 × PDL, on B200 and B300.
- [ ] Decision (not counted below): keep or retire the 18 exact-expert union specializations (9,507 lines; the kernels of 30 routes). If they are retired, every (arch, ws, dtype, pdl) class runs its class program and `ROUTES` shrinks from 60 to 24. This needs the benchmark above, since a SASS diff cannot settle it. `test_cake_moe_allreduce_distributed.py:42-49, 467-476` derive rows from `_SPECIALIZATION_RULES` and must change in the same PR.

**Expected size:** about 37.4K lines of kernel and binding source → about 27.6K after the mechanical steps (−9.8K) → about 23.8K after the structural steps (−13.6K). Retiring the exact-expert specializations would remove up to 9.5K more.

title: feat(comm): add experimental allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm
body:
## 📌 Description Adds an **experimental** fused kernel, `flashinfer.comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm`, that performs the tensor-parallel MNNVL one-shot all-reduce **and** the mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connection) post-map + pre-norm partials in a single launch. It targets the decode path of **GLM-5.3-Flash** served with TP8 on Blackwell MNNVL systems (e.g. two 4-GPU GB300 trays). ### Where it is used GLM-5.3-Flash replaces the single residual stream with **4 mHC residual streams** (hidden 4096). After every attention and every MoE/MLP sublayer, the row-parallel sublayer output has to be all-reduced across the 8 TP ranks, mixed into the 4 residual streams (mHC *post*), and projected for the next sublayer's mHC *pre* mapping (24 mix logits = 4 pre + 4 post + 16 comb). In a decode step this boundary runs **89 times** (every sublayer boundary except the last one, whose all-reduce feeds the final mHC post). At decode batch sizes (1 to 32 tokens) each of these steps is tiny and latency-bound, so the boundary is dominated by launch and synchronization cost rather than math. ### What is fused One sublayer boundary, on each of the 8 GPUs. The two red kernels (dashed box) are merged into the one green kernel; the gray steps do not change. ```mermaid %%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 420, "nodeSpacing": 40, "rankSpacing": 40}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph BEFORE["Before: 3 kernels per boundary"] direction TB b0["Sublayer output
(this GPU's partial sum)"] subgraph MERGED[" "] direction TB b1["Kernel 1: all-reduce
sum the partials of all 8 GPUs → x"] b2["Kernel 2: mHC post + pre-norm partials
mix x into the 4 residual streams,
start the next sublayer's projection"] b1 -->|"x written to HBM,
then read back"| b2 end b3["Kernel 3: mHC pre finalize
(Sinkhorn + RMSNorm)"] b4["Next sublayer"] b0 --> b1 b2 --> b3 --> b4 end subgraph AFTER["After: 2 kernels per boundary"] direction TB a0["Sublayer output
(this GPU's partial sum)"] a1["Fused kernel: allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm
sum the partials of all 8 GPUs → x
(x stays in registers)
then mHC post + pre-norm partials"] a3["Kernel 3: mHC pre finalize
(unchanged)"] a4["Next sublayer"] a0 --> a1 --> a3 --> a4 end BEFORE ~~~ AFTER classDef removed fill:#f8d7da,stroke:#b02a37,color:#000 classDef fused fill:#d1e7dd,stroke:#146c43,stroke-width:2px,color:#000 classDef same fill:#f1f3f5,stroke:#868e96,color:#000 class b1,b2 removed class a1 fused class b0,b3,b4,a0,a3,a4 same style BEFORE fill:#ffffff,stroke:#adb5bd style AFTER fill:#ffffff,stroke:#adb5bd style MERGED fill:#fff5f5,stroke:#b02a37,stroke-dasharray: 5 5 ``` Inside the fused kernel: steps ① and ② are the unchanged stock one-shot all-reduce, and steps ③ and ④ are the old kernel 2, now run as an epilogue on `x` while it is still in registers. ```mermaid %%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 420}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph AR["from Kernel 1 (stock one-shot all-reduce, unchanged)"] direction LR s1["① write this GPU's partial
to the 7 peers over NVLink"] s2["② wait for all 8 partials,
sum in fp32 in rank order → x"] s1 --> s2 end subgraph EPI["from Kernel 2 (now an epilogue on x in registers)"] direction LR s3["③ mHC post
new_r = post·x + comb·residual
→ residual_out (bf16)"] s4["④ pre-norm partials
yp = fn·new_r, rp = Σ new_r²"] s3 --> s4 end s2 --> s3 classDef ar fill:#f1f3f5,stroke:#868e96,color:#000 classDef epi fill:#d1e7dd,stroke:#146c43,color:#000 class s1,s2 ar class s3,s4 epi style AR fill:#ffffff,stroke:#adb5bd style EPI fill:#ffffff,stroke:#146c43 ``` Per token `m`, with `x` the all-reduced sublayer output: ``` new_r[m, j] = post_layer_mix[m, j] * x[m] + sum_k comb_res_mix[m, k, j] * residual[m, k] (fp32) residual_out = bf16(new_r) yp[s, m, n] = sum_{j, h in split s} fn[n, j*H + h] * new_r[m, j, h] (8 splits of H/8) rp[s, m] = sum_{j, h in split s} new_r[m, j, h]^2 ``` The fused kernel removes one launch (one CUDA-graph node) per boundary, the HBM round trip of `x`, and the second kernel's fixed latency. ### Design - **Same all-reduce, bit-identical.** The kernel uses the stock MNNVL one-shot Lamport protocol and the same `MNNVLAllReduceFusionWorkspace` (buffers, flags, rotation, clearing), so it interleaves freely with `trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce` on one workspace. The reduction is fp32 in rank order with one bf16 rounding, identical to `oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`. - **Epilogue in registers.** After the peer reduction, each CTA applies the post-map to its hidden slice and accumulates the `yp` / `rp` split-K partials in fp32. Seven token-count-specialized kernels cover T = 1..32; every grid stays co-resident so the Lamport polling cannot deadlock. - **Numerics.** No fast-math (`use_fast_math=False`, no `.ftz` in PTX). `residual_out` is bit-exact against an fp32 reference; `yp` / `rp` differ only by fp32 summation order. - **CUDA-graph safe.** `allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_prepare()` builds the JIT module outside graph capture; `allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_supported()` lets a caller check whether a call takes the fused path. Outside the supported surface the API falls back to the stock all-reduce plus a PyTorch epilogue with the same outputs. ### Experimental scope - **Experimental API and backend.** Core holds only a thin `@flashinfer_experimental_api` entry point in `flashinfer/comm/allreduce_mhc.py`; the kernels, JIT spec, support checks and fallback live in `flashinfer/experimental/allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm/`. JIT-only, nothing in `aot.py`. - **Opt-in:** calling the API is the opt-in. It takes no part in automatic backend selection, dispatch, autotuning or trace-apply. - **Supported surface:** world size 8 on one MNNVL domain, hidden 4096, 4 residual streams, bf16, 1 to 32 tokens, SM100 / SM103. ```python import flashinfer.comm as comm comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_prepare(...) # once, outside CUDA-graph capture if comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm_supported(...): yp, rp, residual_out = comm.allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm( input, residual, post_layer_mix, comb_res_mix, fn, workspace) ``` See `examples/experimental/allreduce_mhc_post_prenorm.py` for a runnable 8-rank example (`torchrun --nnodes 2 --nproc-per-node 4 ...`). ### Kernel-level results 8x GB300 (two trays, MNNVL), CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer main. Unfused = MNNVL one-shot all-reduce + the TileLang mHC post-map / pre-norm kernel used by the serving stack. Each variant is a CUDA graph of 90 back-to-back boundaries; microseconds per boundary, max over the 8 ranks, the two graphs replayed alternately in one process. | tokens (T) | unfused (µs) | fused (µs) | saved (µs) | speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 10.91 | 5.40 | 5.51 | **2.02x** | | 2 | 11.88 | 6.17 | 5.71 | 1.93x | | 4 | 11.82 | 5.83 | 5.99 | 2.03x | | 8 | 12.31 | 7.05 | 5.26 | 1.75x | | 16 | 12.84 | 7.75 | 5.09 | 1.66x | | 24 | 14.09 | 9.26 | 4.83 | 1.52x | | 32 | 14.32 | 9.66 | 4.66 | 1.48x | - Faster at every token count 1..32: **1.48x to 2.05x**, 4.7 to 7.7 µs saved per boundary. - **1.86x** weighted by GLM-5.3-Flash's decode token-count mix (1.91x when each graph is timed alone). - The all-reduce output and `residual_out` are bit-exact; `yp` / `rp` stay within 0.13 / 0.02 of the fp32 tolerance; 280/280 fused calls interleaved with stock all-reduces on one workspace are exact. Inside the model (CUDA-graph replay at T = 1, one boundary): ``` unfused all-reduce ████████████████████ 4.93 µs + post/pre-norm ███████████████████████ 5.86 µs = 10.78 µs fused ████████████████████████ 6.02 µs ``` Per decode step that is 89 boundaries x ~5.5 µs ≈ 0.49 ms, and 89 fewer CUDA-graph nodes (1372 → 1283). ### End-to-end results GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 on vLLM, TP8 across two GB300 trays (MNNVL), CUDA graphs, multi-turn conversation trace replay (~30 min per point). Baseline: the same vLLM with stock FlashInfer main. | | c=1 baseline | c=1 fused | Δ | c=8 baseline | c=8 fused | Δ | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | mean ITL (ms) | 4.401 | 3.964 | **−9.9%** | 5.636 | 5.052 | **−10.4%** | | p50 ITL (ms) | 4.583 | 4.165 | −9.1% | 5.439 | 4.894 | −10.0% | | p90 ITL (ms) | 5.068 | 4.568 | −9.9% | 7.105 | 6.242 | −12.1% | | p99 ITL (ms) | 6.077 | 5.790 | −4.7% | 9.418 | 8.283 | −12.1% | | output tok/s | 123.5 | 129.6 | +5.0% | 348.8 | 349.4 | +0.2% ¹ | | mean TTFT (ms) | 660 | 655 | −0.8% | 487 | 518 | +6.4% ² | - Median decode step is **0.43 to 0.50 ms shorter** at every batch size, matching the kernel-level projection. With the fused path disabled in the same build the numbers match the baseline within run-to-run drift. - ¹ At c=8 the replay is demand-bound, so throughput cannot rise; latency is the signal. - ² Mean TTFT at c=8 is pulled up by a few requests beyond p99; median (388 vs 416 ms) and p90 are not worse. Prefill does not use this kernel; the cause is not isolated yet. ## 🔍 Related Issues ## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete. ### ✅ Pre-commit Checks - [ ] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method). - [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`. - [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues. > If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/). ## 🧪 Tests - [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed. - [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.). ## 🔬 Experimental Track - [x] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: # - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release. - [x] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff). - [x] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included. - [x] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.) - [x] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows. ```experimental-tests # One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not # supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under # tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g. # # tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py # tests/experimental/my_backend/ # # Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every # experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell. ``` ## Reviewer Notes ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added an experimental fused all-reduce operation that combines mHC post-map and pre-norm processing for supported hardware and input configurations. * When the fused operation is unavailable, processing uses standard all-reduce followed by PyTorch operations. * Added an example and guidance on hardware requirements and preparation for CUDA graph capture.

title: [Tracking] Deslop Cake-generated kernels (smaller, reviewable generated code)
body:
## Background

Many kernels generated by Cake have been upstreamed into FlashInfer over the past months. They live in `csrc/cake_*`, `flashinfer/experimental/*`, and parts of `csrc/kda`, `csrc/gdn`, and `csrc/fused_moe`. The kernels are fast, but the way they are delivered does not meet the software-engineering bar of the rest of the library:

- The 244 PRs from the automated export account added about 8.0M lines and removed about 1.5M. The files those PRs added that are still on `main` come to 4,441 files and 4.9M lines. Of those, 3,522 are C++/CUDA/PTX files with 4.1M lines.
- A single PR routinely adds 10^4–10^5 lines. Examples: #5523 (+466K), #5697 (+178K), #5183 (+162K), #5684 (+157K / −77K), and #5694 (+142K / −17K).
- These PRs cannot really be reviewed. They also bloat the source distribution and the JIT cache, and they make regressions hard to bisect.

## What is wrong

Examples below are from `main` at 45d35e4e7.

1. **Unused kernel instances.** Some sources are never registered, or cannot be reached from any dispatch path. Superseded generations were never deleted.
2. **Near-duplicate kernels in separate files.** For example, `csrc/cake_trtllm_moe_allreduce_union` has 322 kernel files. After normalising the generated hash names and the architecture tag, only 48 distinct bodies remain.
3. **Per-architecture copies.** Several families keep SM100a and SM103a trees that are identical or differ by a line or two. For example, in `flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_latent_moe` each SM100a/SM103a kernel pair differs only in the symbol name and one shared-memory address-conversion line.
4. **Problem sizes and launch configs baked in as constants.** For example, `csrc/cake_minimax_h3_mxfp8_pre_attention` has 176 kernel files. That is 2 schedules × 44 values of `#define M` × 2 architectures.
5. **Hard-coded strides and contiguity.** These force `.contiguous()` copies on the Python side, or make the op reject views.
6. **Host overhead.**
   - The Python hot path does per-call device-property queries, workspace allocations, tensor construction, and dict/string work.
   - Generated C++ bindings carry their own device-guard classes, mutexes, and caches instead of using `tvm_ffi_utils.h`.
7. **Other bloat.** Multi-thousand-line generated Python registries and dispatch tables, per-architecture generated dispatchers, large metadata JSON files, raw PTX blobs, and README benchmark dumps.

## Plan

There are two tracks.

**Fix the generator and exporter so new exports are lean by construction.**

- One source per schedule, shared across architectures. Architecture differences go behind `__CUDA_ARCH__` guards only where they are real.
- Runtime problem sizes and strides instead of per-shape clones.
- Only export the instances that dispatch can reach.
- Emit identical bodies once.
- Keep bindings thin and built on `tvm_ffi_utils.h`.
- Cache host-side planning, with no syncs or allocations on the hot path.
- Add export-time checks that reject all of the patterns above.

**Clean up what is already on `main`, family by family.** Each task gets a sub-issue below with measured findings and a concrete plan. Cleanup PRs follow these rules:

- **Mechanical steps**: deleting unreachable sources, merging per-architecture copies, and deduplicating identical bodies.
  - They change neither behaviour nor performance.
  - Equivalence is shown by comparing the compiled SASS before and after, in addition to the existing tests.
- **Structural steps**: runtime shapes and strides, and consolidating clones into one template.
  - These are regenerated by the exporter, not edited by hand.
  - They come with per-shape before/after benchmarks.
- Every PR is small enough to review, and has a negative net line count.

Sub-issues are added below as each family's analysis completes.

title: [CPU][Xeon6] Scope RedHatAI FP8 variants to validated hardware
body:
## Summary

Extend the variant-level hardware scoping introduced in #1029 to additional RedHatAI FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints.

The Xeon nightly recipe validation identified seven RedHatAI FP8 variants that failed during model startup. These variants were exposed because their parent recipes declare `xeon6: verified`, even though the specific checkpoints were not validated successfully on Xeon.

This PR adds explicit `supported_hardware` declarations to prevent unsupported variants from being selected for Xeon validation.

## Changes

- Add variant-level `supported_hardware` to 11 RedHatAI FP8/NVFP4 variants across five recipes.
- Restrict the seven failing FP8 variants to hardware already marked `verified` in their parent recipes, excluding Xeon.
- Preserve Xeon eligibility for the two RedHatAI FP8-block variants that passed validation.
- Ensure every new `supported_hardware` entry is a subset of the parent recipe's verified hardware list.
- Preserve existing BF16, INT8, INT4, and previously scoped variants.
- Do not introduce new hardware support.

Affected recipes:

| Recipe | Variants updated |
|---|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 3 |
| Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct | 3 |
| Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct | 3 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct | 1 |
| Qwen3-4B | 1 |

The Llama 3.1 NVFP4 variant is left unchanged because its intended Blackwell targets are not included in the parent recipe's verified hardware list.

## Validation


Baseline results:
- 47 recipes tested.
- 40 passed.
- 7 failed during model startup, all RedHatAI FP8 checkpoints.
- Two additional RedHatAI FP8-block variants passed and remain Xeon-eligible.

Patch checks:
- All 11 new variant hardware declarations are subsets of their parent recipes' verified hardware lists.
- No existing variant-level hardware declarations are modified.

A follow-up nightly validation is required to confirm the updated Xeon discovery results and pass rate.

## Motivation

PR #1029 introduced variant-level hardware scoping to prevent model-level `xeon6: verified` from implicitly enabling unsupported checkpoint variants.

This PR closes the remaining gap for RedHatAI FP8 variants while retaining checkpoints that passed Xeon validation.

The change is limited to recipe metadata and does not modify vLLM runtime behavior.

body:
## Summary

Adds [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) (2026-10-17 weight update) to the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe and makes it the default variant, mirroring how DeepSeek-V4-Pro rolled its 0813 release forward.

- `default` → `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, pill **FP8 (1017)**
- new `fp8` variant → the 2026-09-09 launch checkpoint (recipe's own repo), pill **FP8 (0909)**, kept for reproducing earlier results
- Both variants share the H100 (Engram CPU offload) and DGX Station (expert offload) per-GPU overrides via a YAML anchor
- Guide: new *Checkpoints* section; client examples (reasoning snippet, Verifying curl) use the 1017 model id; 1017 model card added to References
- `date_updated: 2026-10-17`

## Why a variant swap is safe

Compared the two HF repos:
- `config.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `encoding/` and `inference/config.json` are byte-identical
- `model.safetensors.index.json`: same 96,085 tensors, same 510.3 GB total
- 1017 ships no `chat_template.jinja` — not needed, since `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41` (already in `base_args`) encodes prompts in vLLM's Python encoder

So the generated commands are identical apart from the model id (checked on H100, GB200, DGX Station GB300, MI355X).

## Install: pip wheel, no nightly

vLLM 0.30.0 registers `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` and the `deepseek_v41` tokenizer; 0.31.0 adds the KV-offload fix (#57145) and the ROCm Engram host-memory gate (#57491). Checked against the `v0.31.0` tree: every flag the NVIDIA commands emit (`--engram-config`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` / `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, `--kernel-config`, `--prefill-schedule-interval`, `--offload-backend`/`--cpu-offload-params`, the DSpark adaptive-verification config) is present, and the Rust frontend registers the `deepseek_v41` parsers.

- `min_vllm_version: "0.31.0"`; drop `nightly_required` and `install.pip: false` → pip tab + `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` on NVIDIA
- AMD Docker stays on `nightly-rocm100` (the verified image). **MI355X hides pip** (`install.pip: false` per GPU): `--monokernel` (#60397/#61082), the ROCm MXFP4 indexer (#58671) and Gluon sparse MLA (#53492) are on main but not in 0.31.0. MI300X/MI325X/MI350X can use the ROCm wheel — 0.31.0 force-disables SWA bounded replay on ROCm, so the pre-#59039 prefix-hit fault does not apply.
- Prerequisites, KV offloading and the DGX Station note updated accordingly

## Caveat

`meta.hardware` verified badges and the measured numbers in the guide (MI355X benchmark, KV offloading validation) were taken on the 0909 checkpoint; the guide states this explicitly. The 1017 weights have not been separately re-run.

## Validation

- `node scripts/build-recipes-api.mjs` — ✓ 213 models
- `pnpm test:schema` — pass
- `pnpm test:overlay` — pass

title: perf: add push-based allreduce for small tensor reductions
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a push-based 2-buffer allreduce protocol to vLLM, targeting small-message reductions during decode (e.g., the per-layer attention and MoE allreduces in DeepSeek-V4 models). The existing barrier-based `CustomAllreduce` uses two explicit cross-GPU NVLink barrier round-trips per call, which dominate latency for small tensors. The push protocol eliminates these barriers entirely by having each rank push its data to all remote GPUs via NVLink volatile stores and then polling locally for arrival using a positive-zero sentinel mechanism with double-buffered epoch alternation.

The new `PushAllReduce` communicator is inserted into the `CudaCommunicator` dispatch chain above the existing `CustomAllreduce` for messages below a dynamic size threshold (~720 KB at TP=8 on B200). Messages above this threshold continue to use the barrier-based path. No existing `CustomAllreduce` code is modified. The implementation includes a consolidated CUDA kernel header vendored from SGLang's proven push kernel with minimal macro substitutions (namespace, C++17 compatibility, AOT compilation guards), a C++ host-side manager class following vLLM patterns, torch custom op bindings, and a Python communicator wrapper with CUDA graph support.

The kernel uses all available SMs (vs 2 CTAs in the barrier-based approach), supports PDL (`griddepcontrol`) overlap on sm_90+ architectures, and avoids the `cudaMemcpy` to IPC staging buffer required by the barrier-based path in eager mode. CUDA graph safety is ensured by placing the epoch counter in device memory (read live during replay) with a fixed grid size equal to the SM count.

## Performance Results

| Configuration | Metric | Baseline | Patched | Delta | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | Throughput (tok/s) | 82.301 | 84.060 | +1.759 | **+2.14%** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | TPOT (ms/tok) | 12.152 | 11.897 | -0.255 | **-2.09%** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | Throughput (tok/s) | 127.035 | 130.905 | +3.870 | **+3.05%** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | TPOT (ms/tok) | 7.873 | 7.640 | -0.233 | **-2.96%** |

Workload: decode, BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=33024, KV cache FP8. Baseline = same patched code with push allreduce disabled via env var (falls back to barrier-based `CustomAllreduce`).

Per-call improvement on V4-Pro (122 allreduce calls per forward pass across 61 layers): ~2.09 us/call.

## Correctness (lm_eval)

| Configuration | Metric | Baseline | Patched | Delta | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | flexible-extract exact_match | 0.9515 | 0.9530 | +0.0015 | PASS |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro (8xB200, TP=8) | strict-match exact_match | 0.9515 | 0.9538 | +0.0023 | PASS |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | flexible-extract exact_match | 0.9598 | 0.9530 | -0.0068 | PASS |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (2xB200, TP=2) | strict-match exact_match | 0.9606 | 0.9530 | -0.0076 | PASS |

Benchmark: gsm8k 5-shot (1319 prompts). All deltas are within 1 standard error (~0.006) and statistically indistinguishable (z-scores < 1.96). The sign reversal between configurations confirms random variance, not a systematic shift.

## Feature Toggle

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Environment variable | `VLLM_DISABLE_PUSH_ALLREDUCE` |
| Disable command | `VLLM_DISABLE_PUSH_ALLREDUCE=1` |
| Startup log (enabled) | `AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is ENABLED` |
| Startup log (disabled) | `AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is DISABLED (env override)` |

When disabled, `PushAllReduce.__init__` returns immediately without allocating any GPU resources. `should_use()` returns `False` for all inputs, and `CudaCommunicator` falls through to the barrier-based `CustomAllreduce`.

## Test Coverage

24 tests included in the patch, all passing on 2x NVIDIA B200:

- **Unit tests (16):** build verification, initialization/IPC exchange, `should_use()` predicate logic, bit-exact integer correctness vs NCCL, float correctness, positive-zero sentinel handling, 1000-call epoch alternation, thread count selection, threshold boundary, out-of-place semantics, dtype coverage (fp16/bf16/fp32), multi-layer simulation (122 ARs x 3 steps), lifecycle/cleanup, warmup path, asymmetric rank data, identical-values edge case
- **Integration tests (3):** dispatch priority routing (small->push, large->fallback), coexistence with existing allreduce backends, interleaved push AR + NCCL operations
- **CUDA graph test (1):** graph capture + 10 replays with varying data, epoch counter correctness
- **E2E test (1):** transformer block simulation (61 blocks x 2 ARs x 2 decode steps)
- **Feature toggle tests (3):** enabled default, disabled via env var, non-"1" values do not disable

title: [Bugfix] Don't sync-police or retry FlashInfer all-reduce workspace creation in eager mode
body:
## Purpose

Fix a nightly regression from #58197 ("[Core] Disable JIT warmup in eager mode").

With `--enforce-eager` the V2 `warmup_kernels` dummy forward is now skipped. The standalone FlashInfer all-reduce (`FlashInferAllReduce`, enabled by default through `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`) creates its workspace lazily. The profile run uses large tensors that are above the FlashInfer size cap (e.g. 0.5 MB at TP8 or 2 MB at TP4 on H200), so it never touches the workspace. As a result, the workspace is first created inside the first real `execute_model`, which runs after `enable_gpu_sync_check()`. In CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`), `flashinfer_comm.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(...)` then raises `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` part-way through a collective. The failure is caught and returns `None`, and `get_fi_ar_workspace` does not remember it. The mnnvl attempt fails, the trtllm fallback fails, and the collective creation keeps getting retried. Each retry leaks partially created buffers, which leads to CUDA OOM, then a deadlock, then `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out` and `EngineDeadError`.

Evidence (nightly build 90589):
- H200 LM Eval DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 (`--enforce-eager`): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90589#01a0ccda-d861-443c-bcb5-9c8b22260601. At 11:45:56 it logs `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected`, followed by repeated `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. OOM follows by 11:46:18 and the RPC timeout at 11:50:53.
- B200 HiSparse (GLM-5.2-NVFP4 TP4), job `01a0cd35-9fed-4cff-a2be-b8c4ea5fb773` in the same build, fails the same way.
- Passing build 90513 (before #58197) logs `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during warmup.
- This is likely also behind the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E failure (`rank 0 did not report UNHEALTHY within 45s`) that #58318 is bisecting. That link is not verified.

## Fix

In `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py`:
1. Wrap the one-time `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace` call in `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This covers both the regular and the quant workspace paths, since both go through `_create_workspace`. Setup syncs are expected here and are not a per-step cost.
2. Remember a failed creation (`_fi_ar_workspace_failed` / `_fi_ar_quant_workspace_failed`) so a collective creation is never retried on every all-reduce call. `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()` resets both flags.

I also considered creating the workspace eagerly before `enable_gpu_sync_check()` when warmup is skipped. That approach would have to guess the hidden size and dtype in the worker. It would also leave the retry-storm failure mode in place for any other lazy-creation failure. The change above is smaller and local to the module that owns the workspace.

## Not a duplicate

- `gh pr list --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce workspace"`, `"58197"`, `"gpu_sync_allowed"`, `"flashinfer allreduce eager"` and `"enforce-eager warmup"` returned no PR that fixes this.
- #58318 is a DNM CI-bisect probe that reverts #58197. It is not a fix.

## Test Plan / Results

GPU checks ran on an idle 8×H200 host (GPUs 0-3), using the nightly image `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:de6674b0023b...` (the same image as build 90589). For "after", the patched file was mounted over the installed one. At that commit the file is identical to current `main`.

Repro: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", tensor_parallel_size=4, enforce_eager=True)`, 3× `generate` of 4 prompts. TP4 puts the FlashInfer cap at 2 MB, so the profile run skips it, which matches the CI case.
- **Before:** `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: GPU<->CPU sync detected` (mnnvl, then trtllm), then `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=trtllm`. Generation still finished because this small model falls back to other all-reduce backends, so the full OOM/deadlock cascade seen with DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 did not reproduce here.
- **After:** `Initialized FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` during the first step. No sync errors, and output is correct (`' Paris. ...'`).

Unit tests, run in the same image with the patched files mounted:
```
pytest distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer or checkpoints"
14 passed, 17 deselected
```
The new `test_flashinfer_workspace_failure_is_not_retried` checks that a failing creation runs once (mnnvl plus the trtllm fallback) across repeated calls and runs again after `destroy_fi_ar_workspace()`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.

Not verified: the full DeepSeek V3.2 TP8 and GLM-5.2 HiSparse CI jobs themselves, and the H100 Fault Tolerance E2E job.

title: [Distributed] Island-aware hierarchical allreduce for PCIe-only multi-island boxes
body:
## Purpose

On PCIe-only boxes whose GPUs form multiple islands — e.g. 2×4 A100/A800, where GPU0-3 and GPU4-7 are each PIX-connected and the two halves are bridged by the CPU interconnect — `CustomAllreduce` is unavailable (`is_fully_connected` is false) and every allreduce falls to the NCCL ring, which crosses the slow inter-island link repeatedly. Profiling DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 decode on an 8×A800 box put **allreduce at 68.6% of decode GPU time** (292 µs/call at decode shapes), far ahead of attention (2.3%) or the MoE GEMMs.

This adds an opt-in island-aware communicator. It is off unless the operator supplies an explicit island partition, so nothing changes for existing deployments.

## Design

Enabled with `VLLM_HIER_ALL_REDUCE="0,1,2,3;4,5,6,7"`. Two Triton kernels share one set of IPC-registered buffers and dispatch on message size:

- **one-shot** (< 24576 elements): publish the input, reduce the island over direct P2P reads, then one cross-island exchange. Two sync rounds, 4n remote bytes.
- **two-shot** (≥ 24576): reduce-scatter within the island, exchange only the `1/island_size` shard across islands, allgather. Three sync rounds, 7n/4 remote bytes — and only `n/island_size` crosses the slow link instead of `n`.

Three details are load-bearing and worth calling out for review:

1. **Push-based signalling.** PCIe has no native remote atomics, and having a reader poll a remote flag costs a PCIe round trip per spin. Writers instead store sequence tokens into the *reader's* local flag array and readers spin on local memory only, with `fence.acq_rel.sys` for ordering. Same shape as the existing CUDA custom-allreduce kernels.
2. **Device-side sequence counters.** A host-supplied token would be baked into a CUDA graph and replay out of order, so the token comes from a device-side fetch-and-increment. Buffers then alternate by token parity, which makes it impossible for a rank that has lapped a slow peer to overwrite data the peer is still reading (a two-call lap is blocked by the flag waits).
3. **Stripe CTA partitioning in the two-shot kernel.** CTA *k* owns slice *k* of *every* shard rather than one contiguous range, so a reader CTA always waits on the same CTA index of its peers across all three phases. That removes the need for a grid-wide barrier, which Triton has no primitive for.

Note the IPC buffers are allocated and mapped through `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` with the importing device current, rather than via torch's `_new_shared_cuda`: torch opens IPC handles inside the *owner's* device context, so the mapping is never made peer-accessible to the importing device's kernels — `copy_()` works but a kernel dereference is an immediate IMA, and `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess` does not retroactively fix an already-imported handle.

## Not a duplicate of

- **#36834 (Added Hierarchical all reduce)** — that is a *node-level* hierarchy for multi-node inference: intra-node NVLink custom allreduce plus inter-node RDMA through UCCL-EP. This PR is single-node and hierarchical *within* the box, over PCIe islands, on hardware that has no NVLink at all. No overlap in code or target.
- **#44891 (push-based allreduce for small tensor reductions)** — shares the push/poll idea but is a flat (non-hierarchical) protocol in CUDA C++ targeting NVLink (threshold tuned on B200). This is a two-level algorithm in Triton for PCIe-island topologies. They compose: that PR's dispatch entry is above `CustomAllreduce`, this one is likewise independent and gated behind an explicit env.
- **#39633 (Fix PCIe custom-allreduce eligibility on >2 GPU topologies)** — that reuses the *existing* barrier-based kernel on PCIe. I tried exactly that on this hardware first (the P2P access matrix is fully connected here, so the NVLink-only gate looked like policy rather than capability). It runs at 21 µs but returns **numerically wrong results** at `world_size=8` (max error 1.5 to `inf` against an NCCL reference), so I abandoned that route and wrote a separate kernel instead. Details posted on that PR — it may be worth verifying on SM120 before enabling.

## Test plan

New `tests/distributed/test_hier_all_reduce.py` checks the communicator against `torch.distributed.all_reduce` across sizes that straddle the one-shot/two-shot threshold in both directions, plus a size that is not a multiple of the CTA tiling to exercise the masked tails. Each size runs twice so both parity buffers are used.

```
$ pytest tests/distributed/test_hier_all_reduce.py -q
2 passed, 14 warnings in 64.69s
```
(`tp_size` 2 and 4 on an 8×A800 node.)

Standalone correctness/latency sweep against NCCL, bf16, 8×A800, max error ≤ 0.016 at every size (bf16 reduction-order tolerance), µs/call:

| size | NCCL | one-shot | two-shot |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8KB | 56.9 | **46.5** | 47.5 |
| 32KB | 95.8 | **45.6** | 47.3 |
| 48KB | 64.7 | 54.3 | **49.6** |
| 64KB | **49.8** | 64.5 | 52.9 |
| 128KB | 132.2 | 102.2 | **66.7** |
| 256KB | 169.4 | 174.8 | **91.2** |
| 512KB | 160.4 | 324.2 | **143.0** |

64KB is the one point where NCCL still wins; I left the dispatch alone rather than special-casing around a single measurement.

## Serving results

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 8×A800, TP=8, EP, fp8 KV, `vllm bench serve` with in 2048 / out 512, toggling only `VLLM_HIER_ALL_REDUCE`:

| config | concurrency | on | off | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DSpark spec decode, `max_num_seqs=16` | 1 | 101.3 | 90.2 tok/s | **+12.4%** |
| | 8 | 356.2 | 315.5 tok/s | **+12.9%** |
| no spec decode, `max_num_seqs=64` | 16 | 402.9 | 384.0 tok/s | +4.9% |
| | 32 | 690.6 | 609.1 tok/s | **+13.4%** |
| | 64 | 911.1 | 845.8 tok/s | +7.7% |

Peak output throughput goes 846 → 911 tok/s. The gain tracks message size: the payload is `batch × hidden × 2` bytes, so concurrency 16/32/64 lands near 128/256/512KB, matching the kernel table above.

Accuracy is unaffected (the op is a drop-in allreduce). As an end-to-end sanity run, the same stack completed Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks, 18.4 hours, 13,264 requests, 200.7M prompt + 5.5M generated tokens) with no crashes and no numerical corruption.

## Notes

- Opt-in only; when `VLLM_HIER_ALL_REDUCE` is unset the dispatch chain is unchanged.
- Requires exactly two equal islands and bf16 input; anything else falls through to the existing backends.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change.

title: perf: port push-based 2-buffer allreduce from SGLang
body:
## Summary

Port SGLang's push-based 2-buffer allreduce protocol into vLLM as a new collective communication backend for small tensor reductions. The push protocol eliminates 2 explicit NVLink barrier round-trips per allreduce call by using a push-based data arrival detection mechanism (positive-zero sentinel) with a 2-buffer epoch alternation scheme.

The new `PushAllReduce` communicator is inserted into `CudaCommunicator`'s dispatch priority above the existing barrier-based `CustomAllreduce` for messages below a configurable size threshold (720 KB for TP=8 on B200). For DeepSeek-V4-Pro decode (BS=1, TP=8, 8x B200), all 122 allreduce calls per forward pass (14,336 bytes each) use the push protocol.

This implements improvement plan step I2 from cross-trace analysis comparing vLLM and SGLang allreduce performance on DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 8x NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

### Key Design Decisions
- CUDA kernel vendored from SGLang with minimal macro substitutions (no SGLang dependencies)
- No modification to existing `CustomAllreduce` code paths
- CUDA graph safe: epoch counter in device memory, fixed grid size = SM count
- No `cudaMemcpy` in eager mode (performance advantage over barrier-based approach)
- PDL (`griddepcontrol`) runtime dispatch for sm90+ GPUs (Blackwell/Hopper)
- Out-of-place semantics matching vLLM convention

### Files Changed
- **New** (6): `push_all_reduce_kernel.cuh`, `push_all_reduce.cuh`, `push_all_reduce.cu`, `push_all_reduce.py`, `test_push_all_reduce.py`, `_test_push_ar_worker.py`
- **Modified** (5): `CMakeLists.txt`, `torch_bindings.cpp`, `_custom_ops.py`, `cuda_communicator.py`, `parallel_state.py`

## Performance Results

Benchmarked on DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 8x NVIDIA B200 (TP=8), BS=1, ISL=4, OSL=33024:

| Metric | Patched (enabled) | Baseline (disabled) | Delta | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (tokens/s) | 84.060 | 82.301 | +1.759 | **+2.14%** |
| Output tokens/s | 84.05 | 82.29 | +1.76 | **+2.14%** |
| Elapsed time (s) | 392.912 | 401.308 | -8.396 | **-2.09%** |
| Derived TPOT (ms/token) | 11.897 | 12.152 | -0.255 | **-2.09%** |

TTFT is not separately reported; with ISL=4 (single prefill step), TTFT is negligible (~10-20 ms) and identical between runs.

The baseline uses the same patched code with the feature disabled via env var (`VLLM_DISABLE_AUTO_PERF_PLAN_2=1`), falling back to barrier-based `CustomAllreduce`.

## Correctness (lm_eval)

lm_eval gsm8k 5-shot (1319 prompts), DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP=2 (identical architecture):

| Metric | Enabled | Disabled | Delta | Within Tolerance? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flexible-extract exact_match | 0.9530 | 0.9515 | +0.0015 | YES (< 0.005) |
| strict-match exact_match | 0.9538 | 0.9515 | +0.0023 | YES (< 0.005) |

**VERDICT: PASS** -- No correctness regression. Deltas are within 1 standard error (~0.0058), statistically indistinguishable.

## Feature Toggle

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Env var | `VLLM_DISABLE_AUTO_PERF_PLAN_2` |
| Enable (default) | Do not set the env var |
| Disable | `export VLLM_DISABLE_AUTO_PERF_PLAN_2=1` |
| Startup log (enabled) | `[AutoPerf] Plan step 2: AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is ENABLED` |
| Startup log (disabled) | `[AutoPerf] Plan step 2: AllReduce push-based 2-buffer protocol is DISABLED (env override)` |

When disabled, `PushAllReduce.__init__` returns immediately with no resource allocation. The existing barrier-based `CustomAllreduce` is used as the fallback.

## Test Coverage

24 tests, **all passing** (138s on 2x B200):

| Category | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Unit Tests (UT-1 to UT-16) | 16 | Build verification, init, should_use, correctness (int/float), sentinel, epoch alternation (1000 iters), thread count, threshold, out-of-place, dtype, multilayer (366 ARs), lifecycle, warmup, asymmetric data, identical values |
| Integration Tests (IT-1, IT-4, IT-10) | 3 | Dispatch priority routing, coexistence with CustomAllreduce, interleaved push AR + NCCL |
| CUDA Graph Tests (CG-1) | 1 | Graph capture + 10 replays with varying data |
| E2E Tests (E2E-4) | 1 | Transformer block simulation (61 blocks x 2 ARs x 2 steps) |
| Feature Toggle Tests (FT-1 to FT-3) | 3 | Enabled/disabled/not-disabled env var semantics |

title: [Kernel] Accumulate ranks in absolute order in 2-stage custom all-reduce
body:
## Purpose

`cross_device_reduce_2stage` rotates the rank pointers, so each partition's owner starts its sum at its own rank. `cross_device_reduce_1stage` sums ranks in absolute order `0..N-1`. Both reduce through the same `packed_reduce`, which accumulates into float32 (`csrc/custom_collective_common.cuh:87`, `:323-330`). When those partial sums round, the two kernels can return different bits for the same all-reduce — and the choice between them is made by message size (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:298-307`: 1-stage below 512 KiB at ≤4 ranks and 256 KiB at ≤8, 2-stage above).

(Line numbers are at main `b49c921a27`, this PR's base; the comment added here shifts the `.cuh` ones after line 47 by 2 on this branch.)

The rotation also makes 2-stage output depend on the total tensor size, even with no switch between kernels. This was independently measured by @curvedinf ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57042#issuecomment-5686335910)). `part = size / ngpus` moves the ownership boundaries whenever the size changes (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:38-40`), and each owner starts its sum at its own rank (`:45-48`). In their on-GPU in-vitro run of the unmodified kernels at 4 ranks and fp32, 14.86% of the elements of a 1664×5120 tensor differ bitwise from the same rows of its 2048×5120 parent. Both sizes are above the 512 KiB threshold, so this comes from a chunked-prefill geometry change alone. The 1-stage control on the same data is bit-identical, which pins the cause to the rotation this PR removes.

This PR makes the 2-stage kernel read the rank pointers in absolute order, so both kernels produce identical bits whichever one the heuristic selects, and 2-stage output no longer depends on the tensor size. The direction was proposed by @sfeng33 in the review of #50505; this is that change, split out and self-contained against main. cc @sfeng33

**The change** is one line in `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh`: `ptrs[i] = (const P*)_dp->ptrs[target]` → `_dp->ptrs[i]`.

Only `ptrs` loses the rotation. `tmps[i]` must keep it: `tmp_out = tmps[0]` has to be the rank's own scratch buffer, and the stage-2 gather indexes `tmps` with the same `(rank + i)` rotation. De-rotating both would make every rank write its stage-1 results into rank 0's scratch region. The code comment records this.

**Why the kernels then agree bit-for-bit.** For every element, both compute `downcast(((up(x0) + up(x1)) + ...) + up(xN-1))` through the same float32 accumulator. There are no partial sums on the 2-stage path: each partition's owner computes the full N-term sum, and stage 2 only copies already-downcast values. Once the order matches, every operation matches.

**Effect outside batch invariance.** This changes 2-stage output bit patterns for all runs, not only under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. Before and after, each result sums the same terms through the same float32 accumulator; only the order of the additions differs. How often bits actually change depends on the data and dtype: in the CPU emulation below, plain random fp16/bf16 inputs changed no elements and fp32 inputs changed ~32% (31.28% on GPU in @curvedinf's run, below). No existing test asserts bit-exact 2-stage output: the custom all-reduce tests either run at TP=2, which always selects 1-stage, or force 1-stage (`test_custom_allreduce_chunked`), and the bit-exact all-gather/reduce-scatter tests never dispatch `allreduce()`.

**Prior art, and why this is a separate PR.** #52231 by @mawong-amd already contains this same one-line change, with `ptrs` de-rotated and `tmps` kept rotated. It is part of a 36-file PR adding batch invariance on ROCm, which describes the change as making 2-stage batch-invariant and keeps that path disabled on CUDA pending tuning. This PR splits out only the kernel line, with a 4-rank differential test, so it can be reviewed and land on its own. If #52231 lands first, this PR reduces to the test. cc @mawong-amd

#56358 also targets fixed-order TP reduction, but through an opt-in Python gather-and-sum path (`VLLM_TP_FIXED_ORDER_ALLREDUCE`); it doesn't touch this kernel. Relationship to #50505: complementary. This PR makes kernel *selection* irrelevant to the bits; #50505 keeps *backend* selection (custom vs NCCL) batch-independent. Whichever lands second should drop #50505's force-1-stage gate.

## Test Plan

New test `test_one_and_two_stage_allreduce_bitwise_identical` in `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`. No NVIDIA CI job runs this file: the `:nvidia: (A100) Distributed` step it is declared in is no longer emitted, because the A100 fleet is retired. Its AMD mirror, `:amd: (MI355) Distributed`, still runs it on 4× MI355. The mirror inherits `optional: true`, so it runs only when someone unblocks it (`Run :amd: (MI355) Distributed` in build #93586).

- 4 ranks. It forces each kernel in turn with `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=1stage|2stage` (read on every `allreduce()` call, `csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:271`) over the same per-rank inputs, and asserts bitwise-identical outputs.
- fp16 / bf16 / fp32 × 4 sizes, from 16,336 B to 4,194,224 B. The sizes straddle the 512 KiB threshold, and three leave an uneven last partition.
- Adversarial inputs: each element holds `+B`, `-B` and small terms below float32's resolution at `B`, in a random rank order. Ordinary random fp16/bf16 data almost never detects a change of order, because its float32 partial sums are almost always exact (see the emulation below).
- Both forced kernels must also return the exact sum on integer inputs. The existing custom all-reduce tests run at TP=2 or force 1-stage, so none of them reaches 2-stage.
- Why 4 ranks: at 2 the rotation only turns `a+b` into `b+a`, which is commutative, so no 2-rank run can tell the orders apart.
- Skips cleanly with fewer than 4 GPUs, without the custom all-reduce ops, or without full NVLink (custom all-reduce disables itself above 2 PCIe-only ranks).

## Test Result

**4-rank GPU differential: run on 4× MI355.** @mawong-amd ran it on 4× MI355 (gfx950, XGMI) with this PR rebased onto main ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57042#pullrequestreview-5454848047)). The test passes on this branch, and against main's kernel it fails with `fp16, 16336 bytes: 2-stage differs from 1-stage in 5113/8168 elements`.

It has not been run on NVIDIA. It needs 4 GPUs with NVLink all-to-all; to reproduce there, the test should **fail** against main's kernel and **pass** on this branch:

```bash
TEST=tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
git fetch https://github.com/mosafariuk/vllm.git rankorder-2stage
# main's kernel (this PR's base; a precompiled build is enough, since main's kernel is unchanged):
git checkout b49c921a27083c25c16f308be1326055dbc87bbf && VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
git checkout d7f127882cd37a5f57f313493a7498688f5457b8 -- "$TEST"
pytest -rA "$TEST" -k one_and_two_stage   # expect FAILED: "... 2-stage differs from 1-stage in N/M elements"
# this branch (kernel change, needs a source build):
git checkout d7f127882cd37a5f57f313493a7498688f5457b8 && uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
pytest -rA "$TEST" -k one_and_two_stage   # expect PASSED
```

Other runs:

Independent in-vitro run by @curvedinf on an AMD gfx1100 ([comment with harness and logs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57042#issuecomment-5686335910)). It used the unmodified kernel headers from main `241e9391e`; `custom_all_reduce.cuh` and `custom_collective_common.cuh` there are byte-identical to this PR's original base `2983fc6286`. Main has since added only an unrelated `mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter` declaration to `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. Four logical ranks are staged sequentially on one GPU with the barrier flags pre-armed. That exercises the kernels' arithmetic (pointer order and partition ownership), but not IPC, NVLink, or this PR's pytest test. Inputs are `N(0,1)·(0.1 + 0.05·rank)`:

| comparison, 4 ranks | fp32 | bf16 |
|---|---|---|
| 1-stage vs 2-stage, same 2048×5120 data | 31.28% of elements differ | 0 |
| 2-stage at 1664×5120 vs the same rows at 2048×5120 | 14.86% | 0 |
| control: 1-stage at 1664 vs 2048 | 0 | 0 |

With this PR's line applied to the harness's header copy, all fp32 rows are reported as 0. The attached logs cover the unmodified runs. A CPU emulation of the same geometry, with a different RNG, gives 30.9% and 14.7%. 34.6% of the smaller tensor's elements change owner between the two sizes.

CPU, full test file (run before the rebase; line numbers and skip counts differ at the current head):
```
$ pytest -rA -v tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
SKIPPED [4] tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py:217: Not enough GPUs to run the test.
SKIPPED [1] tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py:312: Not enough GPUs to run the test.
================== 11 passed, 5 skipped, 14 warnings in 6.35s ==================
```

4× A100-SXM4-40GB without NVLink (`nvidia-smi topo -m` shows every pair as `NODE`), with a wheel built from this branch before the rebase — the skip path on real hardware:
```
is_fully_connected(0..3): False
SKIPPED [1] tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py:320: Custom all-reduce needs fully connected GPUs above 2 ranks.
================ 1 skipped, 15 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.45s ================
```

CPU emulation of `packed_reduce`'s float32 accumulation (emulated, not GPU). For each element, 1-stage order vs the unpatched 2-stage owner-rotated order, downcast and compared bitwise at 4 ranks:

| inputs | fp16 | bf16 | fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| this test's adversarial inputs, all 4 sizes | 62.5–62.6% of elements differ | 62.4–62.5% | 61.8–62.5% |
| plain `randn` | **0** differ | **0** differ | ~32% |

Partition owner 0 differs in 0% of elements, as expected (its order already matches); owners 1–3 differ in ~83%. The plain-`randn` row is why the test uses adversarial inputs. The fp16/bf16 zeros are structural at 4 ranks, not luck. Those terms carry 11 or 8 significant bits, so float32's 24-bit accumulator adds them exactly unless their magnitudes differ by roughly 2^11–2^14 or more. The rare rounding that remains is erased by the downcast: in an emulation with @curvedinf's input distribution, 480 of 10.5M 1-stage bf16 sums round in float32, and 0 bits differ between orders after the downcast. For realistic data the practical impact is on fp32 all-reduces. fp16/bf16 bits change mainly for inputs like this test's cancellation.

`pre-commit run --files csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`: all applicable hooks passed (ruff check/format, clang-format, typos, mypy, SPDX).

No model evaluation was run. The change only reorders a float32 accumulation of the same terms, so outputs can differ at the bit level but not in expected accuracy. Happy to run an lm-eval comparison if reviewers want one.
