title: feat(gdn): add SM8x prefill for the gated delta rule, fused and chunk-parallel
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The SM8x fused prefill kernel for the gated delta rule assigns one block to each `(sequence, head, value slice)`. This provides enough parallelism for larger batches, but underutilizes the GPU on a single long sequence: only a few blocks are resident, and each walks the whole token axis serially. For `1x8192` with two heads it reached 0.60x of the vendored flash-linear-attention Triton op.

This PR adds:

1. a **chunk-parallel path** that splits the token axis across blocks and reconciles the per-chunk states afterwards;
2. a **pointer ABI** and a shared invocation context, which reduce the host-side launch overhead that path incurs;
3. a **`v32` specialization** of the fused kernel for one measured shape that neither path won.

It also adds the dispatch logic that selects between them, and tests that pin the selection.

## Chunk-parallel path

The state recurrence is serial in the token axis. A chunk-parallel decomposition cannot remove that, only shorten the chain each block walks and repair the result afterwards. Four launches:

| stage | what it computes |
|---|---|
| `T` precompute | the per-chunk inverse `(I + tril(diag(beta) K K^T, -1))^{-1}` |
| `MN` precompute | each chunk's local state contribution and its output term |
| `fixup` | the serial scan over chunks that turns local states into absolute ones |
| prefill | the per-chunk output, reading the reconciled state |

Only `fixup` is serial, and it is serial over chunks rather than tokens: at a 2048-token chunk an 8192-token sequence scans four, where the fused kernel walks 128 block iterations. The other three stages are parallel over `(chunk, head)`.

`CollectiveInverse` is shared with the fused kernel rather than forked, as it already is with the SM90 and SM120 paths.

## Launch overhead

A CP call launches four kernels. With the tensor ABI, repeated `from_dlpack` conversion and layout construction per tensor per launch accounted for most of the call. Two changes:

**Pointer ABI.** Each stage has a variant taking `cute.runtime.make_ptr` pointers plus host-rebuilt layouts instead of DLPack tensors. Every entry is alignment-checked against the layout's claim before construction, so a pointer that would be read at the wrong offset is rejected rather than dereferenced.

**Shared invocation context.** `_CPInvocation` holds what the four stages share for one call: device and stream binding, compile options, chunk geometry, and one alignment-checked pointer per `(address, dtype, alignment)`. Stages two through four reuse it. At the caller-visible boundary on a single `1x8192` two-head sequence, three processes: backend `0.883 → 0.775 ms`, integration `1.053 → 0.942 ms`, device time unchanged. The reduction is host-side.

`_ptr_abi` is private and is not part of `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s signature; the wrapper sets it for the SM8x branch.

## Dispatch

```python
max_seq_len >= 8192 and num_seqs * max(num_q_heads, num_v_heads) <= 8
```
on compute capability 8.0, and the fused kernel otherwise.

Two restrictions:

**An exact longest sequence is required.** `cu_seqlens` lives on the device, and reading it in the wrapper would synchronize on every call. `total_seq_len` over-states the maximum for every multi-sequence batch, which is where CP loses. `max_seqlen` may be any safe upper bound, so the SM8x rules read the exact maximum from `cu_seqlens_cpu`, the caller's host copy of `cu_seqlens`, through the same host-offset validation the Cake route uses. Without it, dispatch selects the fused path.

**Compute capability 8.0 only.** SM86 and SM89 differ in SM count, L2 size and register file per SM, and neither threshold was fitted on them. They stay fused until measured.

Unsupported checkpointing, state layouts or dtypes fall back to the fused kernel rather than erroring. An explicit `use_cp=True` that CP cannot serve still raises, because the caller named a path.

Measured through the public entry on ten cells, three processes each, at `c6ca8964` (`f026c462` changes comments and docstrings only): on the seven cells whose selection changed, what the wrapper now picks is 1.235x to 2.292x of what it picked before, at both boundaries, in every process. The three cells left on the fused kernel read 1.001x–1.006x, which is the same call measured twice.

## The `v32` specialization

One cell was ahead on neither path: `1x8192` with 4 query heads and 16 value heads. CP declines it — `num_seqs * num_sab_heads` is 16 — and the fused kernel ran 0.911x–0.939x of Triton across the four boundaries below.

All V-dependent GEMMs in the fused kernel — the state update, `S@K`, new V, `O1`, `O2` — use `D_v` as the M dimension and split it across the warps. At 16 rows of M per warp, halving `D_v` leaves two warps idle without reducing per-warp work, so the dependency chain keeps its length. An earlier `BLK_V = 32` attempt failed at construction for the same reason.

The specialization partitions N instead: two warps in M and two in N, which halves each warp's work in all five GEMMs. That breaks the chain handing each accumulator on as the next GEMM's A operand, since a warp then holds half of an accumulator's N while the next GEMM needs all of it as K. Four shared buffers reassemble the wholes:

```
smem_hstate         the state, read as A by O1 and by S@K
smem_hu             V - S@K, read as A by new V
smem_hnewv          new V as it is, read as A by O2
smem_hnewv_decayed  new V after the per-token decay, read as A by the state update
```

Four rather than three because new V's two consumers need different values, and two buffers cost less than sequencing one with extra barriers. Four barriers per block. QK, KK and the chunk inverse are unchanged at `M = 64` and 128 threads, so the grid doubles: per-CTA tensor work falls `1194 → 810` static instructions while the launch total rises about a third, since QK/KK/inverse are recomputed in both halves of the band. The trade holds only while the grid stays inside one wave.

The value tile's layout atom must follow `D_v`. `K_SW128` requires 128 B of contiguous elements, 64 at `bfloat16`, and `tile_to_shape` does not narrow it: asked for a 32-wide tile it returns a 64-wide one without error, making every derived extent wrong, including the `d_v` the V chain reads. `_k_major_atom_kind` picks the widest atom a row can carry.

### Contract

```
compute capability 8.0, one sequence, exact longest sequence 8192,
4 query heads, 16 value heads, bfloat16 q/k/v, a bfloat16 initial state,
a final state, no checkpointing, no state indices
```

Only this configuration was measured, and only it is selected. The host-side facts are checked in the wrapper and the rest in the SM8x entry, which can still decline the offer. Note the initial state dtype: a caller that converts its state to fp32 on the way in does not get this path.

### Measurements

`1x8192`, 4 query heads, 16 value heads, three independent processes, four rounds of twenty reps, all three implementations interleaved within each round. The norm is the same `rmsnorm_fn` the serving stack calls, checked against `RMSNormGated.forward_static` before timing.

| item | shipped fused vs Triton | this specialization vs Triton | this specialization vs shipped fused |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare, backend | 0.933, 0.939, 0.924x | **1.018, 1.025, 1.010x** | **1.091, 1.091, 1.093x** |
| bare, integration | 0.925, 0.926, 0.911x | 0.991, 0.991, 0.977x | **1.071, 1.070, 1.072x** |
| GDN + rmsnorm, backend | 0.931, 0.934, 0.920x | **1.004, 1.007**, 0.993x | **1.079, 1.079, 1.079x** |
| GDN + rmsnorm, integration | 0.920, 0.926, 0.913x | 0.985, 0.987, 0.975x | **1.071, 1.066, 1.068x** |

Ratios are the other implementation over this one; above 1.00x means this one is ahead. All are steady-state, first round dropped. Against the shipped fused path the specialization is 1.066x–1.093x on all four items in all three processes — the comparison the selection rests on. Against Triton it is ahead at the bare backend boundary, at parity at the normalized backend boundary, and 0.975x–0.991x at the two integration boundaries: it narrows the fused path's gap against Triton rather than closing it, and does not claim consistent Triton parity.

### Known costs

Two costs are visible in the compiled kernel; neither is intrinsic to the design:

* **spills** — an 80 B stack frame where the shipped kernel has none. The state, `u` and two copies of new V stay live around the publishes, and the live ranges have not been addressed.
* **scalar publishes** — `STS.U16` goes 96 → 258, because the handoffs go through the producing MMA's C layout, which is one store per element for these buffers. A tile-walking publish would be 128-bit on both sides.

Both are left for follow-up; neither affects the fused-path margin the selection rests on.

## Verification

On a compute-capability 8.0 device. The performance numbers above were measured before the rebase, at `c6ca8964`; its rebased counterpart is `0d3bd50c`, and the commits after it touch the SM8x kernel files in comments only.

At `cc7a7b7d`:

```
test_prefill_delta_rule.py, test_prefill_cp_delta_rule.py,
test_prefill_state_indices.py, test_prefill_auto_backend.py,
test_prefill_cudnn_backend.py                3171 passed, 1071 skipped, 4 failed
test_prefill_cp_dispatch.py, test_prefill_qk_normalization.py   224 passed
```

The four failures were state-index tests from this branch that the rebase left behind main's contract: the out-of-pool child called `_run` without its `backend` argument, and two CP cases ran an unequal batch without `max_seqlen`. `7f315e0f` fixes those tests and nothing else. At `7f315e0f`:

```
tests/gdn/test_prefill_state_indices.py      114 passed, 68 skipped
tests/gdn/test_prefill_qk_normalization.py   172 passed
pre-commit on the files this PR changes      pass
scripts/check_pr_document.py                 0 new findings
```

Before the rebase, at `a7000d97`, the delta-rule, CP, dispatch and state-index files read 2690 passed / 928 skipped, 369, 48 and 114 passed.

`tests/gdn/test_prefill_cp_dispatch.py` uses recorder-based entries to cover 52 routing cases without launching a kernel. They cover CP boundaries and exact-maximum handling, architecture fallback, checkpoint behaviour, private ABI routing, the exact `v32` contract, and the absence of both private arguments from the public signature. It was added after a shape rule in `chunk_gated_delta_rule` read a host-side maximum no caller passed, got `None`, and silently disabled auto CP for Hopper and Blackwell callers.

Thirteen correctness and routing cases cover initial and final state variants, dtype and sequence-length boundaries, ragged batches, alternate head counts, `state_indices`, and checkpointing. The path each case took is read from the deciding predicate rather than inferred from timings.

A separate thirty-two cell grid over both CP argument interfaces re-froze the routing rule with the pointer entries in place. Each cell is gated in its own process before timing: all four implementations finite and agreeing to tolerance, the two CP interfaces byte-identical. Correctness, provenance and routing pass.

**Measurement method.** All ratios are within-process. The implementations were compiled and interleaved in each process, and cross-process comparisons were excluded because they varied by up to 10%. The first round was discarded to exclude clock-ramp effects, where every implementation reads about 28% slow, and the allocator was cleared and rewarmed before each measurement.

## 🧪 Tests

body:
Stacked on #6395 (R22: GDN decode `mid4` small band, BGMV 256-bit B loads on CC 10.7); same backend family as #6323; architecture-support tracking in #4254. Until #6395 merges this PR's diff shows both heads; the R23 delta alone is five commits on top of `b8db4aa97` (22 files, +3743 / −31; +3740 / −31 before the lint-only commit).

**Delivered head**: `a2fd40d9f` = `b9c54a81496` + one lint-only commit (`a2fd40d9f`: the pair-publish fallback table typed with the variant Literal for mypy, one dict literal wrapped for ruff-format; no kernel, loader-behaviour or test change). `b9c54a81496` = `b8db4aa97` + `3937b6b14` (GDN prefill adapter: cached unit gate tensors) + `e5622f142` (packed KDA T=1 tile128 pair-publish record) + `76ce8dea9` (GDN decode bf16 verify → `tile16_vpre_es_pro`) + `b9c54a814` (GDN decode fp32 T=1 register-direct `splitv8_reg` band). The first two are cherry-picks of the measured commits (`0457480a20e`, `27b5e8324b5`; identical patch-ids); the decode commits re-apply the measured branches with their `manifest.json` entries unioned (188 variants = 183 + 3 + 2). The per-record A/B measurements and the lane gates ran on the measured commits, whose kernel sources are byte-identical to the delivered ones (each record's own loader and test files differ only by the other decode record's additions, the manifest union and the lint-only commit; the decode GPU test file also by the format-only rewrap already in `b8db4aa97`). The 11 FI test files, the cubin identity check, the packed KDA official table and the band sanitizer below ran on the delivered head `a2fd40d9f`; the GDN decode official table, the delivery-tree sanitizer chain and Cake e2e, and the Blackwell legs ran on `b9c54a81496` (= `a2fd40d9f` minus the lint-only commit).

## What this PR does

Three exporter-produced, CC 10.7-gated record sets plus one host-side adapter change. Every new record is bitwise-identical to the incumbent route on the same inputs; no precision, accumulation-order or tolerance change anywhere.

1. **GDN decode, bf16 draft-verify tile16 (T = 4 / 7 / 8) → `tile16_vpre_es_pro`** (three CC 10.7-only records `cuda/cake_gdn_{c8a625d96f88cfb18aec,e44ad8c82c22ceccc75c,f71a82ca2eb4945e0df7}_*.cu`; SM100 / SM103 keep the shipped `tile16` body; the CC 10.7-only `tile16_vpre` records remain in the manifest but are no longer selected by the loader). Public path, seeds 17 / 29, ratio = shipped / new (> 1 = faster): geomean 1.0896 / 1.0909 over the 14 verify rows, minimum row 1.0530 / 1.0412, 1.1122 / 1.1198 over the five T7 / T8 rows. Two control rows with untouched bodies: 1.0025 / 1.0052 and 1.0080 / 0.9961 — every per-pair delta is within two 32 ns CUPTI ticks. Output + state digests equal 28 / 28.
2. **GDN decode, fp32-state T=1 pretranspose, 64 < state heads (B × HV) < 256 → `splitv8_reg`** (two CC 10.7-only records sharing `cuda/cake_gdn_76dbd9616fc3d0d426f4_96be6ea3c235.cu`): the shipped splitv8 mapping (eight CTAs per state head) with the state rows loaded straight into registers via `ld.global.v4` — no shared memory, no CTA barrier. 128 state heads 1.0249 / 1.0321, 192 heads 1.043 / 1.0467; band-interior check on the register-band commit, whose kernel and loader files are the delivered ones (two base / new pairs per seed): 96 heads 1.0038 / 1.0228, 224 heads 1.0555 / 1.0250, no pair slower than the shipped body; the 64-head edge (0.9959 / 1.0) stays on `splitv8`; 32 heads (1.0 / 0.9998) and ≥ 256 heads keep the shipped bodies. A `tilev32_reg` variant for 256–1023 heads was measured and dropped (320 heads 1.0 / 0.977, 480 heads 0.8708 / 0.8652, 512 heads 0.8825 / 0.8811). Digests equal on every measured row.
3. **Packed KDA T=1, tile128 register pipeline with BF16x2 pair publish** (`csrc/kda/cake_kda_packed_t1_cpasync_tile128_register_pipeline_pair_publish.cu`; CC 10.7 aligned-row band B ≥ 64; no Blackwell band selects it). Same arithmetic, reduction order, loads and state stores; each element is the same round-to-nearest BF16 conversion and only the store width changes. The binding checks 4-byte output alignment (`TVM_FFI_ICHECK`); a 2-byte-aligned BF16 output falls back to the scalar tile128 body of the same band (same bits); the legacy tile8 / tile16 generator declares `CAKE_KDA_PACKED_T1_PAIR_PUBLISH 0`. Exporter-rendered record vs the shipped tile128 body (pair / full, < 1 = faster), two interleaved rounds × two seeds: B64 0.984 / 0.984 / 0.988 / 0.988, B72 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.993 / 0.982, B96 0.984 ×4, B128 0.982–0.987, B256 0.988–0.991, B512 0.993–0.995; band geomean 0.9850–0.9889, no row slower. 4. **GDN prefill adapter (`flashinfer/gdn_prefill.py`): cached unit gate tensors.** The compiled kernels keep `UNIT_GATES` off, so a call without `g` or `beta` filled a fresh `torch.ones` per call (one or two fill kernels ahead of the main kernel). title: perf(cake_comm): QkvNormRopeExchangeOverlap SM107 four-rank plans use the bulk-row-store build
body:
`QkvNormRopeExchangeOverlap` combines the QKV projection, per-head QK RMSNorm and RoPE with the Ulysses QKV all-to-all exchange in one kernel (BF16 activations and weights, fp32 accumulation). Its producer kernel, which writes the exchanged rows, has four builds: the shipped build, `ow256` (operand load width 256), `bulk_ow256` (bulk row store plus operand load width 256) and `bulk` (bulk row store alone, at the shipped operand load width 128). Each build exists as bn128 / bn256 and single / two-CTA pair programs, plus two fold programs per pair build. The default build depends on architecture and world size:

- `ow256` on SM100 (B200) four-rank and on SM103 (B300) four- and eight-rank
- `bulk_ow256` on SM100 eight-rank
- the shipped build on SM90 (H100) at every world size and on SM107 (Rubin) two- and four-rank

title: fix(alphamoe): add the missing barrier before the expert_ids search in moe_align_block_size_kernel
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

In `csrc/alphamoe_nvfp4_sm100.cu`, `moe_align_block_size_kernel` in `alphamoe_complete_small_alignment` (CUDA path) publishes `scan_buf` with a `__syncthreads()`. After it:
1. threads with `tid < num_experts` write `prefix[tid] = scan_buf[tid]` (line 27359);
2. every thread then binary-searches `prefix[]` to fill `expert_ids` (line 27372).

There is no barrier between the writes and the search. A thread can read `prefix[mid]` before thread `mid` has written it, and `prefix[0..num_experts-1]` holds no defined value before that write. This is a shared-memory data race, which is undefined behavior in CUDA C++. A stale read sends the binary search the wrong way, so a block of tokens can get the wrong expert id.

We tested SGLang's copy of this kernel, which matches this code around the race; we did not run this file. On an A100, Compute Sanitizer's `racecheck` reports read-after-write hazards between this write and the search, and under racecheck's thread schedule the kernel returned wrong `expert_ids` in 11 of 18 launches. With the added `__syncthreads()`, there are no hazards and the output is correct. At native speed we have not observed wrong output.

This PR adds `__syncthreads()` right after the `prefix[tid]` write. The new barrier sits directly below an existing unconditional `__syncthreads()` at the same scope, so every thread of the block reaches it. It costs one barrier per launch. Alternatively, the search could read `scan_buf[mid]`, which the preceding barrier already published and which holds the same values for `mid < num_experts`.

The same fix for SGLang's copy of this kernel: sgl-project/sglang#43030.

title: fix(sampling): reserve RNG offsets for the current call
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Fix generator-managed RNG offset reservation in sampling, including Philox draw reuse across consecutive speculative sampling calls.

`get_seed_and_offset()` currently advances the generator and returns the advanced offset, so the current call starts beyond the range it just reserved. `chain_speculative_sampling()` also reserves `B * (N + 1)`, while rejection consumes `N + 2` draws per Philox stream: `N + 1` across the two acceptance loops, plus one recovery draw.

For `B=1, N=3`, consecutive calls currently start at offsets 4 and 8. A rejecting first call consumes offsets 4 through 8, reusing offset 8 in the next call.

This PR:

- Returns the current offset before advancing the generator to the end of the current call's reservation. This keeps reservations associated with their own calls even when successive call shapes differ.
- Changes the speculative sampling reservation to `B * (N + 2)`, retaining the existing batch multiplier and four-draw alignment. The example above now starts at offsets 0 and 8, with the first call consuming offsets 0 through 4.
- Adds two focused regression tests (three parametrized cases, 44 lines) covering the helper contract and consecutive rejecting speculative calls with different lengths.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #5637.

Thanks to @cudabinary for the detailed report and reproducer.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

`pre-commit run --all-files` passed with pre-commit 4.6.2 and the repository-pinned hook versions: 15 hooks passed, and the broken-symlink check was skipped because there were no matching files. No tracked files were modified. `git diff --check` also passed.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Validated on NVIDIA H800 PCIe with PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128 and CUDA 12.8, using the sampling CUDA module freshly compiled from source:

- All three new regression cases fail against the original implementation and pass with this fix.
- The helper test checks initial offsets 0 and 12, varying reservation sizes, four-draw alignment, and seed preservation.
- The speculative test forces rejection for consecutive `N=3` and `N=1` calls, checks generator cursor advancement, and compares all three returned tensors exactly against explicit seed/offset calls. It also verifies that explicit seed/offset calls do not advance the generator.
- The related sampling test selection passes: **174 passed, 1872 deselected** (three deprecation warnings). This includes the three new cases and 171 existing cases.

```bash

  -k 'reserves_current_range or chain_speculative_sampling or seed_offset or sampling_with_default_device_cuda or int64_indices_sampling' \
  --tb=short
```

The complete repository test suite and cross-architecture validation were not run; the full-suite checkbox above is therefore left unchecked.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

title: [Perf] Add an adaptive prefill delayer for data-parallel serving
body:
## Purpose

  When a large prefill is scheduled on only one DP engine, that engine performs a
  much longer model iteration while the other engines wait for it to finish. This
  creates uneven iteration times and delays ongoing decode requests.

  This PR adds an optional adaptive prefill delayer. It coordinates large prefill
  work onto the same engine steps across DP ranks, reducing iterations where one
  rank is doing prefill while others are decoding. Decode continues while prefill
  is delayed, with bounded fail-open and recovery behavior to guarantee progress.

  ## Test Plan

  Tested DeepSeek-V4 using:

  ```bash
  vllm serve "$MODEL" \
      --trust-remote-code \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
      --block-size 256 \
      --no-enable-prefix-caching \
      --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
      --data-parallel-size 8 \
      --enable-expert-parallel \
      --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
      --prefill-schedule-interval 1 \
      --enable-adaptive-prefill-alignment \
      --prefill-alignment-max-delay-passes 30 \
      --prefill-alignment-target-step-lead 2 \
      --max-model-len 16384 \
      --max-num-batched-tokens 2048
  ```

  Added unit tests for coordinated release, delay limits, capacity release,
  missing acknowledgments, and DP-wave resets.

  ## Test Result

  ```text
  10 passed in 9.68s
  Ruff checks passed
  All changed files are formatted
  ```

title: [DARFT][Core][DP] Add an opt-in cross-DP prefill delayer (--dp-prefill-delayer)
body:
## Overview

The DP ranks of a MoE engine step in lockstep. When any rank has prefill, the step becomes a long mixed (and, on some backends, eager) step for every rank. Agentic multi-turn traffic makes prefill frequent, so decode keeps getting interrupted. `--dp-prefill-delayer` (opt-in, default off) aligns prefill across the ranks and protects the decode steps after a prefill. It follows ATOM's PrefillDelayer.

## Claims

Measured on a development branch with an earlier version of this change: DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8, AgentX agentic workload, 1200 s runs, metrics over 300-1200 s, single runs per configuration.

| Concurrency | Configuration | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | P50 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Total tok/s/GPU | TTFT p50 (s) | Node |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 | no delayer (`--prefill-schedule-interval 32`), mean of 2 runs | 16.65 | 31.03 | 22.0K | 3.76 | A, B |
| 64 | + prefill delayer (10 protected steps) | **45.54** | **56.89** | 22.2K | 8.63 | A |
| 128 | no delayer (`--prefill-schedule-interval 32`) | 7.29 | 11.96 | 23.8K | 7.47 | D |
| 128 | prefill delayer, 10 protected steps | 22.82 | 26.97 | 39.7K | 5.41 | C |
| 128 | prefill delayer, 20 protected steps | **26.36** | **28.92** | 38.6K | 10.03 | C |

- The c128 rows use a later recipe with other changes; they differ only in the prefill policy. The no-delayer c128 row ran on a different node of the same type.
- The trade-off is TTFT: prefill waits for the other ranks, and long prompts wait for alignment chunk by chunk.

Validation on this upstream branch is still to be added.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefill_delayer.py`: 14 passed (CPU). The tests cover each FIRE / HOLD rule and bound, the per-rank state, the scheduler gating and the config check.
- `pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py` and `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`: pass. They cover the changed `defer_prefills` expression with the delayer off.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, mypy included.
- No GPU runs on this branch yet.

## Details

- **Protocol.** Once per engine step, each rank reports 6 ints in one CPU SUM all-reduce on the DP group: prefillable, pending prefill tokens (capped at `max_num_batched_tokens`), running decodes, KV usage >= 0.9, chunk in progress, prefill ran. Every rank then takes the same FIRE / HOLD decision for its next schedule.
- **Placement.** The all-reduce sits next to `_has_global_unfinished_reqs()`. Every rank reaches that point on every non-idle step (real, dummy and pause steps alike), which the existing DP state sync already relies on, so the extra collective cannot be skipped by one rank. The state resets at each DP wave boundary.
- **Rules (ATOM's), in order:**
  1. A step that ran prefill arms `--dp-prefill-delayer-protected-steps` (default 10) steps that HOLD while decodes run.
  2. FIRE if no rank has prefill, no rank decodes, or KV usage is high.
  3. FIRE after 200 held steps, or after 100 with a chunk in progress.
  4. HOLD until all ranks have prefill.
  5. FIRE when the pending tokens reach 0.9 x prefillable ranks x `max_num_batched_tokens`, or when the backlog stops growing for 10 steps.
- **HOLD scope.** HOLD defers all prefill compute, new requests and in-progress chunks, even on a rank without local decodes, so that ranks prefill together.
- **Interaction with `--prefill-schedule-interval`.** The delayer replaces it; setting both is an error.
- **Cost.** Off: none. On: one 6-int CPU all-reduce per step.
- **Not supported:** elastic EP and custom scheduler classes.
- **Relation to #51199** (cc @kjiang249). That PR coordinates releases through the DP coordinator (asynchronous, with acks and a 2-step lead); this one uses a synchronous per-step all-reduce in the engine loop and adds protected decode steps and a token fill target. We drove both decision functions in a CPU simulation of 8 lockstep ranks with agentic traffic:
  - #51199's all-ranks release rarely triggered; most of its releases came from its capacity and 30-pass fail-open bounds.
  - This delayer had 2-4x fewer mixed steps and about half the mean decode latency.
  - #51199 had about 3x lower TTFT.

  The two are complementary, and I am happy to merge efforts.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.

---

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).

@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Cross-DP prefill delayer.
+
+The DP ranks of a MoE model step in lockstep, so a step in which any rank runs
+prefill is a long step for every rank. Once per engine step all ranks
+all-reduce their prefill state and take the same decision: FIRE lets every rank
+with prefill work run it in the next step, HOLD defers all prefill (new requests
+and in-progress chunks) on every rank. The rules follow ATOM's PrefillDelayer.
+"""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler
+
+# FIRE once the pending prefill tokens fill this fraction of the prefillable
+# ranks' token budgets.
+FILL_TARGET = 0.9
+# Upper bounds on HOLD, in steps.
+TTFT_MAX_HOLD_STEPS = 200
+PARTIAL_MAX_HOLD_STEPS = 100
+STALL_STEPS = 10
+# FIRE when a prefillable rank's KV cache usage reaches this fraction.
+KV_HIGH_USAGE = 0.9
+
+
+def local_state(scheduler: "Scheduler", token_budget: int) -> list[int]:
+    """[prefillable, pending prefill tokens (capped), decodes, KV high,
+    chunk in progress, prefill ran since the last call] of one rank."""
+    pending = decodes = partial = waiting = 0
+    for request in scheduler.running:
+        if request.is_prefill_chunk:
+            partial = 1
+            pending += max(request.num_tokens - request.num_computed_tokens, 0)
+        else:
+            decodes += 1
+    for request in scheduler.waiting:
+        if request in scheduler.deferred_waiting:
+            continue
+        waiting = 1
+        if pending >= token_budget:
+            break
+        pending += max(request.num_tokens - request.num_computed_tokens, 0)
+    prefillable = int(bool(partial or waiting))
+    kv_high = int(
+        bool(prefillable) and scheduler.kv_cache_manager.usage >= KV_HIGH_USAGE
+    )
+    ran = int(scheduler.ran_prefill)
+    scheduler.ran_prefill = False
+    return [prefillable, min(pending, token_budget), decodes, kv_high, partial, ran]
+
+
+class PrefillDelayer:
+    def __init__(self, dp_size: int, token_budget: int, protected_steps: int):
+        self.dp_size = dp_size
+        self.token_budget = token_budget
+        self.protected_steps = protected_steps
+        self._buf = torch.zeros(6, dtype=torch.int64)
+        self._first = True
+        self.reset()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        self._protected_left = 0
+        self._hold_steps = 0
+        self._stall_steps = 0
+        self._prev_pending = -1
+
+    def step(self, scheduler: "Scheduler", dp_group: dist.ProcessGroup) -> bool:
+        """Returns whether the next step may run prefill. Must run on every DP
+        rank in every engine step (a CPU all-reduce on the DP group)."""
+        self._buf.copy_(
+            torch.tensor(local_state(scheduler, self.token_budget), dtype=torch.int64)
+        )
+        dist.all_reduce(self._buf, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM, group=dp_group)
+        fire, _ = self.decide(*self._buf.tolist())
+        return fire
+
+    def decide(
+        self,
+        num_prefillable: int,
+        pending: int,
+        decodes: int,
+        kv_high: int,
+        partial: int,
+        ran: int,
+    ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        """FIRE (True) or HOLD (False) from the DP-summed state, with the rule
+        that decided it."""
+        if ran:
+            self._protected_left = self.protected_steps
+        if self._first:
+            self._first = False
+            return self._fire("first")
+        if self._protected_left > 0:
+            self._protected_left -= 1
+            if num_prefillable and decodes:
+                return False, "protected"
+        if num_prefillable == 0:
+            return self._fire("no_prefill")
+        if decodes == 0:
+            return self._fire("no_decode")
+        if kv_high:
+            return self._fire("kv_high")
+        if self._hold_steps >= TTFT_MAX_HOLD_STEPS:
+            return self._fire("ttft")
+        if partial and self._hold_steps >= PARTIAL_MAX_HOLD_STEPS:
+            return self._fire("partial")
+        if num_prefillable < self.dp_size:
+            return self._hold("align")
+        if pending >= FILL_TARGET * num_prefillable * self.token_budget:
+            return self._fire("fill")
+        if pending <= self._prev_pending:
+            self._stall_steps += 1
+        else:
+            self._stall_steps = 0
+        self._prev_pending = pending
+        if self._stall_steps >= STALL_STEPS:
+            return self._fire("stall")
+        return self._hold("fill")
+
+    def _fire(self, reason: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        self._hold_steps = 0
+        self._stall_steps = 0
+        self._prev_pending = -1
+        return True, reason
+
+    def _hold(self, reason: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        self._hold_steps += 1
+        return False, reason

+        # not restore the warmup exception.
+        self.skip_first_delay = True

+        self.current_wave = wave
+        self.current_release_id = 0
+        self.delayed_passes = 0
+        self.delay_started_at = None
+        self.latest_observed_step = 0
+        self.pending_release = None
+        self.pending_acks.clear()
+        self.pending_release_sent_at = 0.0
+        self.last_resend_step = -1
+        self.snapshots.clear()
+        self.incomplete_started_at.clear()
+

+        self.engine_count = engine_count
+        self.reset_wave(self.current_wave)

+    ) -> PrefillAlignmentRelease | None:
+        if observation.wave < self.current_wave:
+            return None
+        if observation.wave > self.current_wave:
+            self.reset_wave(observation.wave)

+        self._acknowledge(engine_index, observation.ack_release_id)
+        if self.pending_release is not None:
+            return self.retry_due(observation.step)

+            return None

+            self.delay_started_at = None

+        if any(item.force_allow for item in ordered):
+            return self._release(observation.step, "capacity_force_allow")
+        if num_prefillable != self.engine_count:
+            return self._delay_or_release(observation.step)
+
+        max_running = max(item.running_batch for item in ordered)
+        max_prefill = max(item.max_prefill_batch for item in ordered)
+        max_requests = max(item.max_running_requests for item in ordered)
+        if max_requests - max_running < max_prefill:
+            if self.skip_first_delay:
+                self.skip_first_delay = False
+                return self._release(observation.step, "first_delay_skip")
+            return self._delay_or_release(observation.step)
+        return self._release(observation.step, "all_prefillable")
+
+    def _delay_or_release(self, step: int) -> PrefillAlignmentRelease | None:
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if self.delay_started_at is None:
+            self.delay_started_at = now
+        self.delayed_passes += 1
+        if self.delayed_passes >= _MAX_DELAY_PASSES:
+            return self._release(step, "max_delay_passes_fail_open")
+        if now - self.delay_started_at >= _MAX_DELAY_SECONDS:
+            return self._release(step, "max_delay_time_fail_open")
+        return None
+
+    def _release(self, step: int, reason: str) -> PrefillAlignmentRelease:
+        release = PrefillAlignmentRelease(
+            wave=self.current_wave,
+            release_id=self.current_release_id,
+            target_step=step + _TARGET_STEP_LEAD,
+            reason=reason,
+        )
+        self.pending_release = release
+        self.pending_acks.clear()
+        self.delayed_passes = 0
+        self.delay_started_at = None
+        self.incomplete_started_at.clear()
+        self.pending_release_sent_at = time.monotonic()
+        self.last_resend_step = release.target_step
+        return release
+
+    def seconds_until_deadline(self) -> float | None:
+        if self.pending_release is not None:
+            deadline = self.pending_release_sent_at + _RESEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS
+        elif (started_at := self._deadline_started_at()) is not None:
+            deadline = started_at + _MAX_DELAY_SECONDS
+        else:
+            return None
+        return max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic())
+
+    def deadline_action_due(self) -> PrefillAlignmentRelease | None:
+        if self.pending_release is not None:
+            return self.retry_due()
+        if self._delay_timed_out():
+            return self._release(self.latest_observed_step, "max_delay_time_fail_open")
+        return None
+
+    def _delay_timed_out(self) -> bool:
+        started_at = self._deadline_started_at()
+        return (
+            started_at is not None
+            and time.monotonic() - started_at >= _MAX_DELAY_SECONDS
+        )
+
+    def _deadline_started_at(self) -> float | None:
+        started_at = list(self.incomplete_started_at.values())
+        if self.delay_started_at is not None:
+            started_at.append(self.delay_started_at)
+        return min(started_at, default=None)
+
+    def retry_due(self, step: int | None = None) -> PrefillAlignmentRelease | None:
+        release = self.pending_release
+        if release is None:
+            return None
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        step_due = (
+            step is not None and step - self.last_resend_step >= _RESEND_INTERVAL_PASSES
+        )
+        time_due = now - self.pending_release_sent_at >= _RESEND_INTERVAL_SECONDS
+        if not step_due and not time_due:
+            return None
+        if step is not None:
+            self.last_resend_step = max(self.last_resend_step, step)
+        self.pending_release_sent_at = now
+        logger.warning(
+            "Resending prefill alignment release %d; awaiting acks from ranks %s.",
+            release.release_id,
+            sorted(set(range(self.engine_count)) - self.pending_acks),
+        )
+        return release
+
+    def _acknowledge(self, engine_index: int, release_id: int) -> None:
+        release = self.pending_release
+        if release is None or release_id != release.release_id:
+            return

+            self.pending_release_sent_at = 0.0

+class EnginePrefillAlignment:
+    """Engine-side state for the coordinator release protocol."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.release_queue = queue.Queue[ReleasePayload]()
+        self.generation = 0
+        self.release: ReleasePayload | None = None
+        self.applied_release: tuple[int, int] | None = None
+        self.last_ack: int | None = None
+        self.last_schedule_sequence = 0
+
+    @property
+    def allows_prefill(self) -> bool:
+        return self.applied_release is not None
+
+    def enqueue(self, release: ReleasePayload) -> None:
+        self.release_queue.put_nowait(release)
+
+    def reset(self, schedule_sequence: int = 0) -> None:
+        self.generation = 0
+        self.release = None
+        self.applied_release = None
+        self.last_ack = None
+        self.last_schedule_sequence = schedule_sequence
+        while True:
+            try:
+                self.release_queue.get_nowait()
+            except queue.Empty:
+                break
+
+    def prepare(self, wave: int, step: int, rank: int) -> bool:
+        """Apply a due release and return whether a stale release needs an ack."""
+        resend_ack = False
+        while True:
+            try:
+                release_wave, release_id, target_step = self.release_queue.get_nowait()
+            except queue.Empty:
+                break
+            if release_wave != wave:
+                continue
+            if release_id < self.generation:
+                resend_ack |= release_id == self.last_ack
+                continue
+            if release_id > self.generation:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "DP%d resynchronizing prefill alignment release %d to %d.",
+                    rank,
+                    self.generation,
+                    release_id,
+                )
+                self.generation = release_id
+                self.applied_release = None
+            self.release = release_wave, release_id, target_step
+
+        if self.applied_release is not None or self.release is None:
+            return resend_ack
+        _, release_id, target_step = self.release
+        if step < target_step:
+            return resend_ack
+
+        self.applied_release = release_id, target_step
+        self.generation = release_id + 1
+        self.release = None
+        logger.debug(
+            "DP%d applying prefill release wave=%d release_id=%d "
+            "target_step=%d current_step=%d.",
+            rank,
+            wave,
+            release_id,
+            target_step,
+            step,
+        )
+        return resend_ack
+
+    def observe(
+        self,
+        wave: int,
+        step: int,
+        telemetry: PrefillAlignmentTelemetry | None,
+        has_requests: bool,
+    ) -> PrefillAlignmentObservation:
+        fresh_walk = (
+            telemetry is not None
+            and telemetry.schedule_sequence != self.last_schedule_sequence
+        )
+        if fresh_walk:
+            assert telemetry is not None
+            self.last_schedule_sequence = telemetry.schedule_sequence
+            if self.applied_release is not None:
+                self._consume_release()
+            candidate_deferred = telemetry.candidate_deferred
+            force_allow = telemetry.force_allow
+            running_batch = telemetry.running_batch
+            max_prefill_batch = telemetry.max_prefill_batch
+            max_running_requests = telemetry.max_running_requests
+        else:
+            if self.applied_release is not None and not has_requests:
+                self._consume_release()
+            candidate_deferred = force_allow = False
+            running_batch = max_prefill_batch = max_running_requests = 0
+
+        return PrefillAlignmentObservation(
+            wave=wave,
+            step=step,
+            release_id=self.generation,
+            candidate_deferred=candidate_deferred,
+            force_allow=force_allow,
+            running_batch=running_batch,
+            max_prefill_batch=max_prefill_batch,
+            max_running_requests=max_running_requests,
+            ack_release_id=self.last_ack if self.last_ack is not None else -1,
+        )
+
+    def finish(self, wave: int, step: int) -> PrefillAlignmentObservation | None:
+        if self.applied_release is not None:
+            self._consume_release()
+        return self.ack_observation(wave, step)
+
+    def ack_observation(
+        self, wave: int, step: int
+    ) -> PrefillAlignmentObservation | None:
+        if self.last_ack is None:
+            return None
+        return PrefillAlignmentObservation(
+            wave=wave,
+            step=step,
+            release_id=self.generation,
+            candidate_deferred=False,
+            force_allow=False,
+            running_batch=0,
+            max_prefill_batch=0,
+            max_running_requests=0,
+            ack_release_id=self.last_ack,
+            ack_only=True,
+        )
+
+    def consume_idle_release(self) -> None:
+        if self.applied_release is not None:
+            self._consume_release()
+
+    def _consume_release(self) -> None:
+        assert self.applied_release is not None
+        self.last_ack = self.applied_release[0]
+        self.applied_release = None

title: [Fix] deepseek-v4: Fix DeepSeek-V4 non-EP TBO for attention TP > 1
body:
## Motivation

Depends on #31700.

DeepSeek-V4 Two-Batch Overlap (TBO) with DP attention,
`moe_a2a_backend=none`, and attention tensor parallelism greater than one
applies full-TP variable-length collectives to tensors replicated within each
attention-TP group. Treating those replicas as independent shards corrupts the
gather and combine layouts and produces invalid model output.

This change gives each full-TP rank one shard of its replicated DP-local tensor
and reconstructs the DP-local result across the attention-TP group after the
combine.

## Modifications

- Derive and validate DP-local token counts and full-TP shard counts for each
  TBO child batch.
- Shard replicated hidden states and input IDs across attention-TP ranks before
  the full-TP variable-length gather.
- Reduce-scatter the MoE output into one shard per full-TP rank, then
  all-gather within the attention-TP group to reconstruct the replicated
  DP-local output.
- Compute the replicated TP1 shared expert on the DP-local tensor and add it
  after the reducing combine.
- Select the non-EP TBO strategy for CP1, multi-rank DP, and SUM_LEN padding.
- Exercise attention TP in the registered DeepSeek-V4 TBO accuracy test and
  add focused tests for collective-size mapping and validation.

## Accuracy Tests

### H100 end-to-end setup

- Model: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4`
- Hardware: 2 hosts × 8 NVIDIA H100 80GB
- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260801-e4c4faf8`
- Topology: TP16 / DP2 / attention-TP8
- MoE A2A backend: `none`
- TBO enabled
- Infrastructure: [NemoRL Sandbox Infrastructure Report](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sT9QbbzXC110IC4f6T964OgKCnUouaSLYKznNnw35O8/edit?tab=t.0)

On host 0:

```bash
export NODE_RANK=0
export HEAD_NODE='<host-0 hostname>'
```

On host 1:

```bash
export NODE_RANK=1
export HEAD_NODE='<host-0 hostname>'
```

### Before: failure reproduction

The failure was reproduced both on pristine upstream `574ead753` and on the
parent of this change, `68d70aa8f`. Both reached the real two-chunk TBO path
and returned HTTP 200 responses with corrupted generated text.

The following server command was run on both hosts:

```bash

unset SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE
unset SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER
export SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1
export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1
export SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1
export SGLANG_TBO_DEBUG=1

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /model \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --enable-prefill-delayer \
  --enable-two-batch-overlap \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --dist-init-addr "$HEAD_NODE:5000" \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --fp4-gemm-backend marlin \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.94 \
  --context-length 2200 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 \
  --max-running-requests 256 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
```


This exact probe and assertion were then run:

```bash
jq -r '.choices[0].message.content' single.json | tee single.txt
```

Patched output:


`grep` exited 0: **PASS**.

The following multi-answer check was run twice so both DP routes served it:

```bash
curl --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 180 -sS \
  "http://$HEAD_NODE:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

title: [Perf] [NPU] attn: add not needs_cpu_seq_lens for dsa modules
body: ## Motivation Currently, `AscendAttnBackend` inherits `needs_cpu_seq_lens=True`. However, for DSA models that don't actually require `seq_lens_cpu`, we can bypass this dependency to reduce—or even eliminate—the CPU-bound bubbles. This PR sets `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` for `AscendAttnBackend` when running DSA models. ## Modifications - Added a `needs_cpu_seq_lens` member variable to both `AscendAttnBackend` and `AscendAttnMultiStepDraftBackend`. It is set to False when running DSA models without the HybridSWA feature, which enables the optimization introduced by this PR. - Added branches for `needs_cpu_seq_lens is False` at device synchronization points within `AscendAttnBackend`, allowing device-side tensors to be used directly in computations. - Moved the `all_reduce` communication in `EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner.can_run_graph` to the CPU to eliminate blocking waits. ~~This PR builds upon PR #36472 and should be merged after it.~~ The predecessor to this PR is #21895. Both aim to eliminate the CPU-bound overhead during Draft execution, and both are exclusively applicable to DSA models. ## Summary

Field data from running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** as a production SGLang backend on **8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only — no NVLink)**, including the *only* topology we could get to start, measured prefill/decode, a speculative-decoding A/B, and the configuration traps that cost us real experiments. Posting because SM120 + V4.1-Flash users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch.

Full write-up (with methodology and reproduction artifacts): https://github.com/Lei-010/hermes-agent/blob/main/docs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-SM120-Performance-and-Production-Config.md

Related: vLLM field report https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56700 (same hardware, vLLM side), vLLM https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892 (SM120 bug/perf tracker).

## What works

```bash
docker run --gpus all -d --name dsv41 \
  --shm-size=64g --ipc=host --network host \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TP_SIZE=8 -e DP_SIZE=1 -e EP_SIZE=8 \
  -e SPEC_ALGORITHM=dspark -e DSPARK_BLOCK_SIZE=6 \
  -e CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=2048 \
  -v /ssd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/model \
  <sglang image>
```

Effective `server_args` (verified at runtime via `/get_server_info`):

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `tp_size` / `ep_size` / `dp_size` | 8 / 8 / 1 |
| `speculative_algorithm` | DSPARK, `speculative_dspark_block_size = 6` |
| `chunked_prefill_size` | 2048 |
| `context_length` | 1,048,576 |
| `kv_cache_dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| `mem_fraction_static` | 0.72 |
| `max_running_requests` | 16 |
| `attention_backend` / `moe_runner_backend` | `dsv4` / `flashinfer_mxfp4` |
| CUDA graph decode / prefill | full (max_bs 16) / **disabled** |

**TP8/EP8 is not a preference — it is the only layout that starts** (see "Topologies SGLang rejects" below).

## Measured throughput (cold, single stream, tokens from `usage`, not SSE chunk counts)

128K cold prefill:

| Config | tok/s |
|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill_size=2048` (production) | **6,853** |
| same config re-run | 6,765 (−1.3%) |
| flashmla prefill backend | 6,845 |
| fused-MoE all-reduce | 6,828 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=4096` | 6,301 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=1024` | 6,012 |

32K prompt: ≈7,196 tok/s. GPU util ≈87% at 220 W of 600 W → **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.

Radix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix ≈ 325K tok/s (≈39×)**.

Decode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143–169 ms.

## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)

| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 76.5–78.9 tok/s | 36.4–36.5 tok/s |
| structured | 120.3–120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |
| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |

With DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class — speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured ≈237–252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).

## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)

1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** — SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.
2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your "new" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).
3. **`ep_size ≤ tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.
4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** — but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).

## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| DP2 × TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` — both replicas die within ~70 s |
| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |
| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) — looks fine, isn't |

Other SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).

## Operational notes

- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks — which silently mislabels the next experiment. Loop `docker rm -f` until the container is gone **and** nothing listens on the port.
- A parse failure must never satisfy an "expected config" assertion, or a server that has not started yet gets recorded as "spec disabled".
- Verify intended config from the server (`/get_server_info`) before timing anything; discard legs that fail the gate rather than recording them.

## Not established

No 24 h soak (numbers come from a working day of production use), block sizes 4/8/12 not re-measured with the fixed sweep tool, and >32K prefill/long-context degradation not characterised.

title: Fairness-Aware and Latency-Controllable Scheduling for Chunked-Prefill LLM Serving
body: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed with highly heterogeneous workloads, chunked-prefill execution has emerged as a mainstream serving architecture. Balancing scheduling fairness and latency stability in such environments is critical; otherwise, severe head-of-line blocking and request starvation will degrade user experience. However, existing systems rely on rigid First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) policies and static token budgets, leading to fairness degradation and unpredictable latency jitter. To address these issues, we propose a fairness-aware and latency-controllable scheduling framework for chunked-prefill LLM engines. Specifically, we design a lightweight aging-based scheduling policy that dynamically calculates priorities using accumulated waiting time and remaining prefill work. Furthermore, we develop Latency-Prediction-Based Request Scheduling (LPRS) and Active Prefill Control (APC) to replace static budgets with target-time constraints and actively regulate prefill concurrency. We evaluated our scheduling framework on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend accelerators using real-world workloads. Results show the aging policy reduces mean end-to-end latency by over 10\% compared to FCFS. Moreover, LPRS and APC significantly reduce P99 tail latency and suppress prefill fragmentation, confirming that the structural prefill control and the temporal latency constraints are fundamentally complementary. All codes have been released in Github.

title:
Prepacking: A Simple Method for Fast Prefilling and Increased Throughput
  in Large Language Models
body:
During inference for transformer-based large language models (LLM),
prefilling is the computation of the key-value (KV) cache for input tokens in
the prompt prior to autoregressive generation. For longer input prompt lengths,
prefilling will incur a significant overhead on decoding time. In this work, we
highlight the following pitfall of prefilling: for batches containing
high-varying prompt lengths, significant computation is wasted by the standard
practice of padding sequences to the maximum length. As LLMs increasingly
support longer context lengths, potentially up to 10 million tokens, variations
in prompt lengths within a batch become more pronounced. To address this, we
propose Prepacking, a simple yet effective method to optimize prefilling
computation. To avoid redundant computation on pad tokens, prepacking combines
prompts of varying lengths into a sequence and packs multiple sequences into a
compact batch using a bin-packing algorithm. It then modifies the attention
mask and positional encoding to compute multiple prefilled KV-caches for
multiple prompts within a single sequence. On standard curated dataset
containing prompts with varying lengths, we obtain a significant speed and
memory efficiency improvements as compared to the default padding-based
prefilling computation within Huggingface across a range of base model
configurations and inference serving scenarios.

title: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
body: Existing training-free approaches for GUI grounding often rely on multiple inference runs, such as iterative cropping or candidate aggregation, to identify target elements. Despite this additional computation, each forward pass still independently interprets the instruction and parses the visual layout, without enabling progressive interaction among visual tokens. In this paper, we study what happens during GUI grounding in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and identify a previously overlooked bottleneck. We show that grounding follows a two-stage paradigm: the prefill stage determines candidate UI elements, while the decoding stage subsequently refines the final coordinates. This asymmetry establishes prefill as the critical step, as errors in candidate selection cannot be effectively corrected during decoding. Based on this observation, we propose Re-Prefill, a training-free method that revisits inference by introducing an attention-guided second prefill stage to refine target selection. Specifically, visual tokens that consistently receive high attention from the query position, i.e., the final token, across layers are extracted as a preliminary target hypothesis and appended to the input, together with the instruction hidden states, enabling the model to deeply re-think its decision before coordinate generation. Experiments across four VLMs and five benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-V2, OSWorld-G, UI-Vision, and MMBench-GUI, demonstrate consistent improvements without additional training, with gains of up to 4.3% on ScreenSpot-Pro. Code will be available at https://github.com/linjiaping1/Re-Prefill.

title: config(dsv41flash): offload MI325X Engram tables to host DRAM / 将 MI325X Engram 表卸载到主机 DRAM
body:
## Summary

Three changes to the **existing** `dsv41flash-fp4-mi325x-vllm-agentic-dspark` TP8 arm. No new arms, no retuning — the point is to isolate the Engram lever on an already-validated curve.

1. `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'` — offload the Engram tables to pinned host memory.
2. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` — work around the ROCm SWA fault.
3. Repin the image `nightly-eed1f3d0` → `nightly-rocm100-3df4ae15`, which is where both of the above land. This is the same ROCm 10 nightly the MI355X arm runs, at the same vLLM commit.

## Why

**Engram.** [vllm-project/vllm#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) widened the two `is_cuda()` gates to `is_cuda_alike()`, so gfx942 now resolves an `EngramConfig` where it previously ignored the flag. Left resident, the tables cost 183 GiB per rank at TP8 — HBM a 256 GB card would otherwise spend on KV.

Every NVIDIA DSv4.1-Flash arm has offloaded since [#2963](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/2963) (2026-09-11); MI355X and MI325X are the only holdouts. On the MI355X sweep ([run 35574132719](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35574132719)) the resident-table arm is exactly the one whose KV pool starves at high concurrency:

| | KV memory | KV tokens | max concurrency @ 1M ctx |
|---|---|---|---|
| B300 TP4 (offloaded) | 132.48 GiB | 63.1M | 60.17x |
| MI355X TP4 (resident) | 38.05 GiB | 14.8M | 14.14x |

**SWA bounded replay.** [vllm-project/vllm#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227) turned it on by default after the `eed1f3d0` pin. The window clamp it depends on landed only in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA kernels; the ROCm sparse SWA path got just the `replay_start` kwarg. Every gfx950 point of [run 35567570539](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35567570539) died with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` at the first prefix hit carrying a replay start; adding this flag turned all 16 points green. gfx942 runs the same ROCm sparse path, so it needs the same guard on this image.

## Not a duplicate of #3337

[#3337](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3337) also touches this recipe, but the two differ on purpose:

| | #3337 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Engram at TP8 | **resident** (kept for comparability) | **offloaded** |
| Engram below TP8 | offloaded | n/a |
| New TP4 / TP2 arms | adds both at conc 1-32 | none |
| TP2 batched-token / seq / capture caps | adds | none |

#3337 explores *new* TP4/TP2 arms while holding TP8 fixed. This PR changes only TP8 so the delta against its own validated baseline is attributable to the Engram flip alone. They conflict textually; happy to rebase onto whichever lands first, or to fold this into #3337 if maintainers prefer one MI325X PR.

## Testing

Config-only change; correctness rides on the sweep this PR triggers. Supporting evidence gathered on MI355X (gfx950, same ROCm sparse path):

- Engram offload verified on-device at TP4: `Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory: 96002514 rows x 256, 23.60 GiB per rank`, byte-identical row sharding to the B300 arm.
- `--no-swa-bounded-replay` converted 16/16 crashed points to success on [run 35574132719](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35574132719), GSM8K 0.9750-0.9757.

## AI assistance

Investigation and patch drafted with AI assistance (Cursor). All conclusions are backed by the CI logs and on-device measurements linked above; a human reviewed every changed line.

title: [DNM] Add MI355X TP2 Engram CPU offload / 添加 MI355X TP2 Engram CPU 卸载
body:
## Scope

**AgentX ONLY. No fixed-sequence or 8k1k benchmarks.**

Add `dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark-tp2-engram-cpu` for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on MI355X TP2 at concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, with a c32 real-rejection eval. Pin `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e` and pass `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`.

The bundled patch adds AMD pinned-host Engram TP storage through the existing ROCm-capable UVA helper and permits explicit TP-only configuration. Common hashing, lookup math, TP ownership and graph staging are unchanged. Engram DP sharding and shared memory remain rejected. Original TP4 config and image stay unchanged. KV stays GPU-resident; AgentX throughput retains golden AL 3.51 and eval uses real block rejection.

The earlier mixed sweep was cancelled at the user's correction. The 8k1k config, entrypoint and client path have been removed. `full-sweep-enabled` now selects only the AgentX experiment.

## Verification

- Three local recipe behavior tests cover TP4 preservation, TP2 offload, and real-rejection eval.
- CPU configuration validation and clean patch application to the pinned source pass.
- GPU jobs must pass real lookup/graph preflight before model loading. GPU-less skips cannot pass preflight.
- [Run 35181013534, attempt 2](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35181013534/attempts/2) passed on head `6f87d7427967a03ac8fae42bc97486630c850702`: AgentX TP2 c1, c2, c4, c8, c16, c32 and c32 eval.
- All seven GPU jobs ran all three preflight tests successfully, including actual host/HBM lookup, TP2 shard reconstruction and graph replay; no GPU skips. Serving logs confirm pinned-host Engram tables and `cpu_offload=True`.
- All six throughput jobs passed result/error-rate and required server-metric validation and uploaded benchmark artifacts. Request errors were 0 at c1/c2/c4/c16, 1/1172 (0.085%) at c8, and 2/3369 (0.059%) at c32, within the unchanged repository threshold.
- [Real-rejection c32 eval](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35181013534/job/105101151381) passed GSM8K: strict-match 0.9712, flexible-extract 0.9704 (threshold 0.9). Eval artifacts were uploaded and collection passed.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35181013341) passed Lint and Tests. No fixed-sequence benchmark jobs ran in this AgentX-only sweep.

Hardware validation is complete for this experiment. Keep draft pending human review and the upstream-publication gate below; do not merge or bypass review.

## Patch disclosure

The bundled patch is now the runtime part of upstream [vllm-project/vllm#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) ("[ROCm][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram tables in host memory on ROCm"), applied to the same pinned image: the two `is_cuda()` gates in `vllm/config/engram.py` and `vllm/config/vllm.py` widen to `is_cuda_alike()`, and `amd/model.py` imports the shared `Engram` from `nvidia/engram.py`. The earlier private `amd/engram.py` implementation is removed; `rocm_preflight.py` now exercises the upstream `ParallelEngramEmbedding` and `Engram` classes on the GPU. The upstream test-file hunk is not shipped because the image has no test tree. The branch was merged with `origin/main` (append-only changelog resolution) to clear the conflict and retrigger the sweep. [Waiver](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/feat/dsv41flash-mi355x-tp2-engram-cpu/docs/waiver/3217.md) records patch scope and the removal plan; the upstream PR is open, not merged, so the upstream-publication merge gate remains outstanding. Model-support context: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56214. The hardware evidence above is from the previous patch and must be re-established by the new sweep.

AI assistance was used for implementation and local testing.

**仅运行 AgentX，不运行固定序列或 8k1k。**

为 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 添加 MI355X TP2 Engram CPU 卸载配置，并发为 1、2、4、8、16、32，c32 执行真实拒绝采样 eval。固定 af1c014 ROCm 镜像，并传入 `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`。补丁采用现有 ROCm UVA helper 实现 pinned-host TP 表，保留公共计算和图暂存逻辑；仍拒绝 DP 分片及共享内存。原有 TP4 不变，KV 驻留 GPU，吞吐保留黄金 AL 3.51。

title: [Klaud Cold] Add MI325X TP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash vLLM AgentX arm with Engram host offload / 新增 Engram 主机卸载的 MI325X TP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash vLLM AgentX 臂
body:
## Summary
Adds a **TP4** arm with **Engram CPU offload** to `dsv41flash-fp4-mi325x-vllm-agentic-dspark`, beside the existing TP8 arm, and repins the image.

- New search-space row `tp: 4` at concurrency 1-32, mirroring the TP8 grid so the two are directly comparable.
- `dsv41flash_fp4_mi325x_mtp.sh` now sets `--engram-config` **explicitly per TP**: `cpu_offload:false` at TP8, `cpu_offload:true` at TP4.
- Image repinned from `nightly-eed1f3d0…` to `nightly-3df4ae153eb385e27b52f26c81f8edb9e20b9984`.
- New `--no-swa-bounded-replay` flag.

## Why the image had to move
The pinned `nightly-eed1f3d0…` tag **404s on Docker Hub**; it survives only on node caches. The new pin is the same upstream commit the MI355X arm moved to in #3326, on the plain ROCm channel that the gfx942 arms already use rather than the `rocm100` channel, which no gfx942 recipe has exercised.

That commit is also what makes this change possible: [vllm-project/vllm#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) widened two `is_cuda()` gates to `is_cuda_alike()`, so `engram_config` finally resolves on gfx942. Previously this recipe had to omit the flag entirely.

## Why `--engram-config` is now explicit on both arms
On builds carrying #57491, `cpu_offload` **defaults on** through `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD`. Bumping the image without setting it would silently move the TP8 tables to host memory and change that curve. Setting it explicitly to `false` at TP8 keeps the existing arm behaviourally identical, and `true` at TP4 is what makes TP4 fit.

## Why `--no-swa-bounded-replay`
[vllm-project/vllm#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227) turned SWA bounded replay on by default **between the two pins**. It relies on a window clamp that landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA kernels; the ROCm sparse SWA path only gained the `replay_start` kwarg. On gfx950 that crashed every point with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` at the first prefix hit carrying a replay start. **gfx942 runs the same ROCm sparse path**, so this recipe pre-empts it rather than burning a sweep to rediscover it. Prefix caching stays on.

## Memory
With the Engram tables offloaded, resident weights are ~81 GiB per rank at TP4, from the per-rank fit across the measured H100 TP8, H200 TP4 and B200 TP2 points (256 GiB sharded plus 17.2 GiB replicated). On a 256 GB card at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` that leaves roughly **100 GiB of KV per GPU** after the indexer's 32 GiB `[batched-tokens, 1M]` logits buffer. TP8 with the tables resident is unchanged at roughly 73 GiB per rank.

## Test plan
- [ ] `full-sweep-enabled` sweep: TP4 concurrency 1-32 AgentX + evals green
- [ ] TP8 re-runs green on the new image and matches the prior curve
- [ ] Confirm the c1 log shows the Engram offload line at TP4 and no offload at TP8

- 新增 `tp: 4` 搜索空间行，并发 1-32，与 TP8 网格一致以便直接对比。
- `dsv41flash_fp4_mi325x_mtp.sh` 现按 TP **显式**设置 `--engram-config`：TP8 为 `cpu_offload:false`，TP4 为 `cpu_offload:true`。

make concurrent first use of

initialize exactly one shared object

body:
Draft sampling uses a different distribution than speculative rejection
#31
New issue
Copy link
New issue
Copy link

Draft sampling uses a different distribution than speculative rejection
#31
Copy link
Description
morluto
opened
on Jun 30, 2026
Issue body actions
Problem
sample_tokens
samples draft tokens through the native-dtype logits path, while speculative rejection/correction uses the float32 distribution produced by
logits_to_probs
.
In speculative decoding, the proposal sample must be drawn from the same draft distribution used in the acceptance ratio and correction distribution. If the sample is drawn from
r
but the algorithm computes acceptance as if it came from
p
, the final marginal distribution is generally biased.
Impact
With bfloat16 logits, the sampled draft distribution can differ from the float32 draft distribution used for rejection. That breaks the exact-distribution guarantee expected from speculative decoding.
Fix
Fixed in PR
#30
by casting logits to float32 before temperature scaling and softmax in
sample_tokens
, so sampling and rejection use the same draft distribution.
