title: fix: treat retryable image failures as server-side in the example server
body:
`server-py/main.py` picks the HTTP status for an `ImageError` out of a hardcoded set of two names:

```python
status_code = 500 if error.kind in {"Client", "TokenBudget"} else 400
```

`ImageError` also carries `is_retryable`, and `deepseek-recipe-image/src/error.rs:99-111` documents what it means: `Fetch` is retryable regardless of its source, and `FetchStatus` is retryable at 5xx. Neither name is in that set, so both are answered `400 invalid_request_error` - the client is told its request was malformed and should not be retried, which is the opposite of the classification the library hands over on the exception object.

## Measured on the published wheel

`deepseek-recipe==0.1.1`, `manylinux_2_28_x86_64`, imported directly. `ImageResolver` was pointed at a local stdlib HTTP server, so nothing here needs egress; the last row uses a closed port.

| upstream condition | `error.kind` | `error.is_retryable` | status today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| upstream answers 503 | `FetchStatus` | `True` | **400** `invalid_request_error` |
| connection refused | `Fetch` | `True` | **400** `invalid_request_error` |
| upstream answers 404 | `FetchStatus` | `False` | 400 `invalid_request_error` |
| 200 with a non-image body | `UnsupportedMediaType` | `False` | 400 `invalid_request_error` |

An upstream image host answering 503 is therefore reported to the API client as the client's own mistake.

## Why `Client` and `TokenBudget` stay at 500

That set is not wrong, only incomplete, so this keeps both entries:

- `Client` is documented as "The HTTP client could not be constructed" (`deepseek-recipe-image/src/error.rs:93-95`) - this server's own failure.
- `TokenBudget` wraps `CalcResizeError`, and the branch immediately below already answers that same failure with 500:

```python
except CalcResizeError as error:
    raise RequestError(str(error), 500) from error
```

## Change

One condition added; nothing else moves.

```diff
-            status_code = 500 if error.kind in {"Client", "TokenBudget"} else 400
+            status_code = (
+                500 if error.is_retryable or error.kind in {"Client", "TokenBudget"} else 400
+            )
```

I did not add a regression test. `server-py/tests/test_smoke.py` has no image-error coverage, and reproducing this needs a controllable upstream that the suite does not currently stand up. Happy to add one with a local stub server if you would like it.

title: fix(image): accept case/space variants of the data URL base64 marker in the size precheck
body:
## Motivation

`estimated_decoded_len` (`deepseek-recipe-image/src/resolver.rs`) decides base64 vs percent-encoding with an exact `header.ends_with(";base64")` — but the actual decoder (`data_url::DataUrl::process`, data-url 0.3.2 per Cargo.lock) accepts the marker **ASCII-case-insensitively and with optional spaces after the semicolon**. For `data:image/webp;BASE64,…` or `data:image/webp; base64,…`, the parser decodes as base64 while the precheck takes the percent-encoding branch and estimates `body.len()` — the raw base64 length, ≈ 4/3 of the decoded size.

Concretely: with the default `max_image_bytes = 32 MiB`, a valid ~25.5 MB image supplied as 34,000,000 base64 characters is rejected with `ImageError::ImageTooLarge { size: 34_000_000, max: 33_554_432 }` → HTTP 400 from the example servers. Every image whose decoded size lies in the top quarter of the allowed range is falsely rejected, and the error reports the base64 length as the size. The identical body with a lowercase, space-free marker is accepted.

## Changes

The marker check now looks at the last `;`-separated parameter, trims it, and compares ASCII-case-insensitively — matching the parser in both directions. No API change.

## Testing

Two new unit tests: marker detection for `base64`/`BASE64`/`; base64`/absent/`charset` variants, and the estimator using base64 math (`len/4*3`) for all three accepted spellings. `cargo test -p deepseek-recipe-image --no-default-features --locked`: **13/13 pass** (11 existing + 2 new).

  <details><summary>Proof</summary>

  ```
  test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  ```

  </details>

title: V4.1 Flash: user-supplied special-token literals produce different token counts from the official API
body:
## Description

I found a discrepancy between `DeepseekV41Encoding` and the official V4.1 Flash API when user message content contains literal special-token strings such as `<｜User｜>` or `<think>`.

The recipe recognizes these literals as single AddedTokens. However, the official API reports a larger `prompt_tokens` increase, consistent with ordinary BPE encoding for the individual literals tested.

## Environment

- Test date: September 11, 2026
- Official endpoint: `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions`
- Model: `deepseek-flash` (V4.1 Flash)
- Python package: `deepseek-recipe==0.1.1`
- Repository inspected at commit: `8cadfede7063c896b944e7bae05daa3549ae97ea`
- Bundled tokenizer: `static/tokenizers/v41/tokenizer.json`

## Observed results

Each request contains one user message, with:

```json
{
  "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
  "max_tokens": 1,
  "temperature": 0,
  "stream": false
}
```

The counts below include the conversation template:

| User content | Recipe token count | Official API `prompt_tokens` | API increase over empty content |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Empty string | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `x` | 5 | 5 | 1 |
| `<｜User｜>` | 5 | 9 | **5** |
| `<｜Assistant｜>` | 5 | 9 | **5** |
| `<｜System｜>` | 5 | 9 | **5** |
| `<think>` | 5 | 7 | **3** |
| `</think>` | 5 | 7 | **3** |
| `｜DSML｜` | 5 | 8 | **4** |
| `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>` | 5 | 16 | **12** |
| `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` | 5 | 16 | **12** |

For example, the recipe encodes the user-supplied `<｜User｜>` as `[128803]`. Encoding the same text with the bundled tokenizer’s `added_tokens` table cleared produces `[30, 28217, 6756, 28217, 32]`, matching the API’s five-token increase.

The discrepancy also occurs with default thinking settings: empty content produces 30 prompt tokens, while `<｜User｜>` produces 35.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from the repository root with `deepseek-recipe==0.1.1` installed and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` set:

```python
import json
import os
import urllib.request

from deepseek_recipe import (
    ChatCompletionRequest,
    ConversionOptions,
    DeepseekV41Encoding,
    Tokenizer,
)

encoding = DeepseekV41Encoding().with_tokenizer(
    Tokenizer.from_file("static/tokenizers/v41/tokenizer.json")
)

for content in ["", "x", "<｜User｜>", "<think>", "｜DSML｜"]:
    body = {
        "model": "deepseek-flash",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
        "max_tokens": 1,
        "temperature": 0,
        "stream": False,
    }

    converted = ChatCompletionRequest(body).convert(ConversionOptions())
    local_count = len(encoding.encode(converted.conversation))

    request = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={
            "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"],
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        result = json.load(response)

    print(repr(content), local_count, result["usage"]["prompt_tokens"])
```

Observed counts:

```text
Content          Recipe   Official API
''               4        4
'x'              5        5
'<｜User｜>'      5        9
'<think>'        5        7
'｜DSML｜'       5        8
```

## Possible explanation

The current [tokenizer implementation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/8cadfede7063c896b944e7bae05daa3549ae97ea/deepseek-recipe-encoding/src/tokenizer.rs) calls `encode(text, false)` on the rendered prompt. This still recognizes AddedToken literals, without distinguishing user content from template-generated control tokens.

## Scope and an additional edge case

The API observations above are based on usage counts. The API does not expose input token IDs, so these observations do not establish the exact server-side encoding algorithm.

There is also an edge case with adjacent DSML literals:

| User content | Recipe token count | Official API `prompt_tokens` | Ordinary BPE content + template |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `｜DSML｜` repeated 8 times without separators | 12 | 21 | 36 |

The API result was reproduced. Therefore, simply clearing `added_tokens` is not yet established as a complete fix.

## Expected behavior / clarification

Could you clarify the intended handling of special-token literals in user content?

Should the recipe distinguish them from template-generated control tokens, or is an additional preprocessing step required to match the official API?

title: [cake deslop] cake_mamba_ssd_combined + cake_selective_state_update (2): drop 14 dead/env-only/corner sources, re-template state dtype
body:
**Background.** `csrc/cake_mamba_ssd_combined` and `csrc/cake_selective_state_update` implement two opt-in Cake backends on SM100/SM103: `SSDCombined(backend="cake")` (`flashinfer/mamba/ssd_combined.py`, default `"cute"`) and `selective_state_update(backend="cake")` (default `"auto"`, i.e. FlashInfer). At 3184bbea the Cake code is 90 files / 130,111 lines: SSD 49 device `.cu` (98,051) + 5 host templates (5,025), SSU 28 files (12,487), loaders 5,078, Cake tests 8,998, benchmark 472. The first round covered both families. #5821 (closed by #5924, −36,396) dropped the byte-identical SM103 tree and the per-dtype triplication, leaving 12 main sources, one host launcher and a table-driven loader. #5825 (closed by #6003) regenerated the checkpoint/MTP/FP32 STP programs as arch-neutral `-D` instantiations, but kept the 5 shipped BF16 STP clones because the regenerated direct program was 3.5-4% slower. Since then, #6051 (re-emitted per-dtype files), #6100, #6206 (+14,738), #6291, #6330 (+10,932, 12 `_noring` schedule twins) and #6582 (+72,440: `exactfused`, `exactpre`, look-back `chunkpar`, two more host templates) have grown SSD back to 48 main sources and 5 host templates. #6030 and #6040 added SSU AOT registration, the hd64/paired-rows programs and the `mb4` clone. No per-arch copies came back. Non-Cake code under these paths is out of scope: the CuTe `ssd_kernel.py` and `tests/mamba/triton_reference`, which six non-Cake tests import.

**Findings**
- **8 unreachable SSD sources (12,677 lines).** Only one function produces a program name: `CakeSSDCombined._materialize_workspace` (`flashinfer/mamba/cake_ssd_combined.py:1949`), which combines `two_kernel_family` (1162-1182) with `_exact_scan_variant` (1432-1459). `_noring` is picked only when each item is a single 128-token chunk (batched: batch == 2, no z, 25 < seqlen < 90; varlen: 63·nseq < total < 65·nseq). `exactpre` needs ≥ 2 chunks per item, so the 6 `*_precomputed_noring_*.cu` (`exactpre_*_noring`, 9,000 lines) have been dead since #6582 added them. #6582 also removed the f32 key from `_EXACT_NORING_VARLEN_MIN_ITEMS` (1421-1425), which leaves `exact_f32_varlen_noring` (1,453, #6330) and `exactfused_f32_varlen_noring` (2,224, #6582) dead. `FLASHINFER_CAKE_SSD_CHUNK_PARALLEL` only forces the family, and SSD has no AOT list.
- **Env-only and corner SSD sources (10,065 lines).** `three_phase_preferred` (1000-1013) returns False for varlen. That leaves `chunkpar3_{bf16,f16,f32}_varlen` (3 × 1,961 = 5,883, #6582) reachable only through `FLASHINFER_CAKE_SSD_CHUNK_PARALLEL=three_phase`. Tests keep them alive as the forced-mode oracle: `_forced_runs` 5505-5530 (asserts at 5779/5891), the forced three-phase helper at 1470-1474, and the host-template test at 5373-5376. `exact_*_batched_noring` (3 × 1,394 = 4,182, #6330) needs batch == 2 with one chunk. On that shape `fused_selected` wins unless nheads > 512. Calibration ran at nheads 128, which `exactfused_*_batched_noring` serves, and no test uses nheads > 512.
- **State-dtype triplets (re-introduced).** The 48 main sources are 16 programs × {bf16, f16, f32}. The f16 copy differs from bf16 by 1 normalized line (the state pointer type). The f32 copy differs by 2-5 lines: signature, `(float)` casts, and the exactfused L2-prefetch bound (4 → 8, stride 64 → 32). The f16 and f32 sources together are 32 files / 64,972 lines. After the removals above, 34 sources over 12 shapes remain. Keeping one source per shape with a `STATE_T` define removes 22 files / 48,585 lines. Only tests use f16 state (the loader says it is "unmeasured and follows bfloat16"). It is unconfirmed whether any engine passes it.
- **Ring/`_noring` twins and overlapping generations.** The 18 `*_noring_*.cu` total 30,186 lines. The loader (136-141) calls them the same kernel built with `epilogue_ring=False`, with bitwise-identical outputs, but no test checks that. The surviving noring routes are calibration cells chosen for 1-2% kernel-time wins: batch 2 × 25-90 tokens, mean 64 tokens per sequence, and fused varlen noring only at num_sequences·nheads == 256. The loader carries a 120-line calibration log (1311-1430). All three exact-scan generations are kept (`exact_*`, `exactpre_*`, `exactfused_*`; normalized bf16 diffs of 432-1,045 lines), and so are both chunk-parallel generations (look-back `chunkpar`, three-phase `chunkpar3`). `exact_*` serves only one-chunk items, byte for byte, with 13 SHA-256 pins. `chunkpar3` serves batched cases with tiles ≤ 256, or ≥ 32 items × ≥ 64 chunks, where the look-back measured 1.05-1.32× slower.
- **SSD host templates.** The 5 `generated/host/*.cpp` (5,025 lines) differ by 4-193 normalized lines, and `_render_host_source` (1282-1308) already substitutes 9 placeholders. `mamba_ssd_combined_precomputed_sequence.cpp` (977) differs from `mamba_ssd_combined_fused_sequence.cpp` only by the `if (preprocess_grid_x != 0)` guard. That guard is always true for `exactpre`, because the grid is zeroed only in the `exactfused` branch (2784-2798).
- **SSU clones.** `stp_paired_rows_mb4` (`cake_selective_state_update_8ab15b919ac98b5e1735_{kernel,binding}.cu`, 973 lines, #6040) differs from `stp_paired_rows` (`c7e08dcbb58896052ee9`) only by `#define LAUNCH_MIN_BLOCKS 4` vs `3`, plus the symbol. `_PAIRED_ROWS_MIN_BLOCKS_BANDS` has only an sm_100a band, but `gen_cake_selective_state_update_modules` (672-685) has no arch filter. As a result, `flashinfer/aot.py:892-895` builds the 2 mb4 instantiations for sm_103a even though no route selects them (2 of 52 AOT modules). The shipped BF16 STP sources `ratio8`, `ratio8_saturated`, `ratio16` and `persistent` differ from `stp_bf16_direct.cu` by 14, 18, 22 and 65 normalized lines. The 5 host `.cc` shims are 8-14 lines apart, and each carries a private TMA descriptor arena (static mutex, string-keyed `unordered_map`s, `cuCtxGetCurrent`/`cuStreamIsCapturing` on every call). The 9 regenerated bindings use `tvm_ffi_utils.h` instead.
- **Baked-in SSU shapes.** The `dynamic` program (`ae6bcb235d195b6ef079`, 448 lines) serves only `(nheads, dim, dstate, ngroups) == (16, 64, 128, 1)` with f32 state, and its kernel hard-codes `* 16 + head) * 64`. `mtp_cache_c4_t6` bakes 8 projection strides plus nheads/ngroups into `-D` defines (`cache_defines`, 1155-1187), and AOT ships 3 layouts. Other layouts JIT-compile or fall back to FlashInfer.
- **SSD host path.** Every call encodes 4-5 `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` descriptors, with no cache even though `prepare()` pins shapes. It also runs ~80 TVM-FFI range checks plus private `check_*` helpers, sets the device twice (`CUDADeviceGuard` and a thread-local `cudaSetDevice`), reads `os.environ` on every unprepared call and enters `torch.cuda.device()` twice. Strided inputs are copied into packed workspace buffers. bf16 `dt`/`dt_bias` are converted to f32, which costs one extra copy kernel per forward (2743-2753); which engines pass bf16 `dt` is unconfirmed.
- **Dead code and artifacts.** The non-paired branch of `_plan_stp_batch` (1432-1441) returns `stp_direct`/`stp_persistent`, which are in neither `PROGRAMS` nor `_SHIPPED_STP`; its only caller (1527) passes `paired=True`. The 9 `closure_sha256` fields in `MODULES` are never read for mamba. `_PENDING_EXPORT`/`_require_exported` guard against placeholder hashes, but all 48 entries carry real hashes and the export tool named in the error does not exist in the repo. `tests/mamba/cake_ssd_accuracy_probe.py` (370 lines, #6051) is an argparse script that pytest never collects; only two comments reference it. The SSD loader is 31% comments and docstrings, and the SSU `MODULES` dict is 559 lines.
- **Tests pinning removals** (update each one in the PR that removes what it pins):
  - `tests/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined.py`: `test_source_program_table_names_shipped_sources` (4406-4571: name set including `_noring`, 49 sources, glob == table), `test_source_exact_scan_variant_programs` (6148-6193: 12/12/12/6/6, `len(_PROGRAMS) == 48`, `_EXACTPRE_NORING_SMEM_BYTES`), `test_source_retained_start_programs_are_the_round5_files` (13 SHA-256 pins, 6360-6411), `test_source_host_template_binds_stage_arguments_in_loader_order` (guard assert at 4281-4282), `test_source_program_name_covers_every_state_dtype`, `test_active_source_package_declares_cuda_half_types_explicitly` and `test_source_unexported_program_refuses_to_build`. 14 of the file's 87 tests (1,025 lines) assert only table or template text.
  - `tests/mamba/test_cake_selective_state_update.py`: `test_registry_names_every_program` (1055-1069), `test_paired_heads_per_cta_follows_the_work_and_arch` (627-639), `test_aot_table_names_every_delivered_build`, `test_jit_names_stay_within_the_file_name_limit`, and the shipped-STP file check at 999-1006.

**Proposed steps**
- [ ] Delete the 8 unreachable SSD sources: the 6 `*_precomputed_noring_*.cu` and `mamba_ssd_q_tmem_alias_f32_varlen_noring_{52f48bcff4,0d7e43d838}.cu`. Also remove their table entries, `_EXACTPRE_NORING_SMEM_BYTES` and `_VARIANT_SMEM_BYTES[("exactpre", "noring")]` (8 files, about −12,700). Update the pins above. Add a CPU test that enumerates `two_kernel_family` × `_exact_scan_variant` and asserts that every produced name is in `_PROGRAMS`. No kernel changes. Confirm with the GPU suite and a `CakeSSDCombined.last_program_name` sweep over the calibration cells (loader 1323-1347) on B200 and GB300.
- [ ] Point `_EXACTPRE_HOST_TEMPLATE` at the fused template and delete `generated/host/mamba_ssd_combined_precomputed_sequence.cpp` (1 file, −977). Drop the guard-absent assert at 4282. Confirm by comparing outputs and final states bitwise for one batched `exactpre` shape (16 × 256, nheads 128) and one varlen `exactpre` shape.
- [ ] Fold `stp_paired_rows_mb4` into `stp_paired_rows` (2 files, about −970). Turn c7e08's hard `#define LAUNCH_MIN_BLOCKS 3` into a downstream define, which needs a 3-line edit or a regeneration. Move the two mb4 instantiations (`1b867acabd879d71`, `29f069839e5f8528`) onto it with `LAUNCH_MIN_BLOCKS=4`, and have `_paired_rows_program` return the define. This also drops the 2 unreachable sm_103a AOT modules. Confirm with `cuobjdump -sass` of the 8ab15 cubin vs c7e08 built with `-DLAUNCH_MIN_BLOCKS=4` on sm_100a; this diff has not been run.
- [ ] Remove dead host code and artifacts (−454): the non-paired `_plan_stp_batch` branch and its `paired` parameter, the 9 `closure_sha256` fields, and `tests/mamba/cake_ssd_accuracy_probe.py` (move it to `benchmarks/` or delete it). Also remove `_PENDING_EXPORT`/`_require_exported` together with `test_source_unexported_program_refuses_to_build` and the "pending" asserts. Confidence on this guard is medium because it serves the out-of-tree export; confirm with the Cake export owners before dropping it.
- [ ] Retire the env-only `chunkpar3_*_varlen` programs (3 files, −5,883). Drop their `_CHUNKPAR3_MODULES` entries and make `three_phase` resolve to the look-back for varlen (or restrict it to batched). Move the forced-mode oracle (`_forced_runs`, the helper at 1470-1474, the chunkpar3 host-template test) to the fp64 reference and `chunkpar3_bf16_batched`. Auto-mode selection does not change.
- [ ] Drop the batched noring window of the retained `exact` family (3 files, −4,182, SHA pins at 6371/6375/6379): return `""` from `_exact_scan_variant` when `two_kernel_family` picks `exact` in batched mode. Bitwise identity between ring and noring is only the loader's claim. Confirm it first with `torch.equal` on `exact_bf16_batched` vs `exact_bf16_batched_noring` at batch 2 × 50 tokens, nheads 576.
- [ ] Regenerate the SSD export with one source per shape and a `STATE_T` define (34 → 12 main sources, −48,585). Keep the exactfused f32 prefetch bound keyed on `sizeof(STATE_T)`. This needs the Cake-side generator, which is not in this repo. Confirm with a per-instantiation SASS diff on sm_100a and sm_103a and the full GPU suite, including f16/f32 state. If no engine needs f16 state, skip that instantiation.
- [ ] Fold the 3 remaining ring/`_noring` shapes (exact varlen, exactfused batched, exactfused varlen) behind an `EPILOGUE_RING` define (−4,798). Confirm with SASS diffs against the current ring and noring cubins, and with bitwise parity on the calibration cells.
- [ ] Render the 4 remaining SSD host templates from one placeholder template driven by `_PREPROCESS_ARGS`/`_MAIN_ARGS*`, replacing the private `check_*` helpers with `tvm_ffi_utils.h` (−2,948). Run a bitwise smoke test of one program per family.
- [ ] Fold the shipped BF16 STP `ratio8`, `ratio8_saturated` and `ratio16` into `stp_bf16_direct.cu` via `-DHEADS_PER_GROUP_STATIC`/`-DHEAD_TILES_STATIC`/`-DDIRECT_UNROLL`. Render the 5 host shims from one `tvm_ffi_utils.h`-based template (−3,180). Keep the shipped source text, since #6003 measured the regenerated direct program 3.5-4% slower. Confirm with a SASS diff per shipped cubin and CUPTI timing of the dim-128 STP rows.
- [ ] Perf-gated retirements (−5,784). Retire `exact_*` if `exactpre` is within 0.5% kernel time on one-chunk items. Retire batched `chunkpar3` (with `_MAIN_ARGS_CHUNKPAR3`, `_THREE_PHASE_*`, `three_phase_preferred` and `grid_barrier3`) if the look-back closes the ≤ 256-tile gap. Gate on CUPTI kernel time on B200 and GB300 over the calibration cells via `benchmarks/bench_cake_mamba_ssd_combined.py`; these gates have not been run.
- [ ] Check the 26 SSU `-D` instantiations one by one. Enumerate `plan_route` over the public shape grid on CPU, compare the emitted define tuples with the `MODULES[*].instantiations` digests, and drop any instantiation that is never reached from AOT.
- [ ] Hot-path trims, tests and docs (−500). Have the kernels read bf16 `dt`/`dt_bias` directly; checking which engines pass bf16 `dt` will size this win. Cache TMA descriptors per prepared shape, move the 120-line calibration log into docs, and prune the pure table-structure tests once the tables shrink.

**Expected size:** about 130K Cake lines → about 115K after the four mechanical steps → about 105K after retiring the env-only/corner programs → about 45K after regeneration (dtype, ring, host template, STP) → about 39K if the perf gates pass and the trims land (about −91K total).

title: fix(precompiled-cache-rubin): Include missing MoE and FP8 dependencies in the SM107 precompiled cache
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

The SM107 precompiled-cache provider omits fused_moe_100, fp8_gemm_cutlass, and trtllm_utils, although their existing generators support SM107. Consequently, FlashInfer compiles these modules at runtime even when flashinfer-jit-cache-sm107a is installed.

  This affected vLLM’s DeepSeek FP8 GSM8K evaluation on Rubin: compiling fused_moe_100 took approximately 789 seconds, and subsequent initialization exceeded the test’s unchanged 1,200-second startup deadline.

  This change adds the missing AOT registrations. It does not change kernel implementations, runtime dispatch, or compiler-target generation.

  Why each condition changes

  • fused_moe_100: use has_sm100 or has_sm107 or has_sm110.
    The existing generator supports SM107 by emitting compatible SM100f code. Moving its registration into one shared condition adds SM107, preserves SM100 and SM110 support, and avoids duplicate registration when multiple targets are enabled. SM103 retains its separate fused MoE module.

  • Keep the original if has_sm100: block restricted to SM100.
    Simply adding or has_sm107 to that block would also register gen_fp4_quantization_sm100_module(), which explicitly builds SM100a code. SM107 already has its own quantization generator and registration. Broadening the block would additionally enable the FP4 GEMM module, which supports SM107 targeting but is
    outside this FP8 failure’s requirements and validation.

  • fp8_gemm_cutlass: use has_sm100 or has_sm103 or has_sm107.
    Moving this registration out of the larger SM100/SM103 block adds the missing FP8 dependency without enabling every other module in that block. Existing SM100/SM103 coverage is preserved, and the generator already maps SM107 to SM100f.

  • trtllm_utils: add has_sm107 to its existing condition.
    This module is another dependency required by the same evaluation. Its omission otherwise causes an additional runtime compilation.

## Validation

- 44 AOT registration tests passed, covering SM107, existing architectures, mixed targets, disabled build categories, and duplicate prevention.

- Confirmed modules load with JIT disabled and are loaded from the provider by the actual evaluation engine.

- The original vLLM case passed on Rubin:

tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py::test_gsm8k_correctness[DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8]
Accuracy was 78.47% across 1,319 questions. Engine initialization took 433.32 seconds, with the original accuracy tolerance and startup deadline unchanged.


## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

title: deslop(cake_dsv4): share arch-identical SM100/SM103 kernels, fold NVFP4 launchers, drop dead host paths
body:
> Developed by the **CAKE team**, the kernels in this PR **outperform** the relevant **SOTA baselines at the time of merge** on the **vast majority of performance benchmark shapes**, matching them otherwise.

## Summary

This PR cleans up the SM100/SM103 part of `csrc/cake_dsv4`, which backs `flashinfer.mla.trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(backend="cake")`.

- BF16/FP8 KV caches go through `run_cake_dsv4`. There are 27 variants per architecture, each a generated kernel and binding pair under `sm_100a/` and `sm_103a/`.
- `kv_cache_format="nvfp4"` goes through the NVFP4 decode templates in `common/`.
- The registry is `flashinfer/jit/cake_dsv4.py` (`_ARCH_REGISTRATIONS`). The host code is `flashinfer/mla/cake_dsv4.py`.

The PR has four commits:

1. Delete a host shim header that nothing includes, and bring the SM100/SM103 README up to date.
2. Delete the dead host descriptor pool and the retired host paths.
3. Move the 13 BF16/FP8 kernel pairs that are identical on both architectures into `common/`, so each is stored once instead of twice.
4. Give each NVFP4 decode template one launcher that takes its knobs as launch arguments. Decode modules per architecture drop from 16 to 7.

A SASS gate covering the 26 kernels moved in commit 3 and the 26 NVFP4 kernels rebuilt in commit 4 found every one identical to its base build. Commits 1 and 2 change no device or binding source. The NVFP4 planner is unchanged. The reserved [0, 1024) workspace region and the exported layout are unchanged. The SM120 part of the family (`sm_120a/`) is not touched.

Base: upstream main `7ea1ea5cd6`. Head: 3525f05fb8 (4 commits).

`git diff --stat`: 74 files, +785 / -24,854.
- `csrc/`: 69 files, +406 / -23,713. This is 30 renames into `common/`, 36 deletions, 2 added headers and the README.
- `flashinfer/jit/cake_dsv4.py`: 1,591 → 1,256 lines (+164 / -499).
- `flashinfer/mla/cake_dsv4.py`: 3,192 → 2,956 lines (+73 / -309).
- Tests: 3 files, +142 / -333.
- `csrc/cake_dsv4/README.md`: +22 / -25.

## Changes

### 1. Drop unused host shim header, refresh SM100/SM103 README (`f265f5a4c`, 2 files, +22 / -229)

- `csrc/cake_dsv4/cake_dsv4_host_shim.h` (204 lines) has had no includer since #6045, when the bindings were regenerated to get their checks from `tvm_ffi_utils.h`. Every BF16/FP8 binding now includes `<arch>/cake_dsv4_host_common.cuh`, and every NVFP4 binding includes `common/cake_dsv4_nvfp4_host_common.cuh`. The README was the last place that mentioned the header.
- The README's SM100/SM103 section now says:
  - `common/` holds the NVFP4 decode family. The shared BF16/FP8 reducers moved into the per-architecture directories in #6220.
  - Each per-architecture directory carries its own `*_common.cuh` headers.
  - No registration carries `tma_workspace_bytes`, so the SM103 descriptor-storage bullet is removed.

  The SM120 section is unchanged.

### 2. Remove the dead descriptor pool and retired host paths (`62189c582`, 5 files, +61 / -545)

- The SM103 bindings pass their TMA descriptors by value. As a result, no registered variant uses `tma_workspace_bytes`, a `workspace` argument kind, a `completion_base` parameter or a combined `sparse_indices` table.
- Deleted:
  - the host descriptor pool and its lock
  - the `workspace` argument kind and the `descriptor_slab` plumbing in the binder
  - the tables of retired and unavailable variant names
  - `SparseMetadata.legacy_combined_table`
  - the unused `_SLAB` plan fragment
- The small-head persistent fallback in `_nvfp4_plan` was never selected and now raises a `RuntimeError`. A CPU sweep of the planner on the unchanged base tree reaches that branch 0 times, over sm_count 1-264 × tiles 1-12 × T 1-4096.
- The reserved [0, 1024) workspace region and the exported layout are unchanged.
- Test changes:
  - Removed `test_descriptor_storage_pool_is_bounded_and_capture_safe`, which only exercised the pool.
  - Removed the two hardening tests parametrized over `_SLAB_ROUTES`: `test_descriptor_storage_reassignment_matches_reference` and `test_captured_descriptor_set_survives_eager_churn`. No slab variant is registered, so both always skipped.
  - Renamed `test_launch_variant_reports_unknown_retired_and_unavailable_names` to `test_launch_variant_reports_unknown_and_unavailable_names`.
  - Removed the `descriptor_slab=None` kwargs.
  - Kept every binder assertion that still applies.

### 3. Share 13 arch-identical SM100/SM103 kernel pairs in `common/` (`8680fe890`, 58 files, +239 / -21,632)

- 13 of the 27 BF16/FP8 variants compile the same kernel source on sm_100a and sm_103a:
  - The two generated kernel files differ only in the 20-hex hash in the `kernel_cake_dsv4_<hash>` symbol.
  - The two bindings differ only in that hash and in the `cake_host_shim_<hash>` namespace.
- For each of these 13 pairs:
  - The sm_100a kernel and binding move to `csrc/cake_dsv4/common/` unchanged (git renames).
  - The sm_103a copies are deleted.
  - Both architecture records in `_ARCH_REGISTRATIONS` point to the shared files.
- Module names and identities are unchanged, so the JIT cache still keeps one module per architecture.
- `common/` gets its own copies of `cake_dsv4_device_common.cuh` and `cake_dsv4_host_common.cuh`. The units include these headers with quotes, and `common/` is not on the include path. The per-architecture headers stay for the 14 kernel pairs that do differ between architectures (32-780 lines).
- New CPU test `test_registered_sources_exist_and_shared_sources_live_in_common` checks that every registered source exists and that any source compiled for both architectures lives in `common/`.

### 4. Fold the NVFP4 knob launchers into one per member (`3525f05fb`, 17 files, +465 / -2,450)

- **Before:** each NVFP4 decode template (member: `swap`, `tile`, `tile_h64`, `pv`) shipped one launcher binding and one JIT module per (tile_n, o_chunks) instantiation. That gave:
  - 13 launchers that differed only in the kernel pointer, the dynamic shared memory literal and the `tmap_q` encoder;
  - 11 registry records, each compiling the member's kernel unit behind selector defines.
- **After:** each member has one launcher. It takes the knobs as launch arguments and switches over an instance table. Each table entry holds the kernel symbol (with its own shared-memory opt-in), the shared-memory size in bytes and the `tmap_q` encoder. The member's module compiles the kernel unit once, with every explicit instantiation.
- The planner is unchanged. `NVFP4Plan` keeps `tile_n` and `o_chunks`, and the host passes them to the launcher. Only the registered variant name moves up to the member level.
- The NVFP4 registry records differed only in identity. They are now one table, derived per architecture.
- Decode modules per architecture: 16 → 7.
- Tests:
  - The NVFP4 route tests pin every plan-table row to its (member, tile_n, o_chunks) cell.
  - New CPU test `test_nvfp4_plan_selects_an_instantiated_cell` sweeps the planner and checks that each selected cell is instantiated.

## Validation

The same checks were run on B200 (SM100) and GB300 (SM103).

- **SASS gate: 52 entries, all identical with the toolchains on both GPUs.**
  - Commit 3, 26 (pair, architecture) kernels: each shared `common/` kernel was compiled for sm_100a and for sm_103a and compared against the base's per-architecture file. All are identical once the symbol hash is mapped.
  - Commit 4, 26 (instantiation, architecture) NVFP4 kernels: each symbol's SASS in the old selector build equals the same symbol's SASS in the new build with all instantiations (per-function cuobjdump comparison).
  - Commits 1 and 2 change no device or binding source.
- **Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on the changed Python files.
- **Leftover references:** a repo-wide search for the deleted header, the deleted sm_103a hashes and the removed host names finds nothing.
- **Registry:** imports and lists the same variants per architecture as before, except NVFP4, which now has 7 per architecture.
- **Planner sweep:** the removed `_nvfp4_plan` fallback is hit 0 times (details in commit 2).
- **Full pytest:** the run covered these files on the candidate and on the unchanged base tree, on the same node, with CUDA 13.4 (required by the NVFP4 modules):
  - `tests/mla/test_cake_dsv4.py`
  - `tests/mla/test_cake_dsv4_nvfp4_route.py`
  - `tests/mla/test_cake_dsv4_out_placement.py`
  - `tests/mla/test_cake_dsv4_hardening.py`
  - `tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_blackwell_dsv4_nvfp4.py`

  GB300: candidate 710 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (427 s); base tree on the same node 725 passed, 4 skipped (the 4 skips are the two removed `_SLAB_ROUTES` hardening tests, which never had a registered slab variant); the candidate collects 19 fewer items because the pool test and those two tests are gone and the NVFP4 route tests are parametrized over the collapsed member table. B200: candidate 710 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (289 s); base tree 725 passed, 4 skipped (same breakdown).

## Not in this PR

These steps of the issue stay open:

- **Exporter side:**
  - Arch-independent kernel symbols for the 14 per-architecture kernel pairs, so their bindings could be shared too.
  - Templating the same-architecture clone pairs (`row_first`/`vsplit`, `split_reduce`/`split5_reduce`, `m64`/`m64_multi_tile`, `v43`/`v44`).
  - Templating the cluster sizes of the experimental `cake_nvfp4_sparse_mla_decode`.
- **Binding regeneration:**
  - Folding the 174 inlined TMA encoders and the per-argument checks into the per-architecture host header.
  - A descriptor-encode cache keyed by geometry.
- **Decisions that need timing on both GPUs:**
  - `nvfp4_decode_cluster` vs `t64`.
  - The FP8 exact-shape routes vs their fallbacks.
  - Whether the registry-structure tests stay.

Part of #6644

title: fix(moe, trace): validate the pack contract in SM12xNvfp4Runner and register the new comm trace modules
body:
## Summary

Since #5863 and #6544 merged to `main`, the `JIT Unittest (H100)` job in the `PR Test` workflow fails on two CPU-only test nodes. `main`'s own run of that workflow (run 38930349451 at 19faf79b70) fails on the same two nodes:

- `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_pack_contract.py::test_every_pack_inputs_checks_the_contract[SM12xNvfp4Runner]`: assertion `'self._validate_pack_contract(act)' in ''`
- `tests/trace/test_template_registry.py::test_registration_module_inventory_is_complete`: the scan of the source finds three modules that are not in the inventory

This PR fixes both failures.

## Root cause

- `SM12xNvfp4Runner.pack_inputs` was added in #5863 (397b9607c). It is the only one of the 16 runners in `flashinfer/fused_moe/runners.py` that never calls the shared `MoERunner._validate_pack_contract`. The test requires `pack_inputs` to make that call first, either directly or through a `self._validate_*` helper.
- #6544 (840fb6965) added `flashinfer.comm.mnnvl_cutedsl_ag`, `flashinfer.comm.mnnvl_cutedsl_moe_finalize` and `flashinfer.comm.tp_moe_finalize_rmsnorm` with `@flashinfer_api(trace=...)` decorators. It did not add them to `_TRACE_REGISTRATION_MODULES` in `tests/trace/template_registry.py`. That file's docstring requires the inventory to match the set of modules that use the decorator.

## Changes

2 files, +4/-4.

- `flashinfer/fused_moe/runners.py`: `SM12xNvfp4Runner.pack_inputs` now calls `self._validate_pack_contract(act)` right after `self._require_built()`, as its parent `SM12xNvfp4Bf16Runner.pack_inputs` does. I removed the separate `NotImplementedError("... supports only PackedPrecomputed routing.")` branch. The shared check already rejects any `routing_input_mode` outside `supported_routing_modes`, which is `(RoutingInputMode.PackedPrecomputed,)` for this runner.
  - A pack that is not PackedPrecomputed still raises `NotImplementedError`, now with the standard message. No test checks the removed message.
  - A pack that carries `per_token_scale` is now rejected by the shared check (`ValueError`) before it reaches the runner's own `ValueError`.
  - The `hidden_states_scale` check and the rest of the method are unchanged. Kernels and numerics are unchanged.
- `tests/trace/template_registry.py`: adds the three modules to `_TRACE_REGISTRATION_MODULES`, in alphabetical order within the `flashinfer.comm.*` block.

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass (ruff v0.12.8 check and format, mypy, whitespace/EOF hooks).
- [x] CPU-only run (no GPU; torch 2.10.0a0 from the NGC 26.01 container) of the affected test files on both the base tree (`main` at ed3e64de) and the fixed tree, to check that the newly registered templates add no new failures:
  - `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_pack_contract.py` (fixed tree): 160 passed, 5 skipped; the `SM12xNvfp4Runner` node passes.
  - `tests/trace/test_template_registry.py`: base 1 failed (`test_registration_module_inventory_is_complete`), 3 passed; fixed tree 4 passed.
  - `tests/trace/test_template_init.py` + `tests/trace/test_fi_trace_template_consistency.py`: base 1453 passed, 246 skipped; fixed tree 1465 passed, 246 skipped. The 12 extra nodes are the newly registered `flashinfer.comm.*` templates; 0 new failures.
- [ ] CI (`@flashinfer-bot run`)

## References

- #5863: Canonical-layout NVFP4 W4A4 MoE in CuTe DSL on SM12x
- #6544: Support Muse-Spark-Open with fused normalization and TP/EP MoE optimizations
- Failing `main` run: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/38930349451 (commit 19faf79b70)

title: fix(aot): ship the remaining SM100-family modules in the SM110 provider
body:
## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #5695. The per-SM jit-cache providers (#5096) build each wheel for exactly one arch, so in the sm110a provider `has_sm100` is False and every module gated on SM100 alone is dropped. #5695 fixed this for `fused_moe_100`. Seven more SM100-named modules have the same problem: their generators build for 11.0a, and SM110 loads them at runtime. So today an SM110 install compiles each of them cold on first use, or fails outright under `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1`.

This PR registers them for SM110 using the same pattern #5544 used for SM103. It widens the shared `has_sm100 or has_sm103` gates to include `has_sm110`, and adds `fp4_gemm_cutlass` next to `fused_moe_100` in the SM110 block, registered once when SM100 is not also targeted.

| module | SM110 runtime route on `main` | generator under `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=11.0a` |
|---|---|---|
| `fmha_cutlass_sm100a` | `prefill.py:224` `if is_sm100a_supported(device) or is_sm110a_supported(device)` | `compute_110a` |
| `mla` | MLA cutlass backend accepts `major in (10, 11)` (`mla/_batch_mla/_backends/cutlass_backend.py:195`) | `compute_110a` |
| `fp4_gemm_cutlass` | `get_cutlass_fp4_gemm_module`: `if sm_major in [10, 11]` → `get_gemm_sm100_module_cutlass_fp4()` unless minor is 3 (`gemm/gemm_base.py:2885`); `_cutlass_gemm_fp4_requirement` lists 110 | `compute_110a` |
| `fp8_gemm_cutlass` | `bmm_fp8(backend="cutlass")`: `_match_sm_version(..., ["100", "103", "107", "110"])` (`gemm/gemm_base.py:9315`) | `compute_110a` |
| `mxfp8_gemm_cutlass` | `_cutlass_gemm_mxfp8_requirement`: `[100, 103, 107, 110, 120, 121]` | `compute_110a` |
| `mxfp8_quantization_sm100` | `mxfp8_quantize` has no arch restriction | `compute_110a` |
| `dcp_alltoall` | no arch restriction (kernel supports SM90+) | `compute_110a` |

For `dcp_alltoall`, the existing comment says the SM10x gate is only there to guarantee CUDA >= 12.8 (to avoid a ptxas 12.6 `cp.async.bulk` bug). SM110 implies CUDA >= 13.0, so it satisfies that too. I updated the comment to say so.

### What stays gated

I didn't hand-pick the list. I enumerated every `gen_*()` call under an `if` that tests `has_sm100` or `has_sm103` by walking `aot.py`'s AST, called each generator under `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=11.0a`, and classified it by what `get_nvcc_flags_list` actually does. An empty major-version filter raises `RuntimeError("No supported CUDA architectures …")`, so the classification needs no compiler and no GPU. The modules that share these gates but cannot run on SM110 stay where they are:

- **raise for 11.0a** (major 11 not supported): `gemm_sm100`, `gemm_sm100_cutlass_nvfp4_svdquant`, `trtllm_gen_gemm`, `trtllm_low_latency_gemm`, `trtllm_gen_fused_moe_sm100`, `trtllm_gen_routing`, `blackwell_softmax`, `trtllm_mnnvl_comm`.
- **pinned to another arch:** `fp4_quantization_100`, and `tgv_gemm_*` (`sm_100a` / `sm_100f`). SM110 already has `fp4_quantization_110`.
- **prebuilt SM10x cubins:** `trtllm_gen_fmha`. I split it out of the `fmha_cutlass_sm100a` block so that widening the CUTLASS FMHA gate doesn't register it.

On current main, #6279 makes `moe_utils` architecture-portable, so it is no longer classified as SM10x-only in these tests.

The runtime agrees with this split. For example, `_cutlass_gemm_mxfp8_requirement` includes 110, while the trtllm and cute-dsl MXFP8 requirements next to it are `[100, 103, 107]`.

### Spec counts (default config, `gen_all_modules`)

*Measured on the original base `8803e2fc` (2026-10-09). Not re-measured after rebasing onto `af71dd7c`.*

```
11.0a: 165 -> 172   (+7: dcp_alltoall, fmha_cutlass_sm100a, fp4_gemm_cutlass,
                         fp8_gemm_cutlass, mla, mxfp8_gemm_cutlass,
                         mxfp8_quantization_sm100; 0 removed)
10.0a: 981 -> 981
10.3a: 976 -> 976
```

The SM100 and SM103 providers are unchanged.

### Runtime evidence

*The measurements below were taken on 2026-10-09 against `main` @ `882c177c`. They were not re-run on the rebased branch.*

I measured this on a Jetson AGX Thor (SM110, CUDA 13.0) against `main` @ `882c177c` (before #5544/#5695), with the sm110a provider emulated from each side's own `gen_all_modules()` output and a separate, freshly cleared `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` per run:

| path | provider (before → after) | `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1` (before → after) | correctness |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bmm_fp8(..., backend="cutlass")` → `fp8_gemm_cutlass` | missing → present | `MissingJITCacheError` → loads from the provider, no JIT dir created | cos 0.9999999 vs a `torch.bmm` fp32 reference |
| `cutlass_fused_moe()` → `fused_moe_100` | missing → present | `MissingJITCacheError` → loads from the provider, no JIT dir created | cos 0.9999924 vs a dense torch reference |

With JIT allowed, the "before" side cold-compiles `fp8_gemm_cutlass` on the first call (74.8 s). `fused_moe_100` is the one #5695 already landed; I'm including it here only as a second runtime path. Both modules were built for 11.0a and contain only `sm_110a` cubins (13 and 260 respectively, per `cuobjdump`).

### Not included

`mm_bf16_cublaslt` has the same symptom on SM110: its generator accepts majors `[8, 9, 10, 11, 12]`, and `_cublaslt_mm_bf16_requirement` allows 110 (`gemm/gemm_base.py:376`). But it is gated `has_sm100 or has_sm103`, so it is also missing from the SM8x/SM9x/SM12x providers. That is a different question from "which SM100-family modules does SM110 share", so I left it out. Happy to send it separately if you want it.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Refs #5649 (closed by #5695, which covered `fused_moe_100` only). Follows the SM103 pattern from #5544.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

I ran `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files rather than `--all-files`. Every applicable hook passed: mypy, ruff check, ruff format, and the whitespace/EOF/line-ending hooks.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New: `tests/jit/test_aot_sm110_modules.py`, modelled on `test_aot_sm103_modules.py`:

- **registration, with generators stubbed:** SM110-only, SM100-only, combined, and no-SM10x/SM110 builds register exactly the expected modules. `fused_moe_100` and `fp4_gemm_cutlass` are generated once when both SM100 and SM110 are targeted.
- **real generators under 11.0a:** the seven shared generators plus `fused_moe_100` emit `-gencode=arch=compute_110a,code=sm_110a`, and the SM10x-only counter-examples raise. Each module's `current_compilation_context` is replaced for the test, so the result does not depend on the GPU the test runs on.

`tests/jit/test_attention_utils.py` gains `has_sm110=False` for the new `gen_attention` parameter, as #5544 did for `has_sm103`.

Results on the Thor (2026-10-09, before the rebase; the test file has since lost two exclusions, so counts differ):

```
pytest tests/jit/test_aot_sm110_modules.py                       20 passed
  same, process started with FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a      20 passed
  same, with aot.py reverted to main                             2 failed, 18 passed
pytest tests/jit/                                                464 passed, 1 skipped
```

With `aot.py` reverted, the two failures are the SM110-only registration test and the "`fp4_gemm_cutlass` generated once" test, as expected.

**Rebased onto `af71dd7c` (2026-10-19, host-side, macOS / Python 3.12, no CUDA GPU):**

- `tests/jit/test_aot_sm110_modules.py` and `tests/jit/test_attention_utils.py`: 38 passed.
- Full `tests/jit/`: 575 passed, 9 failed, 4 errors, 1 skipped. An unmodified-main control in the same environment gave 556 passed with the same 9 failing and 4 erroring test nodes. These are CUDA-toolchain and release/sccache checks, which this environment cannot run.

This is spec-generation and host-side checking only. It is not a CUDA build or a GPU runtime test.

title: Show who maintains a recipe, per hardware, and record verified-run details
body:
## Summary

Who stands behind a recipe and whether it was tested are two different facts, so this PR models them as two fields:

- **`meta.maintained_by`**: the organization that maintains the recipe and keeps it current. It can be set per hardware, for example Inferact for the recipe and AMD for its AMD configurations.
- **Details of a `verified` run**: when the test ran, on which vLLM release or image, and a note.

```yaml
meta:
  maintained_by: inferact                 # or by hardware: { default: inferact, amd: amd }
  hardware:
    h200: verified                        # still valid
    gb200:
      status: verified
      date: 2026-10-15
      image: "vllm/vllm-omni:flux-3-image-klein"   # or vllm: "<release>"
      note: "1x GB200 (arm64, CUDA 13.0): T2I 1024x1024 in ~2.1s, …"   # optional
```

### What readers see
- **Page header:** "Maintained by [logo] Inferact". With per-hardware maintainers it reads "Maintained by [logo] Inferact · AMD hardware: [logo] AMD".
- **Hardware row:** when the selected hardware has its own maintainer, it shows "MI355X configuration maintained by [logo] AMD".
- **Command block:** the badge reads "● Verified on NVIDIA GB200 NVL4 · 2026-10-15". The badge and hardware-pill tooltips add the environment and the note.

### Changes
- **Vocabulary:** `taxonomy.yaml` gains `maintainers`, each with a name, URL and logo. Adding one is a reviewed pull request. It starts with Inferact, AMD, NVIDIA, Intel, Red Hat and Huawei.
- **Logos:** they are served from `public/providers/`. `fetch-provider-logos.mjs` fetches a maintainer's `hf_org` avatar when no model provider or hardware vendor already fetches that file; today that is only Inferact.
- **Schema:**
  - `maintained_by` is an id, or a map in the variant-`tp` keyspace: exact GPU id > generation > brand > `default`.
  - A `verified` entry may be `{ status: verified, date?, vllm?, image?, note? }`. Details are allowed only on `verified`, and misspelled keys are rejected.
  - The build also checks `maintained_by` hardware keys.
- **Loading:** `src/lib/verification.js` splits the verified object at load time.
  - `meta.hardware` keeps the status string, so none of the 10+ readers that compare `=== "verified"` change.
  - The details go to `meta.verification`.
  - `src/lib/maintainers.js` resolves the maintainer for each piece of hardware with the shared `hardwareKeyedValue`, which is now exported.
- **Overlays:** `meta.maintained_by.<in-scope key>` is added to `OVERLAY_RULES`, so a future vllm-ascend overlay can declare Huawei as the maintainer of the Ascend configurations. A core shorthand id becomes `{ default: id }` before merging.
- **JSON API:** publishes `meta.maintained_by` in its map form, and `meta.verification`.
- **Docs:** SCHEMA.md and CLAUDE.md.
- **Example:** `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein` sets `maintained_by: inferact`. Its GB200 entry records the run from the guide's "Verified setup" section: 2026-10-15, the day-0 image, the measured numbers, and #1125 by Isotr0py (Inferact).

### Not in this PR
- **Signer check:** a `signers` list per maintainer, with a PR check that a maintainer's entries come from its people. Until then, review covers it.
- **Stale runs:** marking verified runs as stale once the command they ran has changed.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm test:schema` (6/6). New cases:
  - verified-run details are accepted, and so is the bare string;
  - details on a non-verified status and unknown keys such as `by` are rejected;
  - `maintained_by` accepts an id or a per-hardware map, and rejects an unknown maintainer or hardware key.
- [x] `pnpm test:overlay` (8/8). New case: an overlay adds its in-scope maintainer next to a core shorthand, and can't set out-of-scope hardware or `default`.
- [x] `node scripts/build-recipes-api.mjs`: compared with a build of main, only `flux-3-image-klein.json`, `recipe.schema.json` and `taxonomy.json` differ.
- [x] Local render:
  - flux on GB200: the header shows "Maintained by Inferact", and the badge shows "· 2026-10-15".
  - A local-only per-hardware demo, not committed, set `{ default: inferact, amd: amd }` on another recipe. The header listed both maintainers, and MI355X showed its maintainer note.

title: [Model][DSv4.1] Add shared host Engram lookup for SP token owners
body:
## Purpose

Add an opt-in CPU storage mode for DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram that lets each
sequence-parallel rank read all hash heads for its own tokens. Today each rank
reads its head shard for all tokens, then all-gathers embeddings and selects its
local token slice. Sharing the full host table makes that exchange unnecessary.

### Summary

```text
ASIS
TP-owned head shards -> lookup all tokens/local heads
  -> TP all-gather -> select local tokens -> WKV and gate
```

```text
PR
one host table mapped by TP ranks -> lookup local tokens/all heads
  -> final BF16 rows -> WKV and gate
```

Enable with `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"sp_shared_memory":true}'`.
The flag defaults off. The initial path requires same-host TP>1, DP1/PP1,
MRV2, active SP, and single-threaded checkpoint loading. The tested DP1 setup
uses EP and DeepGEMM mega-MoE on GB200.
CP, microbatching/DBO, speculative decoding, sleep mode and DP storage modes are
rejected. Checkpoint parameters retain their TP shard shapes and each loader
writes a disjoint range of the common table. The existing registered shared-host
allocation and lifetime machinery are reused. Padded SP rows are written as
zeros. WKV and gating are unchanged.

The two full host tables occupy about 188.83 GiB once, rather than once per
process. This does not reduce table memory relative to an ordinary TP-sharded
replica. At an 8192-token ceiling, each rank retains 24 MiB of staging per layer:
`[8192,6,256]` becomes `[2048,24,256]`. Registration and NUMA costs remain relevant;
this is an explicit placement option, not a general serving-speedup claim.

Duplicate check: #56435 retains partitioned table visibility and uses all-to-all;
#56989 keeps embeddings packed through exchange; #56929 fuses reorder and input
quantization; #56926 changes prefetch scheduling. This change removes the Engram
exchange through shared visibility and token ownership. It does not implement
those other paths.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py \
  docs/design/engram_sp_shared_memory.md
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/config/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py
```

## Test Result

- 120 Engram kernel/distributed tests passed on the final rebased code.
- Changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy passed.
- TP2/4 exact row parity, disjoint shard loading, padding/empty rank slices,
  graph replay, mapping failure rollback and registered-storage lifetime covered.
- Both model modes pass ten fixed-answer canaries and context retrieval checks.
- Pinned five-shot GSM8K, 32 questions: fixed repeated evaluation gives control
  31/32 then 32/32; direct 32/32 then 31/32, with no truncated outputs. The same
  break-even question varies. This is bounded accuracy evidence, not bitwise or
  broad model-quality equivalence. An earlier 1024-token direct run capped that
  answer; it is retained in the evidence, not counted as an untruncated pass.

TP4/EP4, DP1, GB200, MRV2, normal graphs, APC off, 4 GiB KV/rank, 64 outputs:

| Input tokens | Batch | Control tok/s | Direct tok/s | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 1 | 103.35 | 104.14 | +0.76% |
| 8192 | 1 | 95.68 | 101.33 | +5.90% |
| 512 | 16 | 1466.10 | 1477.10 | +0.75% |
| 512 | 64 | 2908.84 | 2978.69 | +2.40% |
| 8192 | 16 | 347.11 | 348.49 | +0.40% |
| 8192 | 64 | 423.98 | 431.71 | +1.82% |
| 512 / 2048 / 8192 mixed | 24 | 726.68 | 709.73 | -2.33% |

One warmup and three timed repeats per case. Prompts and scheduler signatures
match within each pair; no preemptions. B1 uses max_num_seqs=4 and the earlier
synthetic prompts; wider batches use max_num_seqs=64 and varied document prompts.
Mixed means eight requests each at 512/2048/8192 tokens. These are single-load
observations, not a general speedup guarantee; the mixed-length regression is
retained. Registration and NUMA costs remain, and existing shutdown warnings
are not addressed by this change.

[Validation scripts, raw results, and provenance](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/32ce421f9a8a11b02b7a95aee86b275696845df7/evidence/engram-sp-direct).

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Register CPU-offloaded Engram tables at their exact size
body:
## Overview

Same fix as #59848, for DSv4.1. Default `cpu_offload` Engram tables use `pin_memory=True`, which rounds each table up to a power of two. Register them at exact size through the existing THP helper, without huge pages. Draft: GB10 only. cc @Juntian777: could you run your #59327 lookup bench on GB200?

## Claims

- TP2 per-rank table: 66 → 47.2 GiB host memory.
- GB10 lookup kernel: ~1.8× faster unsorted, 7–21% faster with #59327's sort.

## Validation

GB10, Engram lookup kernel, TP4 per-rank table, 32K tokens:

| memory | host | unsorted | sorted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin_memory` (before) | 33.1 GiB | 41.4 ms | 10.9 ms |
| exact `cudaHostAlloc` | 24.9 GiB | 41.4 ms | 10.9 ms |
| registered (this PR) | 24.3 GiB | 22.7 ms | 10.2 ms |

Exact size gives the memory saving; the registered memory type gives the speed. These are 4 KiB pages, not THP.

`pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 116 passed. The new small-page case fails on main.

Still needed before un-drafting: GB200 and an E2E `cpu_offload` run.

## Details

- `_allocate_huge_page_storage(n)` → `_allocate_registered_storage(n, huge_pages)`, called once. The THP path and the sort are unchanged. A failed registration falls back to `pin_memory=True`.
- CUDA only; ROCm is unchanged.
- `use_thp` is opt-in and skips the sort, so default users still pay the rounding.

title: [DS V4.1][Engram] Support async prefetch for offloaded engram lookups and engram DP sharding
body:
Re-open of #56357, rebased onto `main`. The original PR was stacked on
the `dsv41-feat` staging branch and was auto-closed when that branch was
removed after DeepSeek V4.1 merged to main. It now targets `main`
directly and also carries the engram DP-shard support commit that was
previously split out as #56230 (also auto-closed for the same reason).

## What's New

Three commits: engram DP sharding (from #56230) plus two engram
embedding I/O improvements for DeepSeek V4.1:

**0. DP sharding for engram tables (previously #56230).** Engram tables
are sharded across a node-local engram DP (EDP) group instead of being
fully replicated per DP rank; per-step all_gathers trade tokens for
heads so each rank can serve its local shard. Set
`--engram-config.enable_engram_dp_sharding false` to retain TP-only tables
(default: true). This is independent of `embedding_across_dp`; explicitly
enabled DP shared memory still uses a node-local group. Qwen4Exp keeps using
its existing ETP group and does not create an extra EDP group. Row-wise
sharding for configurations with too few hash heads remains a TODO.

**1. Asynchronous lookup prefetch (cpu_offload path).** With
`cpu_offload`, engram table rows live in pinned host memory and are read
over UVA. The lookup used to run inline on the main stream when each
engram layer executes; `prepare_embeddings()` now starts it on a
per-layer side stream at forward entry — the n-gram hash ids for all
engram layers are known before the decoder layers run — with a halved
grid to leave SMs for the main stream. `embed()` only waits on the
stream. `@eager_break_during_capture` keeps the side-stream work out of
captured graphs, and persistent per-layer staging buffers keep
addresses stable across replays. DBO and microbatching are not supported
with DeepSeek V4.1 Engram and are rejected during configuration validation.

**2. Shared host tables (`EngramConfig.enable_engram_dp_shared_memory`,
requires `cpu_offload`).** Engram hashes are deterministic and
replica-independent (tokenizer-derived token map, layer-seeded
multipliers), so DP replicas on one node can share one physical copy of
each TP slice instead of pinning private shards and trading tokens for
heads with two per-step all_gathers. edp rank 0 creates a /dev/shm
backing file; every replica maps it `MAP_SHARED` and
`cudaHostRegister`s the pages; lookups read the shared pages over UVA
with no kernel changes. Only edp rank 0 writes weights (single-writer
barrier per parameter; load formats auto/safetensors/pt, including
multithreaded safetensors loading). `DPSharedEngramStorage` owns the shared
allocation, leader-only loading, and cached UVA views. It rejects replaced
parameter storage and unregisters the pages when their owner is released.
The leader broadcasts file-creation errors; ranks exchange mapping/registration
errors before unlinking, report the failing EDP rank and stage, and roll back
allocations on failure. Shared mode skips both
DP all_gathers, slot padding, and the rows-select kernel while keeping
per-rank and per-node host-link read bytes identical to the DP-shard
path; TP sharding/all_gather are unchanged.

Configuration validation requires CPU offload, DP > 1, elastic EP disabled,
and load format auto/safetensors/pt. Runtime validation checks that a node-local
Engram DP group actually formed. Group eligibility reuses the resolved Engram
configuration; the DP shard-size helper only handles node topology. Shared IPC and sufficient /dev/shm capacity
are also required.

Hashing, TP lookup, and gating remain in `common/engram.py`. The current
DP sharding, CUDA host registration, and prefetch implementation lives in
`nvidia/engram.py`; the AMD model continues to use the common resident path.

## Why not a duplicate

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "engram"` —
no open PR covers this; the only related ones (#56435, #56436, #56440)
touch SP all-to-all / lookup overlap / microbatch positions, not DP
sharding, prefetch, or shared host tables. This PR supersedes the
auto-closed #56230 and #56357 (same author). Shared host tables remain opt-in. Qwen4Exp and DeepSeek V4.1 now default
to CPU offload through `--engram-config.cpu_offload`; setting it to `false`
keeps tables on the GPU. The legacy offload environment setting is removed.

## Benchmarks

Real DeepSeek V4.1, 4xGB200, TP4, 512 output tokens, sync lookup vs
prefetch, 2 rounds each (ms):

| input / concurrency | TTFT sync → prefetch | Δ | decode/tok sync → prefetch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 / 1    | 44.66 → 45.11     | ~0     | 7.452 → 7.451 |
| 4096 / 1   | 168.16 → 167.38   | ~0     | 7.461 → 7.463 |
| 4096 / 8   | 680.98 → 677.45   | -0.52% | 13.006 → 12.969 |
| 8192 / 1   | 304.97 → 303.72   | -0.41% | 7.491 → 7.486 |
| 8192 / 8   | 1447.05 → 1440.92 | -0.42% | 10.703 → 10.683 |
| 16384 / 1  | 573.26 → 568.04   | -0.91% | 7.511 → 7.500 |
| 16384 / 8  | 2636.92 → 2613.28 | -0.90% | 11.849 → 11.882 |


Prefetch recovers exactly the lookup-bytes / host-link time on the
critical path, and is neutral in decode where lookups are us-scale — no
regression anywhere.

## Tests

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -v --timeout=180`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k engram -v`
- `.venv/bin/python -O -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k 'engram_dp_shared_memory or engram_rejects_elastic_cross_dp' -v --timeout=60`
- Pre-commit hooks on all changed files

All passed.

The model evals below predate the latest loader, topology, backend, EDP
configuration, and initialization updates. The common resident path was tested
on GB200; ROCm hardware validation has not been run.


Eval (GSM8K, DeepSeek V4.1, two runs each):
| config | accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP1xDP4 + `enable_engram_dp_shared_memory` (zero DP comm) | 0.9318 / 0.9318 |
| TP4xDP1, prefetch (default) | 0.9363 / 0.9363 |

Cross-node (official V4.1-Flash, 2 nodes, TP1xDP8 — DP spans both nodes,
so this also validates the cross-node topology for both modes):

| mode | engram group | table storage | per-step DP comm | GSM8K flex / strict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP shard | per-node Engram EDP=4 | 8 × 23.60 GiB = 188.8 GiB | yes (gather + token/head exchange) | 0.9265 / 0.9272 |
| shm | per-node Engram EDP=4 | 2 × 94.42 GiB = 188.8 GiB (each mmap'd 4×) | none | 0.9257 / 0.9257 |

Both modes work cross-node. The EDP group is a separate process group
created only for the engram tables — the general DP group is untouched
and still spans all 8 ranks across both nodes for everything else. EDP is
built from node-local DP replicas only (`_engram_dp_shard_size` =
gcd(dp_size, ranks_per_node / replica_size)), so this TP1xDP8 run forms
two independent EDP groups of 4, one per node, each sharing one full
table copy; cross-node replicas therefore see zero engram communication,
and table storage scales with node count, not replica count. The two
modes differ only intra-node: DP shard pays two all_gathers per step in
the node's EDP group, while shm eliminates them via the /dev/shm mmap.

---

AI assistance was used (Kimi Code and Codex) for rebasing, Engram changes,
and test validation. The latest Codex edits await human review.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram all-to-all buffers in one allocator
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 with host-offloaded, DP-sharded Engram tables (`cpu_offload: true`, `dp_shared_memory: false`, e.g. with `use_thp: true`) hangs in the first forward (memory profiling) when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set. This receives the Engram all-to-all into a persistent buffer allocated next to its send buffer, so both come from the same allocator.

No open PR covers this (searched open PRs/issues for Engram all-to-all, cumem, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER`). #62091 changes only the GPU-table path (`cpu_offload: false`), which has no all-to-all.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: DSv4.1-Flash DEP2/DEP4 prefill with host DP-sharded Engram + `--enable-cumem-allocator` now starts and serves.
- No numerical change: the same bytes are exchanged, only the receive buffer's allocation changes. Peak memory is unchanged (the per-step `empty_like` of the same size becomes persistent).

## Validation

GB200 (4 GPUs/node), vLLM nightly 49cb2bbf image (CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.32.3), env `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`. The changed code is identical on main.

Serving: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-cumem-allocator --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"use_thp":true}' --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ...` (same hang with DEP2).

| run | result |
|---|---|
| main | hangs in `determine_available_memory`; all ranks in `EngramBatch._stage` `all_to_all_single` (py-spy, also with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`), GPUs spin at 100%, NCCL watchdog fires after 600 s |
| main, no `--enable-cumem-allocator` | starts |
| main, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | starts |
| this PR | starts (profiling + CUDA graph capture); 48/48 completions with 8 to 30K-word prompts at concurrency 16 (both the all-to-all and the peer-exchange slots) |

Standalone reproducer, no model (4 GPUs):

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py [--same-pool]
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
shape = (32768 * dist.get_world_size(), 2, 6, 264)
with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    sent = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    pool_recv = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
recv = pool_recv if "--same-pool" in sys.argv else torch.zeros_like(sent)
dist.all_to_all_single(recv, sent)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"rank {dist.get_rank()} ok")
```

</details>

| send | recv | result |
|---|---|---|
| cumem pool | caching allocator | hangs (killed after 120 s) |
| cumem pool | cumem pool (`--same-pool`) | ok |
| cumem pool | caching allocator, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | ok |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` passes. No test added: reproducing needs 4+ GPUs with NCCL 2.32 and the cumem allocator, which CI does not run for DSv4.1; validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: `EngramBatch.__init__` runs during model init, inside the cumem pool when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set, so `packed_rows` (the all-to-all send buffer) is a cumem allocation. The receive buffer was `torch.empty_like(rows)` in each forward, from the caching allocator. With NCCL local user-buffer registration on (the default), NCCL 2.32 hangs an all-to-all whose buffers mix the two allocators; the reproducer shows this without the model. I did not pin down the NCCL-internal reason (the serving logs show FABRIC IPC registration failures for some buffers, the reproducer hangs without them).

Allocating the receive buffer next to `packed_rows` keeps both in one allocator in either mode, and removes a per-step allocation. `_stage` is an eager break, so the persistent buffer does not affect CUDA graphs.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and write this change; I reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

title: [Model][Engram] Share host tables across co-located DP replicas by default
body:
## Purpose

`EngramConfig.dp_shared_memory` (#56512) keeps one copy of the CPU-offloaded Engram tables per node instead of one per DP replica, with no per-step Engram DP collectives, but it had to be requested by hand and failed startup whenever its requirements were not met. This PR turns it on by default wherever it can work and falls back otherwise:

- `dp_shared_memory` defaults to unset and resolves to enabled when `cpu_offload` is on, `data_parallel_size > 1` and elastic EP is off. An explicit `true` keeps the existing strict validation.
- Before the layers are built, `can_share_engram_tables` falls back to the existing DP head sharding (same host footprint, one table per node) when the node-local Engram DP group has size 1 (replicas not co-located) or `/dev/shm` is smaller than the full tables: 188.8 GiB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, against Docker's default 64 MiB. Both cases log a `warning_once` pointing at `--shm-size` / `--ipc=host`. The check compares against the tmpfs total, which is identical on every rank of a node, so no collective is needed to keep the decision consistent.
- The `load_format` allowlist is dropped: `dummy` (`fill_`) and `sharded_state` (`copy_`) write identical bytes into the shared mapping on every rank, so the restriction guarded nothing.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-19): [#57195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57195) shares host lookups for SP token owners, [#56757](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56757) backs tables with disk files, [#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) keeps tables in host memory on ROCm. None changes the `dp_shared_memory` default or adds a `/dev/shm` fallback.

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py \
  tests/test_config.py -q -k engram
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/test_config.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/config/engram.py \
  vllm/config/vllm.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py
git diff --check
```

## Test result

- 68 passed on 4xGB200, including the four-process shared-memory storage tests, the new default-resolution cases (offloaded DP on; no offload, DP=1 and elastic EP off) and the new `/dev/shm`-too-small fallback test.
- Pre-commit, mypy-3.12 and `git diff --check` passed.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a`), one GB200 node, DEP4 (TP1 x DP4, EP), DSpark 5 tokens with adaptive verification, **no `--engram-config` flag**. GSM8K 5-shot via MQA, completions API, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, n=1319.

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| exact_match/flexible-extract | 0.931 |
| exact_match/strict-match | 0.931 |
| num_request_errors | 0 |

This matches the 0.9303 recorded for the same model on main (2026-09-13). The engine log confirms the default took the shared path on its own: `Resolved Engram configuration: EngramConfig(cpu_offload=True, embedding_across_dp=False, dp_shared_memory=True)`, `Engram node-local DP group size: 4 (TP=1)`, and both tables reported `94.42 GiB shared across DP replicas` with no fallback warning. On the node, `/dev/shm` held 190 GiB and `free` reported 191 GiB shared, one copy of the tables rather than four private pinned copies.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and this draft (Claude Code). Human review of every changed line and independent execution of relevant tests are required before submission.

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Sequence-parallel mHC boundary and fused Engram gather/seam
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)

## What

Two fused paths for DeepSeek-V4.1, plus the MoE finalize plumbing they expose:

1. **mHC sequence-parallel boundary** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MHC_SP_FUSION`, opt-in): inside the sharded region each sublayer boundary becomes one collective launch — reduce-scatter of the partial sublayer output, hc post + next combine + RMSNorm on this rank's rows, all-gather of the normalized next input — with the mixing statistics produced by dedicated CTAs of the same launch (NVLS from three peers up, peer load/store at two ranks). With decoder SWA bounded replay the SP region ends at the tail boundary instead of excluding SP outright.
2. **Engram**: the hash tables shard on hash-column boundaries in symmetric memory, and the lookup defaults to an in-place gather straight into `wkv`'s MXFP8 operand — no all-reduce, no dequant/requant round trip (a bf16-dequantizing gather covers `wkv` configurations without an MXFP8 input path, exactly; the shared host table is read the same way). The gate + residual update + the next boundary's combine/norm fuse into one seam kernel with SP / DP / TP variants (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_TP_FUSION_MIN_TOKENS` gates the TP variant; the image-token mask rides the kernel as a per-row skip). CUDA only; ROCm and other platforms keep the existing paths.
3. **MoE**: a raw `MoEOutput`'s finalize now defers whenever the producer supports it and lands as one fused finalize + shared-add kernel writing the caller's buffer; `get_merged` honors `out=` on the unfused arm too, fixing a path where the sequence-parallel boundary read an unwritten buffer.

## Accuracy

- Kernel level: the direct gathers are bitwise-identical to the dequantizing reference (including e8m0 zero scales and fp8 denormal payloads) on both sm90 and sm100; the DP and SP seam variants are bitwise-identical to each other across row counts, ragged splits and skip masks, including NaN/Inf injection into masked rows; 200 back-to-back SP launches show stable semaphore rotation.
- End to end (TP4/EP4, gsm8k 1319 questions, greedy): fused SP 0.9014 vs unfused 0.9113, McNemar p = 0.198 (not significant). A same-configuration rerun control scores 0.9113 / 0.9113 with only 36% exact-text agreement, i.e. the engine is not run-to-run stable at temperature 0 on this backend (as the cookbook documents), and the fused path's long-prompt logprob drift sits within that noise floor. TP-mode fusion scores 0.9052; TP2 (host table) 0.8954, all within the observed jitter band.
- The seam consumes the previous boundary's lagged `pre`, so the fused math matches the unfused operator order; equivalence rather than bitwise identity is expected against the old path (the gate's sigmoid was already approximate there).

## Notes

- TP2 cannot hold the device tables beside the weights; the host table is the deployable form there (cookbook updated, along with the gather semantics).
- Online weight updates remain rejected while derived hc weight splits are active; the probe follows the renamed stacked tensors.
