Single-node H20-3e report: vision CP + DSpark, long-prefill improvements, and three upstream PRs
Thanks for maintaining this roadmap and for the kernel/CP work behind it. We have been integrating and testing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on
one 8× NVIDIA H20-3e server
, with text, image+text, tool calling, streaming, and cache reporting as requirements.
Our October 5–7 experiments started from
unmodified SGLang v0.5.21
and ended with a production deployment of a pinned integration build. The strongest paired comparisons were:
524,032-token cold TTFT: 323.261 → 25.531 s
, a
92.1% reduction / 12.66× speedup
.
C64 aggregate output: 877.01 → 2,534.61 token/s (+189.0%)
; per-request streaming decode:
15.69 → 49.10 token/s (+213.0%)
.
These are
whole-deployment improvements
, not the isolated effect of any one PR. We have contributed
#39306
,
#42922
, and
#42924
; their narrower validation and attribution are described below.
1. Setup and measurement scope
Hardware: 8× H20-3e, SM90, approximately 140 GiB visible memory per GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch (NV18 topology), 2 TiB host RAM, two NUMA nodes.
Baseline: v0.5.21 at
e00930c5489053f26d86b179cee0d087f846acbb
,
TP8/EP8, DSpark block size 5 already enabled
, no CP, no decoder bounded replay, GPU-resident Engram, no HiCache.
Final:
TP8/EP4, CP8 interleave, CP decode-attention TP, DSpark5, decoder SWA bounded replay
, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE with FP8 precision; Engram host table in
per_rank
layout, NUMA binding, HiCache ratio 1.5 /
write_through
.
Both use a 524,288-token context limit, static memory fraction 0.8, chunk size 8192 and max-running-requests 64. Prefill CUDA graphs remain disabled; decode CUDA graphs are enabled.
Final local integration revision:
79b468a7435e1bd29ad0d377587ff10b3c214ba3
(
not an upstream release/commit
). Runtime: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18; the final DeepGEMM integration uses
sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.2
. This is a backported integration, not a claim that stock v0.5.21 supports this configuration.
The baseline and final integration use the same V4.1 model weights on the same hardware. No P/D disaggregation is used. All performance below is from a single eight-GPU server. These results describe the pinned October 5–7 snapshots, not the latest heads of every roadmap PR.
Comparison boundary:
the near-512K and C64 baseline measurements were supplemented using exactly the final workload construction, warmup and three measured rounds. Input hashes, token counts, output lengths and zero-cache-hit conditions match. Other baseline cells are historical references: cold-prefill nonces differ, and the early natural-generation prompts/warmup procedure differ from the final protocol. The tables explicitly mark the paired supplements with †. Runs were sequential, on different dates, not randomized interleaved A/B trials.
2. Optimization path and what we retained
Use vision-compatible CP as the foundation.
We chose
model: DeepSeek V4.1 vision CP and single-owner image encoding
#40219
for its merge-before-shard multimodal preparation and single-owner image encoding. We adapted the owner callback API and fixed physical request-pool row mapping in the Torch prefill indexer. We borrowed the replay-tail idea from
[DSV4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1 support prefill CP
#40161
later, rather than importing its entire P/D integration.
Integrate the Hopper paths and H20 configurations.
This included
[Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Hopper paths and Blackwell prefill selection
#41251
,
[DSV4.1] Add H20 block-FP8 tuned configs
#41098
and the relevant
[DSV4.1] Enable Hopper decode optimizations for TP8
#39114
path, plus scorer/Top-K, compression, RoPE, dispatch and preparation changes listed below. We checked actual dispatch and added tables for six further missing matrix shapes encountered in this integration; small tuning differences below 3% retained the default. These additional local tables are distinct from the original six tables in
[DSV4.1] Add tuned H20-3e block-FP8 GEMM configs
#39306
.
Enable Engram host storage and HiCache together, then tune EP.
The
per_rank
layout shards the host Engram table across ranks rather than replicating the entire table eight times. title: [Feat] volundr: Add Agens Volundr model support
body:
## Motivation

Agens Volundr (`Blockway/Agens-Volundr-32B-v1`, `Blockway/Agens-Volundr-32B-v1-INT4` (W4A16)) is a hybrid model that
today only runs from a patched SGLang build (`ghcr.io/blockwayz/agens-sglang:v1-sm89` / `v1-sm90`). This PR adds native support so a stock install serves it.

Architecture, as the runtime sees it:

- **KDA** linear-attention layers (per-channel forget gate), served by the existing `KDAAttnBackend`
  through `RadixLinearAttention`, with grouped value attention (48 value heads over 16 key heads).
- **BCSA** layers: a 4,096-token sliding window plus a 4:1 mean-pooled far field chosen by a learned
  128-wide indexer, merged with the window under one softmax through the window's LSE. The indexer key
  depends on the layer input, so each BCSA layer keeps a per-token side cache indexed by
  `out_cache_loc` like K/V. One `attn` layer is plain dense attention.
- **mHC** (manifold hyper-connections): 4 residual streams with Sinkhorn-normalised mixing around
  every layer.
- **Engram**: hashed n-gram memory on two layers; needs the two previous token ids of every token.
- Optional vision tower: SGLang's qwen3_vl vision model and MRoPE, unchanged.

The layer map comes from `config.mixer_types`; the attention layers do not sit on a fixed interval.

## Modifications

New files

- `srt/models/volundr.py` — `VolundrForCausalLM`, `VolundrForConditionalGeneration`. Weights load
  as shipped (HF names; `gate_up_proj` stacking; blockwise column-parallel loaders for the fused
  `[q|k|v]` projection and conv at tp > 1). Every attention/MLP RMSNorm is the zero-centred
  `GemmaRMSNorm`; mHC and the KDA output norm are plain.
- `srt/configs/volundr.py` — `VolundrTextConfig` (layer map from `mixer_types`, KDA state layout via
  `KimiLinearCacheParams`, BCSA/Engram/mHC fields with defaults), `VolundrConfig` (vision + text);
  registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` and the linear-attention model registry (-> `KDAAttnBackend`).
- `kernels/ops/layernorm/volundr_mhc.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/volundr_bcsa.py` — Triton kernels for
  mHC mix/combine and the BCSA decode block-key write / far branch (~6,000 small launches per decode
  step become a few per layer). Each is bit-exact with the torch reference next to it; the rounding
  rules that make it so (libdevice exp, `div_rn`, fixed reduction order, FMA contraction off) are in
  the module docstrings. Registered for the kernel inventory.
- `srt/function_call/agens_detector.py` — `AgensDetector` (Qwen3-Coder XML body inside
  `<|call|>`/`<|/call|>`).
- `arg_groups/model_overrides/volundr.py` — defaults: `page_size=1` (BCSA pools far-field K/V straight
  from the token-indexed cache), `--attention-backend fa3`.

Edits to shared files (all small)

- `configs/hybrid_arch.py`: an explicit linear-attention registration wins over the `Qwen3Next`
  isinstance chain in `hybrid_gdn_config` (Volundr's config reuses the Qwen3.5 text-config plumbing,
  but its linear layers are KDA, not GDN).
- `configs/model_config.py`: `uses_kda_attention` also recognises registry entries whose backend is
  `KDAAttnBackend` (so the KDA prefill-graph rule applies); multimodal arch lists.
- `layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_triton.py`: `extend` broadcasts q/k heads when
  `num_v_heads > num_k_heads` (the decode/verify kernels already handle grouped value attention).
- `multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py`: Volundr uses the Qwen3.5 vision/MRoPE path (`vision_config.model_type`).
- Parsers: `AgensDetector` reasoning detector in `parser/reasoning_parser.py` (`<|think|>…<|/think|>`,
  `<|call|>` closes reasoning implicitly), `agens` in both registries and both name lists.
- `sampling/custom_logit_processor.py`: `AgensThinkingBudgetLogitProcessor` (thinking-token ids
  248068/248069, newline 198), used through the existing `custom_params.thinking_budget`.

Behaviour notes

- Token ids listed in the checkpoint's `generation_config.suppress_tokens` (padding rows of the
  embedding/lm_head past the tokenizer) are masked from next-token logits, as transformers'
  `SuppressTokensLogitsProcessor` does. Input logprobs are untouched.
- No environment variables. No `trust_remote_code` needed (the config class is native; a checkpoint
  `auto_map` is ignored by the registry reload).
- In this PR: tp >= 1 bf16, INT4 (compressed-tensors) at tp 1, fa3 backend (sm90). Prefix caching,
  the FlashInfer backend / sm89 and far/near decode graphs, and speculative decoding follow as
  separate PRs.

## Accuracy Tests

Teacher-forced against the checkpoint's own transformers implementation (one HF forward per passage,
dumped once, every engine compared against the same dump). Passages: license texts and Python
sources, 285 / 4,000 / 6,000 / 12,133 tokens. "Disagree" = top-1 differs; the reference's own
top1–top2 logprob margin at those positions is listed. KL20 = KL(ref || engine) over the reference's
top-20 tokens (approximation; engine logprobs outside its own top-20 floored at its 20th).

| bf16, sm90, fa3 | 285 | 4,000 | 6,000 | 12,133 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, tp1: top-1 | 100.00 % | 99.97 % | 99.93 % | 99.88 % |
| this PR, tp1: mean abs. dlogprob(target) | 0.0016 | 0.0020 | 0.0014 | 0.0021 |
| this PR, tp1: KL20 | 3.3e-4 | 1.5e-4 | 1.1e-4 | 1.7e-4 |
| this PR, tp2: top-1 | 100.00 % | 99.97 % | 99.95 % | 99.90 % |
| previous out-of-tree build, tp1: top-1 | 100.00 % | 99.97 % | 99.93 % | 99.93 % |
| previous out-of-tree build: mean abs. dlogprob | 0.0018 | 0.0023 | 0.0018 | 0.0023 |

All disagreements sit at reference margins of 0.0–0.375 (bf16 ties). The 12,133-token passage has
15 / 12,132 disagreements here vs 9 for the previous build; mean dlogprob and KL20 are lower here.
Decode path vs prefill (greedy-decode 256 tokens on 8 prompts of 300–6,000 tokens, several crossing
the 4,096 window, then teacher-force the same tokens): mean abs. difference 0.0051, 4 / 2,048
top-1 flips (previous build 0.0045, 10 / 2,048). Runs are deterministic (repeat = bit-identical).

Fused kernels: bit-exact against the torch references (`test/registered/kernels/ops/...`).

Serving smoke (bf16 tp1 and INT4 tp1, text and vision checkpoints): `--reasoning-parser agens`
splits reasoning/content (thinking on and off); `--tool-call-parser agens` parses 8/8 sampled
tool calls at T=0.6; `thinking_budget=32` caps reasoning at 32 tokens; an image of three coloured
shapes is described correctly (`--enable-multimodal`).

Long context: one 32,768-token passage, top-1 99.81 % (63 / 32,767 disagreements, all at reference
margins <= 0.375), KL20 2.6e-4; the mean dlogprob grows along the sequence (0.0019 in the first 4K,
0.0055 in the last 4K).

Benchmarks (sm90, bf16 tp1, the v1 model-card protocol):

| | this PR | previous out-of-tree build |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA diamond, 198 items, 6K thinking budget with forced close, T 0.6 / top_p 0.95, 4 runs | 78.3 / 82.3 / 80.8 / 78.8, mean 80.05 | mean 79.3 |
| HumanEval, greedy, 512 tokens | 78.0 | 78.7 |

Tiny-model e2e (`test/registered/e2e/models/test_volundr_tiny.py`, `Blockway/Agens-Volundr-tiny-random`):
teacher-forced top-1 vs HF reference values recorded from the checkpoint's own implementation >= 99 %,
decode-vs-prefill KL ~1e-3.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

sm90 (141 GB), bf16 tp1, fa3, prefix cache off (this PR), idle host:

| | 1K prompt, 1 stream | 8K prompt, 1 stream | 16 x 1K, aggregate incl. prefill | 16 x 1K, steady decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 48.7 tok/s | 44.3 | 572.5 | 668.6 |
| previous out-of-tree build | 47.8 | 44.2 | 570 | — |

`sglang.benchmark.one_batch` (model only, CUDA graphs, 1K input): 20.6 ms per decode step at bs 1,
23.9 ms at bs 16 (670 tok/s). INT4 tp1: 67.9 / 67.2 tok/s single stream.

## Checklist

- [x] pre-commit
- [x] Unit tests: `unit/function_call/test_agens_detector.py`, `unit/parser/test_agens_reasoning_parser.py`,
      `unit/configs/test_volundr_config.py`, `kernels/ops/layernorm/test_volundr_mhc.py`,
      `kernels/ops/attention/test_volundr_bcsa.py`; existing parser-name and registry tests pass
- [x] e2e: `test/registered/e2e/models/test_volundr_tiny.py` on `Blockway/Agens-Volundr-tiny-random`
      (2 KDA + 1 BCSA + 1 dense, Engram, mHC, BCSA window 64 so the far field is exercised; 81 MB),
      `register_cuda_ci(stage="extra-a", runner_config="1-gpu-large")`; reference values in
      `volundr_tiny_reference.json` (recorded from the checkpoint's transformers implementation, since
      that implementation needs transformers 5.8 and is not run in CI)
- [ ] Docs: `docs/docs/supported-models/` entry and a cookbook recipe
- [x] Accuracy and speed above

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The tests and measurements reported here were
run by us on our own hardware, and we will follow up on review feedback.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

What
Two fused paths for DeepSeek-V4.1, plus the MoE finalize plumbing they expose:
mHC sequence-parallel boundary
(
SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MHC_SP_FUSION
, opt-in): inside the sharded region each sublayer boundary becomes one collective launch — reduce-scatter of the partial sublayer output, hc post + next combine + RMSNorm on this rank's rows, all-gather of the normalized next input — with the mixing statistics produced by dedicated CTAs of the same launch (NVLS from three peers up, peer load/store at two ranks). With decoder SWA bounded replay the SP region ends at the tail boundary instead of excluding SP outright.
Engram
: the hash tables shard on hash-column boundaries in symmetric memory, and the lookup defaults to an in-place gather straight into
wkv
's MXFP8 operand — no all-reduce, no dequant/requant round trip (a bf16-dequantizing gather covers
wkv
configurations without an MXFP8 input path, exactly; the shared host table is read the same way). The gate + residual update + the next boundary's combine/norm fuse into one seam kernel with SP / DP / TP variants (

title: [Feat] hicache: Notify storage backends when the initial host-pool registration burst completes
body:
## Motivation

A storage backend learns its host pools from a burst of hooks: the anchor pool through `register_mem_pool_host`, then every pool of the host pool group through `register_mem_host_pool_v2` — but nothing told the backend when the burst was over. A backend that must finalize once the pool set is known (e.g. register the instance with a remote cache manager whose spec cannot be amended after registration) had no correct moment to act and could only defer that work to the first data-path call, paying seconds of setup on the first request and surfacing config errors (manager unreachable, instance conflict) after startup instead of failing it.

## Modifications

- `HiCacheStorage` gains a no-op `on_host_pools_registered()`: fires exactly once per attach, right after the last call of the initial burst; pools registered later (dynamic draft sidecars) arrive through v2 alone and do not re-fire it. Raising fails the attach.
- The burst ends in different places on the two controllers, so each fires the hook at its own end: the base controller right after the anchor pool, `HybridCacheController` — whose per-pool v2 loop runs after `super().attach_storage_backend()` returns — after that loop. A `_registers_host_pools_after_super_attach` flag tells the two apart; no signatures change and no code moves.
- The hook defaults to a no-op, so existing backends are unaffected.
- Documents the registration lifecycle in `hicache_design.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no model output changes). New CPU unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_storage_registration_hook.py`: the hybrid hook fires after its v2 burst exactly once, the base hook fires right after the anchor pool, base-path hook failure rolls the attach back, hybrid-path failure propagates, dynamic sidecars do not re-fire the hook.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: [Roadmap] DeepSeek V4.1 Optimization
body:
Track optimization and feature support for DeepSeek V4.1 in SGLang.

## Refactor

## General optimization

- [ ] Prefill optimizations
  - [ ] mHC SP + engram fusion — #43065
  - [x] Fold `q_rope_store` into `fused_q_norm_rope` — #41657
  - [x] Faster FP4 index-K gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices` — #41658
  - [x] Prefill indexer: raw selection, row-pair schedule IDs, and host synchronization removal — #41659
  - [x] Fused c1/c2 compression for eager extend and faster c2 decode — #41660
  - [x] Trim prefill model-entry overhead — #41704

  - [ ] TP4 low latency attention layer #44933 
- [x] Add opt-in TRT-LLM sparse attention support — #41603 
- [ ] Integrate the MegaMoE update: locality-aware scheduling, epilogue prefetch, and shared-memory optimizations — [DeepGEMM #462](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/462)
- [x] Add MegaMHC support — #42808 
- [ ] Integrate DeepEP V2.5: migrate to dedicated buffer APIs and enable the new communication optimizations — [DeepEP #763](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/763)

## Feature: bounded replay

Goal: both replay flags on by default — same accuracy, never slower than off, faster prefill.

title: Pooling Engram Conditional Memory in Large Language Models using CXL
body: Engram conditional memory has emerged as a promising component for LLMs by decoupling static knowledge lookup from dynamic computation. Since Engram exhibits sparse access patterns and supports prefetching, its massive embedding tables are well-suited for offloading to lower-tier memory. In this paper, we propose using Compute Express Link (CXL) memory pool for Engram storage. Compared to RDMA, CXL provides fine-grained and low-latency access required by minimal and discrete retrieval patterns of Engram. We integrate the CXL-based Engram pool into SGLang, achieving near-DRAM end-to-end performance. This provides a scalable and cost-efficient storage solution for future Engram-integrated LLMs without compromising inference performance.

title: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for Large Language Models
body: While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) scales capacity via conditional computation, Transformers lack a native primitive for knowledge lookup, forcing them to inefficiently simulate retrieval through computation. To address this, we introduce conditional memory as a complementary sparsity axis, instantiated via Engram, a module that modernizes classic N-gram embedding for O(1) lookup. By formulating the Sparsity Allocation problem, we uncover a U-shaped scaling law that optimizes the trade-off between neural computation (MoE) and static memory (Engram). Guided by this law, we scale Engram to 27B parameters, achieving superior performance over a strictly iso-parameter and iso-FLOPs MoE baseline. Most notably, while the memory module is expected to aid knowledge retrieval (e.g., MMLU +3.4; CMMLU +4.0), we observe even larger gains in general reasoning (e.g., BBH +5.0; ARC-Challenge +3.7) and code/math domains~(HumanEval +3.0; MATH +2.4). Mechanistic analyses reveal that Engram relieves the backbone's early layers from static reconstruction, effectively deepening the network for complex reasoning. Furthermore, by delegating local dependencies to lookups, it frees up attention capacity for global context, substantially boosting long-context retrieval (e.g., Multi-Query NIAH: 84.2 to 97.0). Finally, Engram establishes infrastructure-aware efficiency: its deterministic addressing enables runtime prefetching from host memory, incurring negligible overhead. We envision conditional memory as an indispensable modeling primitive for next-generation sparse models.

title: Smarter and Cheaper at Once: Byte-Exact KV-Cache Grafting Turns a Frozen Small Model into a Verified-Knowledge Flywheel
body: We report a way to make a frozen small language model both more capable and dramatically cheaper at once, without changing any weights. Verified knowledge is deposited once as a byte-exact key-value (KV) state artifact and later restored, by graft, into a fresh inference context. The restore is bit-exact: under a pinned deterministic configuration, the grafted logits are byte-for-byte identical to a fresh computation (SHA-256 equality), with zero KL divergence and 100% argmax agreement over fifty samples. We show that own-position graft is the unique numerically exact operating point on a model with floating-point rotary encoding, and we verify byte-exactness on two model scales (12B, 31B) and two GPU targets, one through a pre-registered replay. On AIME 2025, a frozen Gemma-4-12B moves from 80.0% to 93.3% once a verified solution library is grafted, above its own 77.5% and its 31B sibling's 89.2% published anchors. On the recurring case, eight problems the base model never solves within a 401,026-token budget are answered from cached verified solutions in 61 total decode tokens, a factor of 6,574 fewer tokens and about 8,700x less energy; the capability claim proper rests on held-out transfer (7 of 7 at 31B). The same byte-exact store widens usable context from 32,768 to 2,854,766 tokens at zero extra accelerator memory, and moves byte-identical between machines of the same architecture. We describe the system at the behavior level; the engine is proprietary, and every reported number is backed by committed input and output hashes so the scoring can be re-checked without it.
